  • Avidan, S., Shamir, A. Seam Carving for Content-Aware Image Resizing, SIGGRAPH 2007 — the operator and the e1/e2 gradient energies.
  • Rubinstein, M., Shamir, A., Avidan, S. Improved Seam Carving for Video Retargeting, SIGGRAPH 2008 — the forward-energy criterion used here as the fixed scorer (a better removal-cost model than looking only at the removed pixels).
  • Dalal, N., Triggs, B. Histograms of Oriented Gradients for Human Detection, CVPR 2005 — the HOG energy used as a saliency proxy.
  • Hwang, D.-S., Chien, S.-Y. Content-Aware Image Resizing Using Perceptual Seam Carving with Human Attention Model, ICME 2008 — the saliency-driven line.

What You Can Modify

imgproc-lab/mlsgfx_img/custom_seam.py, lines 41–50 only.

def energy_map(img: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """(h,w,3) image in [0,1] -> non-negative (h,w) importance field."""

The driver recomputes your energy after every single removed column and always removes the current minimum-energy vertical seam — you control only the map. You may add helper functions inside the region and use numpy, scipy, scikit-image.

Fixed Pipeline

  • Each setting takes a full-resolution linear Kodak image and removes 200 vertical seams, one at a time, with the standard cumulative-cost DP.
  • Scoring (fixed driver): forward_energy — the total Rubinstein et al. (2008) forward energy introduced by all removals, normalised by pixels removed; salient_keep — how well the strong-gradient mass is preserved relative to the original (1 = identical saliency fraction); jaggy — the mean absolute Laplacian of the carved image relative to the original (a structural-damage proxy).

Evaluation Scenarios

setting image character
woman kodim04 smooth portrait + door frame
parrots kodim07 fine feather texture + stripes
building kodim15 strong geometry + foliage
lighthouse kodim21 held out

Baselines

  • e1 — max over channels of |Ix| + |Iy| (Avidan & Shamir 2007).
  • e2 — max over channels of Ix² + Iy².
  • entropy — local 9×9 entropy surrogate of the luminance.
  • hog — 8×8 HOG cell orientation-histogram energy (Dalal & Triggs 2005).

Metric

Per setting: forward_energy and jaggy (lower better), salient_keep (higher better). The setting score is a weighted mean of the three normalised terms (1.0 / 0.8 / 0.6); the task score is the geometric mean over the four settings.

files.content:
"""Seam carving energy — editable scaffold.

The driver removes a fixed number of columns from the image with the standard
cumulative-energy dynamic program; the only thing under study is the scalar
importance field (the energy map) from which the seams are computed.

Interface contract
------------------
``energy_map(img) -> (h, w)``
    ``img`` float64 ``(h,w,3)`` in [0,1] linear light.  Return a non-negative
    float64 importance field of the same height and width; larger values mean
    "more important — avoid carving here".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from mlsgfx_img.common import (  # noqa: E402
    guard_finite,
    load_kodak,
    print_test_metrics,
    print_train_metrics,
    psnr,
    seed_everything,
    sobel_edges,
    ssim,
)

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE THIS LINE
# =============================================================================

# ----- BEGIN EDITABLE REGION -----
def energy_map(img: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """e1 energy: per-pixel max of the channel gradient magnitudes.

    Avidan, S. and Shamir, A., *Seam Carving for Content-Aware Image Resizing*,
    SIGGRAPH 2007: the sum of the absolute x and y derivatives, maximised over the
    colour channels.
    """
    per_channel = [np.abs(np.gradient(img[..., c], axis=1)) + np.abs(np.gradient(img[..., c], axis=0))
                   for c in range(3)]
    return np.stack(per_channel).max(0)
# ----- END EDITABLE REGION -----

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — seam DP and the forward-energy scorer below
# =============================================================================

SETTINGS = {
    "woman":      {"kodak": 4,  "remove": 200},
    "parrots":    {"kodak": 7,  "remove": 200},
    "building":   {"kodak": 15, "remove": 200},
    "lighthouse": {"kodak": 21, "remove": 200},
}


def carve_column(img: np.ndarray, E: np.ndarray):
    """Remove one minimum-energy vertical seam (standard DP)."""
    h, w = E.shape
    M = E.copy()
    back = np.zeros((h, w), dtype=np.int32)
    for i in range(1, h):
        left = np.roll(M[i - 1], 1)
        right = np.roll(M[i - 1], -1)
        left[0] = np.inf
        right[-1] = np.inf
        choices = np.stack([left, M[i - 1], right], axis=0)
        idx = np.argmin(choices, axis=0)
        M[i] += choices[idx, np.arange(w)]
        back[i] = idx - 1
    j = int(np.argmin(M[-1]))
    seam = np.zeros(h, dtype=np.int32)
    for i in range(h - 1, -1, -1):
        seam[i] = j
        j = j + back[i, j]
    out = np.empty((h, w - 1, img.shape[2]), dtype=np.float64)
    for i in range(h):
        out[i] = np.delete(img[i], seam[i], axis=0)
    return out, seam


def forward_energy_cost(img: np.ndarray, seam: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Rubinstein-Shamir-Avidan (2008) forward energy of removing one seam."""
    h, w = img.shape[:2]
    cost = 0.0
    for i in range(h):
        j = seam[i]
        jm = max(j - 1, 0)
        jp = min(j + 1, w - 1)
        cost += float(np.abs(img[i, jp] - img[i, jm]).sum())
        if i > 0:
            cost += float(np.abs(img[i, j] - img[i - 1, j]).sum())
    return cost


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--setting", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", type=str, default="/tmp/output")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cfg = SETTINGS[args.setting]
    seed_everything(args.seed)

    img = load_kodak(cfg["kodak"], linear=True)
    h0, w0 = img.shape[:2]
    E0 = np.asarray(energy_map(img.copy()), dtype=np.float64)
    if E0.shape != img.shape[:2]:
        print(f"ERROR: energy_map returned {E0.shape}, expected {img.shape[:2]}",
              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(3)
    if np.any(E0 < 0):
        print("ERROR: energy_map must be non-negative", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(3)
    guard_finite("energy map", E0)

    # carve with the agent's energy map, recomputed after each removal
    img_c = img.copy()
    total_forward = 0.0
    for k in range(cfg["remove"]):
        E = np.asarray(energy_map(img_c.copy()), dtype=np.float64)
        guard_finite("energy map", E)
        pre_carve = img_c
        img_c, seam = carve_column(img_c, E)
        total_forward += forward_energy_cost(pre_carve, np.clip(seam, 0, pre_carve.shape[1] - 1))
        if (k + 1) % 50 == 0:
            print_train_metrics(removed=k + 1, width=img_c.shape[1])

    # scorers (fixed):
    # 1) total forward energy introduced (Rubinstein 2008), normalised
    forward_norm = total_forward / (cfg["remove"] * h0 * 3)
    # 2) salient-content preservation: fraction of the original strong-gradient mass
    #    still present in the carved image (approximate content retention)
    sal_orig = (sobel_edges(img.mean(axis=2)) > 0.2).mean()
    sal_carved = (sobel_edges(img_c.mean(axis=2)) > 0.2).mean()
    sal_keep = 1.0 - abs(sal_carved - sal_orig) / max(sal_orig, 1e-9)
    # 3) seam straightness: mean absolute deviation of the seams is not available
    #    anymore; use the average second-difference of the carved image as a jaggy proxy
    from scipy.ndimage import laplace
    jag = float(np.abs(laplace(img_c.mean(axis=2))).mean())
    jag_ref = float(np.abs(laplace(img.mean(axis=2))).mean())

    print_test_metrics(
        forward_energy=forward_norm,
        salient_keep=sal_keep,
        jaggy=jag / max(jag_ref, 1e-12),
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

entropy.content:
def energy_map(img: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """9x9 local histogram entropy of the luminance."""
    from scipy.ndimage import uniform_filter

    gray = img.mean(axis=2)
    # entropy via local mean of -p log p approximated by the local std and the
    # histogram variance proxy (fast surrogate for the full histogram entropy)
    mean = uniform_filter(gray, size=9, mode="reflect")
    mean2 = uniform_filter(gray * gray, size=9, mode="reflect")
    var = np.maximum(mean2 - mean * mean, 0.0)
    # entropy of a locally Gaussian intensity is ~ 0.5 log(2 pi e var)
    return 0.5 * np.log1p(2.0 * np.pi * np.e * var)

hog.content:
def energy_map(img: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """8x8 HOG cell histogram energy."""
    gray = img.mean(axis=2)
    h, w = gray.shape
    gx = np.gradient(gray, axis=1)
    gy = np.gradient(gray, axis=0)
    mag = np.hypot(gx, gy)
    ang = (np.arctan2(gy, gx) % np.pi) / np.pi   # unsigned orientation, [0, 1)
    nbins = 9
    cell = 8
    # vectorised per-cell orientation histograms
    hc, wc = h // cell, w // cell
    m = mag[:hc * cell, :wc * cell].reshape(hc, cell, wc, cell).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
    a = ang[:hc * cell, :wc * cell].reshape(hc, cell, wc, cell).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
    bins = np.clip((a * nbins).astype(int), 0, nbins - 1)
    hist = np.zeros((hc, wc, nbins))
    flat_b = bins.reshape(hc, wc, -1)
    flat_m = m.reshape(hc, wc, -1)
    for b in range(nbins):
        hist[..., b] = (flat_m * (flat_b == b)).sum(axis=2)
    e = np.linalg.norm(hist, axis=2)
    E = np.kron(e, np.ones((cell, cell)))
    out = np.zeros((h, w))
    out[:hc * cell, :wc * cell] = E
    out[:, wc * cell:] = out[:, wc * cell - 1:wc * cell]
    out[hc * cell:, :] = out[hc * cell - 1:hc * cell, :]
    return out + 1e-6 * mag   # small gradient term to break ties

tasks.description_md:
# HDR Tone Mapping

## Research Question

A high-dynamic-range radiance image must be compressed for display. The operator's
job is to shrink the global range without destroying local contrast — how the
compression adapts to the local image content is the whole algorithm. There is no
ground-truth output: operators are scored on what they preserve.

## Background

* Reinhard, E., Stark, M., Shirley, P., Ferwerda, J. *Photographic Tone Reproduction
  for Digital Images*, SIGGRAPH 2002 — key-normalisation, the global L/(1+L) curve,
  and the local dodging-and-burning variant.
* Drago, F., Myszkowski, K., Annen, T., Chiba, N. *Adaptive Logarithmic Mapping for
  Displaying High Contrast Scenes*, CGF 22(3) (EG 2003) — logarithmic compression with
  a per-pixel adaptive base.
* Fattal, R., Lischinski, D., Werman, M. *Gradient Domain High Dynamic Range
  Compression*, SIGGRAPH 2002 — the gradient-domain alternative.
* Durand, F., Dorsey, J. *Fast Bilateral Filtering for the Display of High-Dynamic-
  Range Images*, SIGGRAPH 2002 — the base/detail decomposition view.

## What You Can Modify

`imgproc-lab/mlsgfx_img/custom_tonemap.py`, lines 40–55 only.

```python
def tone_map(hdr: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Linear radiance (h,w,3), unclipped -> display image in [0,1] (sRGB)."""
```

The output is scored directly; the scorer applies no further gamma. You may add
helper functions inside the region and use `numpy`, `scipy`, `scikit-image`.

## Fixed Pipeline

* Each setting renders a 384×256 perspective crop (75° FOV, fixed orientation) from a
  1k equirectangular HDRI and hands the linear radiance to the operator.
* Scoring (all computed by the fixed driver):
  `contrast_corr` = mean Pearson correlation between the log-luminance gradient
  magnitude fields (σ = 1 and σ = 3) of the HDR input and the output;
  `entropy` = 256-bin histogram entropy of the output luminance, normalised to [0,1];
  `sat_clip` = fraction of pixels crushed to ≤ 1/255 or ≥ 254/255.

## Evaluation Scenarios

| setting | HDRI (Poly Haven, CC0) | character |
|---|---|---|
| `kloofendal` | kloofendal_43d_clear | outdoor, hard sun, deep shadows |
| `studio` | studio_small_03 | indoor studio, soft light |
| `sunset` | the_sky_is_on_fire | strong colour gradient, bright sun disk |
| `night` | moonless_golf | held out, very low key |

## Baselines

* **`gamma`** — percentile exposure (99th → white) + sRGB OETF.
* **`reinhard_global`** — key-normalised global L/(1+L) (Reinhard et al. 2002).
* **`reinhard_local`** — the same paper's local dodging-and-burning operator with 8
  scales and ε = 0.05.
* **`drago`** — the adaptive logarithmic operator with base b = 0.85 (Drago et al.
  2003).

## Metric

Per setting: `contrast_corr` and `entropy` (higher better) and `sat_clip` (lower
better). The setting score is a weighted mean of the three normalised terms
(1.0 / 0.8 / 0.6); the task score is the geometric mean over the four settings.

files.content:
"""HDR tone mapping — editable scaffold.

The driver renders a perspective crop of a high-dynamic-range environment map and
hands the linear radiance image to the operator, which must compress it to a
displayable [0,1] image.  There is no reference image: the scorer measures local
contrast preservation, tonal allocation and clipping directly.

Interface contract
------------------
``tone_map(hdr) -> (h, w, 3) in [0, 1]``
    ``hdr`` float64 ``(h,w,3)`` linear radiance, unclipped.  Return the tone-mapped
    image in display sRGB space (the scorer applies no further gamma).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from mlsgfx_img.common import (  # noqa: E402
    guard_finite,
    linear_to_srgb,
    load_hdri,
    luminance,
    print_test_metrics,
    print_train_metrics,
    seed_everything,
)

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE THIS LINE
# =============================================================================

# ----- BEGIN EDITABLE REGION -----
def tone_map(hdr: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Global Reinhard photographic operator.

    Reinhard, E., Stark, M., Shirley, P. and Ferwerda, J., *Photographic Tone
    Reproduction for Digital Images*, SIGGRAPH 2002: key-normalise the scene,
    apply L / (1 + L) to the log-average-key-scaled luminance, recompose colour,
    then gamma-encode.
    """
    eps = 1e-6
    Lw = luminance(hdr)
    log_mean = float(np.exp(np.mean(np.log(Lw + eps))))
    key = 0.18
    Lm = key * Lw / max(log_mean, eps)
    Ld = Lm / (1.0 + Lm)
    out = hdr / np.maximum(Lw, eps)[..., None] * Ld[..., None]
    return np.clip(linear_to_srgb(out), 0.0, 1.0)
# ----- END EDITABLE REGION -----

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — perspective crop and the objective scorer below
# =============================================================================

SETTINGS = {
    "kloofendal":   {"hdri": "kloofendal_43d_clear"},
    "studio":       {"hdri": "studio_small_03"},
    "sunset":       {"hdri": "the_sky_is_on_fire"},
    "night":        {"hdri": "moonless_golf"},
}


def perspective_crop(equi: np.ndarray, fov_deg: float = 75.0,
                     out_w: int = 384, out_h: int = 256,
                     yaw_deg: float = 0.0, pitch_deg: float = 0.0):
    """Sample a perspective view out of an equirectangular map (bilinear)."""
    H, W = equi.shape[:2]
    fov = np.deg2rad(fov_deg)
    f = 0.5 * out_w / np.tan(fov / 2)
    xs = (np.arange(out_w) + 0.5 - out_w / 2) / f
    ys = (np.arange(out_h) + 0.5 - out_h / 2) / f
    X, Y = np.meshgrid(xs, ys)
    Z = np.ones_like(X)
    d = np.stack([X, -Y, Z], axis=-1)
    d /= np.linalg.norm(d, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    yaw, pitch = np.deg2rad(yaw_deg), np.deg2rad(pitch_deg)
    Ry = np.array([[np.cos(yaw), 0, np.sin(yaw)], [0, 1, 0], [-np.sin(yaw), 0, np.cos(yaw)]])
    Rp = np.array([[1, 0, 0], [0, np.cos(pitch), -np.sin(pitch)], [0, np.sin(pitch), np.cos(pitch)]])
    d = d @ (Rp @ Ry).T
    lon = np.arctan2(d[..., 0], d[..., 2])
    lat = np.arcsin(np.clip(d[..., 1], -1.0, 1.0))
    u = (lon / (2 * np.pi) + 0.5) * W - 0.5
    v = (0.5 - lat / np.pi) * H - 0.5
    u0 = np.clip(np.floor(u).astype(int), 0, W - 1)
    v0 = np.clip(np.floor(v).astype(int), 0, H - 1)
    fu, fv = (u - u0)[..., None], (v - v0)[..., None]
    u1, v1 = (u0 + 1) % W, np.clip(v0 + 1, 0, H - 1)
    return ((1 - fu) * (1 - fv) * equi[v0, u0] + fu * (1 - fv) * equi[v0, u1]
            + (1 - fu) * fv * equi[v1, u0] + fu * fv * equi[v1, u1])


def gradient_field(log_lum: np.ndarray, sigma: float) -> np.ndarray:
    from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter
    s = gaussian_filter(log_lum, sigma)
    gy, gx = np.gradient(s)
    return np.hypot(gx, gy)


def corr(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> float:
    a = a - a.mean()
    b = b - b.mean()
    denom = np.linalg.norm(a) * np.linalg.norm(b)
    return float((a * b).sum() / denom) if denom > 0 else 0.0


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--setting", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", type=str, default="/tmp/output")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cfg = SETTINGS[args.setting]
    seed_everything(args.seed)

    equi = load_hdri(cfg["hdri"])
    hdr = perspective_crop(equi)
    in_lum = luminance(hdr)
    dr = float(np.log2(max(in_lum.max(), 1e-12) / max(np.percentile(in_lum, 1), 1e-12)))
    print_train_metrics(scene=cfg["hdri"], dynamic_range_stops=dr)

    out = np.asarray(tone_map(hdr.copy()), dtype=np.float64)
    if out.shape != hdr.shape:
        print(f"ERROR: tone_map returned {out.shape}, expected {hdr.shape}",
              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(3)
    guard_finite("tone-mapped image", out)
    if out.min() < -1e-6 or out.max() > 1.0 + 1e-6:
        print("ERROR: tone_map output must lie in [0,1]", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(3)

    out_lum = np.clip(luminance(out), 0.0, 1.0)
    log_in = np.log1p(in_lum * 100.0)      # compress HDR log range
    c1 = corr(gradient_field(log_in, 1.0), gradient_field(out_lum, 1.0))
    c2 = corr(gradient_field(log_in, 3.0), gradient_field(out_lum, 3.0))
    hist, _ = np.histogram(np.clip(out_lum, 0, 1), bins=256, range=(0, 1))
    p = hist[hist > 0] / max(hist.sum(), 1)
    entropy = float(-np.sum(p * np.log(p)) / np.log(256.0))
    clip = float(np.mean((out_lum <= 1.0 / 255.0) | (out_lum >= 254.0 / 255.0)))

    print_test_metrics(
        contrast_corr=0.5 * (c1 + c2),
        entropy=entropy,
        sat_clip=clip,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def tone_map(hdr: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Global Reinhard photographic operator."""
    eps = 1e-6
    Lw = luminance(hdr)
    log_mean = float(np.exp(np.mean(np.log(Lw + eps))))
    Lm = 0.18 * Lw / max(log_mean, eps)
    Ld = Lm / (1.0 + Lm)
    out = hdr / np.maximum(Lw, eps)[..., None] * Ld[..., None]
    return np.clip(linear_to_srgb(out), 0.0, 1.0)

reinhard_local.content:
def tone_map(hdr: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Local Reinhard dodging-and-burning."""
    from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter

    eps = 1e-6
    Lw = luminance(hdr)
    log_mean = float(np.exp(np.mean(np.log(Lw + eps))))
    Lm = 0.18 * Lw / max(log_mean, eps)

    phi = 8.0
    eps_c = 0.05
    scales = [2.0 ** k for k in range(8)]   # dyadic scales: 1, 2, 4, ..., 128
    blurred = [gaussian_filter(Lm, sigma=s, mode="reflect") for s in scales]
    # per-pixel scale selection: the largest scale s_i such that the
    # centre-surround contrast between s_i and s_{i+1} stays below eps_c.
    V_sel = blurred[0].copy()
    locked = np.zeros(Lm.shape, dtype=bool)
    for i in range(len(scales) - 1):
        V1, V2 = blurred[i], blurred[i + 1]
        contrast = np.abs((V1 - V2) / ((2.0 ** phi) * eps_c / (scales[i] ** 2) + V1))
        fails_now = (contrast > eps_c) & ~locked
        V_sel = np.where(fails_now, V1, V_sel)
        locked = locked | fails_now
        V_sel = np.where(~locked, V2, V_sel)
    Ld = Lm / (1.0 + V_sel)
    out = hdr / np.maximum(Lw, eps)[..., None] * Ld[..., None]
    return np.clip(linear_to_srgb(out), 0.0, 1.0)

def tone_map(hdr: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Drago et al. (2003) adaptive logarithmic mapping."""
    eps = 1e-6
    Lw = luminance(hdr)
    Lmax = float(Lw.max())
    log_mean = float(np.exp(np.mean(np.log(Lw + eps))))
    # Eq. 3 of the paper: display luminance via adaptive base logarithm.
    # ln(Lw+1) / [log10(Lwmax+1) * ln(2 + 8*(Lw/Lwmax)^(log(bias)/log(0.5)))]
    Ld = (np.log1p(Lw) / np.log10(Lmax + 1.0 + eps)
          / np.log(2.0 + 8.0 * (Lw / (Lmax + eps)) ** (np.log(0.85) / np.log(0.5))))
    out = hdr / np.maximum(Lw, eps)[..., None] * Ld[..., None]
    return np.clip(linear_to_srgb(np.clip(out, 0.0, 1.0)), 0.0, 1.0)

gamma.content:
def tone_map(hdr: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Percentile exposure + gamma."""
    lum = luminance(hdr)
    hi = float(np.percentile(lum, 99.0))
    scale = 1.0 / max(hi, 1e-12)
    out = hdr * scale
    return np.clip(linear_to_srgb(np.clip(out, 0.0, 1.0)), 0.0, 1.0)

# Illuminant Estimation (White Balance)

## Research Question

The same scene under a coloured illuminant produces a systematically distorted image;
colour constancy means estimating the illuminant from the image statistics alone and
neutralising it. Which statistic of the image most reliably points back to the
illuminant?

## Background

* Buchsbaum, G. *A Spatial Processor Model for Object Colour Perception*, Journal of
  the Franklin Institute 310, 1980 — the gray-world assumption.
* Land, E. H. *The Retinex Theory of Color Vision*, Scientific American 237, 1977 —
  the white-patch (Max-RGB) idea.
* Finlayson, G. D., Trezzi, E. *Shades of Gray and Colour Constancy*, CIC 2004 — the
  Minkowski p-norm family unifying both.
* van de Weijer, J., Gevers, T., Gijsenij, A. *Edge-Based Color Constancy*, IEEE TIP
  16(9), 2007 — gray assumptions on spatial derivatives.
* Gijsenij, A., Gevers, T., van de Weijer, J. *Computational Color Constancy: Survey
  and Experiments*, IEEE TIP 20(9), 2011 — the standard comparison.

## What You Can Modify

`imgproc-lab/mlsgfx_img/custom_whitebalance.py`, lines 42–49 only.

```python
def estimate_illuminant(img: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Distorted linear-light (h,w,3) image -> (3,) gains that neutralise it."""
```

Only the distorted image is available; the true illuminant is never revealed. You
may add helper functions inside the region and use `numpy`, `scipy`, `scikit-image`.

## Fixed Pipeline

* Each setting takes a full-resolution linear Kodak image, multiplies it by a fixed
  illuminant gain, and clips to [0,1] (so bright channels saturate, as in a real
  camera).
* The driver's scoring compares your gain direction to the true neutralising gain
  (1/illuminant) by angle, and applies your correction and measures the recovered
  image against the original.

## Evaluation Scenarios

| setting | image | illuminant cast |
|---|---|---|
| `kodim02` | girl | strong warm (red) |
| `kodim06` | flowers/window | strong cool (blue) |
| `kodim13` | house | mild warm |
| `kodim20` | held out | mild cool |

## Baselines

* **`gray_world`** — inverse of the channel means (Buchsbaum 1980).
* **`white_patch`** — inverse of the channel maxima (Max-RGB).
* **`shades_of_gray`** — inverse of the Minkowski p = 6 norm (Finlayson & Trezzi
  2004).
* **`gray_edge`** — first-order grey edge with p = 5 (van de Weijer et al. 2007).

## Metric

Per setting: `angular_err` (angle between the estimated and true neutralising gain,
degrees, lower better) and `psnr_corrected` (PSNR of the corrected image against the
original, higher better). The setting score is a weighted mean of the two normalised
terms; the task score is the geometric mean over the four settings.

files.content:
"""Illuminant estimation (white balance) — editable scaffold.

The driver applies a known illuminant gain to a linear-light image and hands over
the distorted image.  The algorithm estimates the illuminant; the driver applies
the diagonal correction and scores both the illuminant direction and the corrected
image.

Interface contract
------------------
``estimate_illuminant(img) -> (3,)``
    ``img`` float64 ``(h,w,3)`` in [0,1]-ish linear light under the unknown
    illuminant.  Return the estimated illuminant gains ``(3,)`` such that
    ``img * gains`` neutralises it (larger gain = boost that channel).  Any
    positive scale is fine (normalised by the driver).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from mlsgfx_img.common import (  # noqa: E402
    apply_illuminant,
    guard_finite,
    load_kodak,
    print_test_metrics,
    print_train_metrics,
    psnr,
    seed_everything,
)

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE THIS LINE
# =============================================================================

# ----- BEGIN EDITABLE REGION -----
def estimate_illuminant(img: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Gray-world: the scene average is achromatic.

    Buchsbaum, G., *A Spatial Processor Model for Object Colour Perception*,
    Journal of the Franklin Institute 310, 1980: divide by the channel means.
    """
    mean = img.reshape(-1, 3).mean(axis=0)
    return mean.mean() / np.maximum(mean, 1e-12)
# ----- END EDITABLE REGION -----

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — illuminant model and evaluation below
# =============================================================================

SETTINGS = {
    "kodim02": {"kodak": 2,  "illum": (1.35, 1.00, 0.72)},
    "kodim06": {"kodak": 6,  "illum": (0.80, 1.00, 1.45)},
    "kodim13": {"kodak": 13, "illum": (1.15, 0.90, 0.80)},
    "kodim20": {"kodak": 20, "illum": (0.90, 1.05, 1.30)},
}


def angular_error(est, true):
    est = est / np.linalg.norm(est)
    true = true / np.linalg.norm(true)
    return float(np.degrees(np.arccos(np.clip(np.dot(est, true), -1.0, 1.0))))


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--setting", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", type=str, default="/tmp/output")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cfg = SETTINGS[args.setting]
    seed_everything(args.seed)

    clean = load_kodak(cfg["kodak"], linear=True)
    illum = np.asarray(cfg["illum"], dtype=np.float64)
    distorted = np.clip(apply_illuminant(clean, illum), 0.0, 1.0)
    print_train_metrics(image=f"kodim{cfg['kodak']:02d}")

    est = np.asarray(estimate_illuminant(distorted.copy()), dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)
    if est.shape != (3,) or not np.all(np.isfinite(est)) or np.any(est <= 0):
        print("ERROR: estimate_illuminant must return three positive finite gains",
              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(3)

    # the correction that neutralises the distortion is img / illum (up to scale);
    # the estimated gains should align with 1/illum
    true_gain = 1.0 / illum
    ang = angular_error(est, true_gain)

    corrected = distorted * est[None, None, :]
    corrected = corrected / max(corrected.mean(), 1e-12) * clean.mean()
    corrected = np.clip(corrected, 0.0, 1.0)

    print_test_metrics(
        angular_err=ang,
        psnr_corrected=psnr(corrected, clean),
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

gray_edge.content:
def estimate_illuminant(img: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """First-order grey edge (derivative gray-world), p = 5."""
    from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter

    p = 5.0
    norm = np.zeros(3)
    for c in range(3):
        sm = gaussian_filter(img[..., c], sigma=1.0, mode="reflect")
        dx = np.abs(np.gradient(sm, axis=1))
        dy = np.abs(np.gradient(sm, axis=0))
        d = np.hypot(dx, dy)
        norm[c] = (d ** p).mean() ** (1.0 / p)
    return norm.mean() / np.maximum(norm, 1e-12)

# Density Activation / Density Head for a NeRF

## Research Question

The volume density must be non-negative and must start from a sensible prior; the
head that maps the geometry features to the density decides how fast the field
converges and how clean the free space is. Which density parameterisation trains
fastest and cleanest?

## Background

* Mildenhall, B., Srinivasan, P. P., Tancik, M., Barron, J. T., Ramamoorthi, R.,
  Ng, R. *NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis*,
  ECCV 2020 — the ReLU density.
* Wang, P., Liu, Y., Chen, Z., Liu, L. *NeuS: Learning Neural Implicit Surfaces by
  Volume Rendering*, NeurIPS 2021 — the softplus density.
* Li, R., Tancik, M., Kanazawa, A. *NerfAcc: Efficient Sampling Leverages
  Localized Importance*, ICCV 2023 — the truncated-exponential density used in
  instant-NGP pipelines.

## What You Can Modify

`nerfacc/mlsgfx_nerf/custom_density.py`, lines 42–56 only.

```python
def make_density_head(geo_feat_dim: int) -> torch.nn.Module:
    """Return a module mapping geometry features (n, geo_feat_dim) -> density (n,1)."""
```

You may add helper classes inside the region and use `torch`. The field, the
occupancy sampling, the renderer and the trainer are fixed.

## Fixed Pipeline

* Each setting trains a pure-PyTorch NeRF (positional encoding + MLP) on a
  NeRF-Synthetic scene for 6000 steps with nerfacc's occupancy-grid sampling, then
  evaluates on the test split.
* Scoring: test PSNR and the training loss after the warmup phase.

## Evaluation Scenarios

| setting | scene |
|---|---|
| `lego` | lego (hard edges, occlusion) |
| `chair` | chair (thin structure) |
| `mic` | mic (fine detail) |
| `drums` | held out, transparency |

## Baselines

* **`relu`** — density = relu(MLP(feat)) (NeRF).
* **`softplus`** — density = softplus(MLP(feat) − 1) (NeuS).
* **`trunc_exp`** — density = exp(clamp(MLP(feat))) (NerfAcc).
* **`softplus_shifted`** — softplus with a learnable scale.

## Metric

Per setting: `psnr` (higher better) and `loss_2k` (training loss early in training,
lower better — convergence speed). The setting score is a weighted mean of the two
normalised terms (1.0 / 0.6); the task score is the geometric mean over the four
settings.

"""Density activation / density head for a NeRF — editable scaffold.

The field's geometry MLP produces a feature; the density head maps it to the
volume density.  The choice of activation/head decides the density's positivity,
its gradient behaviour and how fast the field converges.  Only the density head
is under study; the field, the renderer and the trainer are fixed.

Interface contract
------------------
``make_density_head(geo_feat_dim) -> torch.nn.Module``
    Return a module mapping the geometry feature ``(n, geo_feat_dim)`` to the
    non-negative density ``(n, 1)``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from mlsgfx_nerf.common import (  # noqa: E402
    DATA_DIR,
    print_test_metrics,
    print_train_metrics,
    seed_everything,
)
from mlsgfx_nerf.trainer import (  # noqa: E402
    NeRFField,
    make_field,
    train_nerf,
)

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE THIS LINE
# =============================================================================

# ----- BEGIN EDITABLE REGION -----
def make_density_head(geo_feat_dim: int):
    """Shifted-softplus head, log(1+exp(x-1)) (mip-NeRF 360)."""
    import torch
    import torch.nn as nn
    import torch.nn.functional as F

    class Head(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, d):
            super().__init__()
            self.net = nn.Linear(d, 1)

        def forward(self, feat):
            return F.softplus(self.net(feat) - 1.0)

    return Head(geo_feat_dim)
# ----- END EDITABLE REGION -----

# =============================================================================

    scene_root = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, cfg["scene"])

# Photometric Loss Shape for NeRF

## Research Question

The per-ray pixel loss that drives a NeRF decides where the field spends its error
budget: linear L2 under-weights dark regions, and the bright HDR outliers dominate
the gradient. Which loss shape converges to the cleanest field?

## Background

* Mildenhall, B., Srinivasan, P. P., Tancik, M., Barron, J. T., Ramamoorthi, R.,
  Ng, R. *NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis*,
  ECCV 2020 — L2 on linear radiance.
* Mildenhall, B., Hedman, P., Martin-Brualla, R., Srinivasan, P. P., Barron, J. T.
  *Mip-NeRF 360: Unbounded Anti-Aliased Neural Radiance Fields*, CVPR 2022 — the
  robust-loss motivation.
* Charbonnier, P., Blanc-Féraud, L., Aubert, G., Barlaud, M. *Two Deterministic
  Half-Quadratic Regularization Algorithms for Computed Imaging*, ICIP 1994 — the
  Charbonnier pseudo-Huber loss.

## What You Can Modify

* Each setting trains a pure-PyTorch NeRF on a NeRF-Synthetic scene for 6000 steps

## Evaluation Scenarios

| setting | scene |
|---|---|
| `lego` | lego |
| `chair` | chair |

## Baselines

The per-ray pixel loss that drives the field optimisation.  The loss shape decides
how the field distributes its error budget across bright and dark regions.  Only
the loss is under study; the field and the trainer are fixed.

Interface contract
------------------

"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys

    return ((rgb - target) ** 2).mean()

# Occupancy-Grid Update Rule for NeRF

## Research Question

Efficient NeRF sampling skips empty space using a coarse occupancy grid refreshed
during training. How the grid is updated — which cells are re-evaluated, how the
estimate is blended, and when — decides both the sampling speed and how quickly
the field resolves geometry. Which update policy trains the cleanest field?

## Background

* Li, R., Tancik, M., Kanazawa, A. *NerfAcc: Efficient Sampling Leverages Localized
  Importance*, ICCV 2023 — the occupancy-grid sampling and its update policy.
* Müller, T., Evans, A., Schied, C., Keller, A. *Instant Neural Graphics Primitives
  with a Multiresolution Hash Encoding*, SIGGRAPH 2022 — the occupancy grid that
  made real-time NeRF training possible.
* Fridovich-Keil, S., Yu, A., Tancik, M., Chen, Q., Recht, B., Kanazawa, A.
  *Plenoxels: Radiance Fields without Neural Networks*, CVPR 2022 — the density-grid
  view.

## What You Can Modify

`nerfacc/mlsgfx_nerf/custom_occupdate.py`, lines 43–55 only.

```python
def update_occupancy(estimator, field, step, render_step_size) -> None:
    """Called once per training step to refresh the occupancy grid."""
```

`estimator` is the nerfacc `OccGridEstimator`; call `field.query_density(x)` to get
densities. The estimator's `update_every_n_steps(step, occ_eval_fn, occ_thre,
ema_decay, warmup_steps, n)` exposes the standard knobs; you may also drive it with
your own cell sampling. You may add helper functions inside the region and use
`torch`, `numpy`.

## Fixed Pipeline

* Each setting trains a pure-PyTorch NeRF on a NeRF-Synthetic scene for 6000 steps
  with nerfacc's occupancy-grid sampling; your hook refreshes the grid.
* Scoring: test PSNR and mean rendering samples per training ray, evaluated at an early checkpoint (step 1500) where update policies still differ, plus final PSNR.

## Evaluation Scenarios

| setting | scene |
|---|---|
| `lego` | lego |
| `chair` | chair |
| `mic` | mic |
| `drums` | held out |

## Baselines

* **`nerfacc_default`** — nerfacc's shipped rule: refresh a uniform sample plus an
  equal number of currently-occupied cells, and blend with the *decayed maximum*
  `occ <- max(occ * 0.95, occ_new)` inherited from Instant-NGP.
* **`ema_true`** — same cells, but the arithmetic moving average the name usually
  implies, `occ <- 0.95 * occ + 0.05 * occ_new`. The shipped max makes occupancy
  sticky; this lets a cell that empties follow the field down at once.
* **`importance`** — same blend and the same evaluation budget, but cells are drawn
  with probability proportional to their current occupancy (half the budget stays
  uniform so empty cells can revive) instead of nerfacc's uniform+occupied mix.
* **`warmstart_dense`** — nerfacc's rule with a 4x longer dense warm start
  (`warmup_steps=1024` rather than 256): every cell is evaluated on every update
  until step 1024, then the sparse sample takes over.

## Metric

Per setting the score is taken mostly at an EARLY checkpoint (training step
1500): `psnr_early` (higher better) and `spr_early` (mean rendering samples per
training ray accumulated up to that step, lower better), plus the final `psnr`
(higher better) at half weight. The update policy decides how quickly the grid
becomes accurate; by the end of training every policy has converged to the
same grid, so only the early checkpoint separates them. A policy that reaches
high PSNR early while sampling little wins; one that culls aggressively but
loses PSNR, or samples everything, does not.

files.content:
"""Occupancy-grid update rule for NeRF — editable scaffold.

Efficient NeRF sampling relies on a coarse occupancy grid that is refreshed as
training proceeds.  How the grid is updated — which cells are re-evaluated and how
the occupancy is blended — decides both speed and quality.  Only the update rule
is under study; the field and the renderer are fixed.

Interface contract
------------------
``update_occupancy(estimator, field, step, render_step_size)``
    Called once per training step.  ``estimator`` is the nerfacc OccGridEstimator
    (its ``.occs`` occupancy field is what you update), ``field`` the radiance
    field (call ``field.query_density(x)``), ``step`` the integer step index,
    ``render_step_size`` the fixed step.  Update ``estimator.occs`` in place.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from mlsgfx_nerf.common import (  # noqa: E402
    DATA_DIR,
    print_test_metrics,
    print_train_metrics,
    seed_everything,
)
from mlsgfx_nerf.trainer import (  # noqa: E402
    make_field,
    train_nerf,
)

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE THIS LINE
# =============================================================================

# ----- BEGIN EDITABLE REGION -----
def update_occupancy(estimator, field, step, render_step_size):
    """nerfacc's default update: evaluate a random subset of cells every step.

    Li, R., Tancik, M. and Kanazawa, A., *NerfAcc: Efficient Sampling Leverages
    Localized Importance*, ICCV 2023: refresh a random 1/4 of the cells with the
    current density estimate, then decay all occupancies by 0.95.
    """
    import torch

    def occ_eval(x):
        return field.query_density(x) * render_step_size

    estimator.update_every_n_steps(step, occ_eval_fn=occ_eval, occ_thre=1e-2)
# ----- END EDITABLE REGION -----

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — training and evaluation below
# =============================================================================

SETTINGS = {
    "lego":   {"scene": "lego"},
    "chair":  {"scene": "chair"},
    "mic":    {"scene": "mic"},
    "drums":  {"scene": "drums"},
}


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--setting", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", type=str, default="/tmp/output")
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=6000)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cfg = SETTINGS[args.setting]
    seed_everything(args.seed)
    os.environ.setdefault("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "0")
    scene_root = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, cfg["scene"])
    print_train_metrics(setting=args.setting, steps=args.steps)

    field = make_field()
    # The update policy decides how FAST the grid becomes accurate; by the end
    # of training every policy has converged to the same grid (measured: three
    # of four within 0.1 dB / 0.3% samples at 6000 steps). So the scored
    # quantities are taken at an early checkpoint (step 1500) as well as at
    # the end: PSNR reached by then, and samples spent per ray to get there.
    EARLY = 1500
    # 64^3, not nerfacc's default 128^3: at 128 the grid is so over-provisioned
    # that every sane update policy converges to the same occupancy within a
    # few hundred steps (measured: three policies within 0.1 dB and 0.03% of
    # samples-per-ray at both step 1500 and step 6000). At 64 the grid is the
    # binding constraint, so which cells the policy keeps actually decides
    # what the renderer can see.
    GRID = 64
    psnr, history, stats = train_nerf(field, scene_root, steps=args.steps,
                                      update_hook=update_occupancy, seed=args.seed,
                                      return_stats=True, eval_steps=[EARLY],
                                      grid_resolution=GRID)
    print_train_metrics(final_loss=history[-1] if history else float("nan"),
                        steps_rendered=stats["steps_rendered"])
    # An occupancy grid exists to cull empty space: its effect is sampling
    # efficiency (samples per ray) at equal quality, which is what nerfacc
    # itself reports. Final PSNR alone does not separate update policies at
    # a fixed step budget (measured: 3 baselines within 0.03 dB).
    print_test_metrics(psnr=psnr, samples_per_ray=stats["samples_per_ray"],
                       psnr_early=stats.get(f"psnr_{EARLY}", float("nan")),
                       spr_early=stats.get(f"samples_per_ray_{EARLY}", float("nan")),
                       loss_2k=history[1] if len(history) > 1 else float("nan"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

ema_true.content:
def update_occupancy(estimator, field, step, render_step_size):
    """Arithmetic EMA blend instead of nerfacc's decayed maximum."""
    import torch

    if step % 16 != 0:
        return

    ema_decay = 0.95
    occ_thre = 1e-2
    warmup_steps = 256

    def occ_eval(x):
        return field.query_density(x) * render_step_size

    with torch.no_grad():
        if step < warmup_steps:
            lvl_indices = estimator._get_all_cells()
        else:
            n = estimator.cells_per_lvl // 4
            lvl_indices = estimator._sample_uniform_and_occupied_cells(n)

        for lvl, indices in enumerate(lvl_indices):
            grid_coords = estimator.grid_coords[indices]
            x = (grid_coords + torch.rand_like(grid_coords, dtype=torch.float32)) / estimator.resolution
            x = estimator.aabbs[lvl, :3] + x * (estimator.aabbs[lvl, 3:] - estimator.aabbs[lvl, :3])
            occ = occ_eval(x).squeeze(-1)
            cell_ids = lvl * estimator.cells_per_lvl + indices
            # the one change: arithmetic EMA, not max(old * decay, new)
            estimator.occs[cell_ids] = (
                ema_decay * estimator.occs[cell_ids] + (1.0 - ema_decay) * occ
            )

        thre = torch.clamp(estimator.occs[estimator.occs >= 0].mean(), max=occ_thre)
        estimator.binaries = (estimator.occs > thre).view(estimator.binaries.shape)

def update_occupancy(estimator, field, step, render_step_size):
    """Dense early (first 1024 steps), sparse late."""
    import torch
    def occ_eval(x):
        return field.query_density(x) * render_step_size
    estimator.update_every_n_steps(step, occ_eval_fn=occ_eval, occ_thre=1e-2,
                                   warmup_steps=1024)

importance.content:
def update_occupancy(estimator, field, step, render_step_size):
    """Refresh cells with probability proportional to current occupancy."""
    import torch

    if step % 16 != 0:
        return

    ema_decay = 0.95
    occ_thre = 1e-2
    warmup_steps = 256
    uniform_frac = 0.5  # half the budget stays uniform so empty cells can revive

    def occ_eval(x):
        return field.query_density(x) * render_step_size

    with torch.no_grad():
        if step < warmup_steps:
            lvl_indices = estimator._get_all_cells()
        else:
            n = estimator.cells_per_lvl // 4
            n_unif = int(n * uniform_frac)
            n_imp = 2 * n - n_unif  # same total budget as uniform + occupied
            lvl_indices = []
            for lvl in range(estimator.levels):
                cell_ids_base = lvl * estimator.cells_per_lvl
                occs_lvl = estimator.occs[cell_ids_base : cell_ids_base + estimator.cells_per_lvl]
                visible = occs_lvl >= 0.0

                unif = torch.randint(estimator.cells_per_lvl, (n_unif,), device=estimator.device)
                unif = unif[occs_lvl[unif] >= 0.0]

                w = torch.where(visible, occs_lvl.clamp_min(0.0), torch.zeros_like(occs_lvl))
                if float(w.sum()) > 0.0:
                    imp = torch.multinomial(w, n_imp, replacement=True)
                else:
                    imp = torch.randint(estimator.cells_per_lvl, (n_imp,), device=estimator.device)
                    imp = imp[occs_lvl[imp] >= 0.0]

                lvl_indices.append(torch.cat([unif, imp], dim=0))

        for lvl, indices in enumerate(lvl_indices):
            grid_coords = estimator.grid_coords[indices]
            x = (grid_coords + torch.rand_like(grid_coords, dtype=torch.float32)) / estimator.resolution
            x = estimator.aabbs[lvl, :3] + x * (estimator.aabbs[lvl, 3:] - estimator.aabbs[lvl, :3])
            occ = occ_eval(x).squeeze(-1)
            cell_ids = lvl * estimator.cells_per_lvl + indices
            estimator.occs[cell_ids] = torch.maximum(estimator.occs[cell_ids] * ema_decay, occ)

        thre = torch.clamp(estimator.occs[estimator.occs >= 0].mean(), max=occ_thre)
        estimator.binaries = (estimator.occs > thre).view(estimator.binaries.shape)

# View-Dependence Encoding for a NeRF

## Research Question

View-dependent effects (specularity, reflections) require the colour head to see the
view direction. The encoding of that direction decides how much view-dependent
structure the field can represent. Which view encoding captures the most view
dependence without overfitting?

## Background

* Mildenhall, B., Srinivasan, P. P., Tancik, M., Barron, J. T., Ramamoorthi, R.,
  Ng, R. *NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis*,
  ECCV 2020 — the 4-frequency positional encoding.
* Kerbl, B., Kopanas, G., Leimkühler, T., Drettakis, G. *3D Gaussian Splatting for
  Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering*, SIGGRAPH 2023 — the spherical-harmonics view
  encoding used by splatting.
* Barron, J. T., Mildenhall, B., Tancik, M., Hedman, P., Martin-Brualla, R.,
  Srinivasan, P. P. *Mip-NeRF: A Multiscale Representation for Anti-Aliasing Neural
  Radiance Fields*, ICCV 2021 — the integrated positional encoding.

## What You Can Modify

`nerfacc/mlsgfx_nerf/custom_viewenc.py`, lines 42–44 only.

```python
def view_encode(directions) -> torch.Tensor:
    """(n,3) unit view directions -> encoded features (n, d), any fixed d."""
```

You may add helper functions inside the region and use `torch`, `numpy`.

## Fixed Pipeline

* Each setting trains a pure-PyTorch NeRF on a NeRF-Synthetic scene for 6000 steps;
  the colour head's input width adapts to your encoding's width.
* Scoring: test PSNR and the training loss after the warmup phase.

## Evaluation Scenarios

| setting | scene |
|---|---|
| `lego` | lego |
| `chair` | chair |
| `mic` | mic |
| `materials` | held out, glossy |

## Baselines

* **`diffuse_only`** — no view dependence (a constant token).
* **`pe4`** — 4-frequency positional encoding (NeRF).
* **`sh2`** — real spherical harmonics up to degree 2.
* **`ipe_cone`** — integrated positional encoding under a small cone (Mip-NeRF).

## Metric

Per setting: `psnr` (higher better) and `loss_2k` (lower better). The setting score
is a weighted mean of the two normalised terms (1.0 / 0.6); the task score is the
geometric mean over the four settings.

"""View-dependence encoding for a NeRF — editable scaffold.

How the view direction is encoded into the colour head decides how well the field
captures specular reflection and view-dependent effects.  Only the view encoding
is under study; the field and trainer are fixed.

Interface contract
------------------
``view_encode(directions) -> torch.Tensor``
    ``directions`` (n,3) unit view directions.  Return the encoded features fed to
    the colour head (any fixed output width; the trainer adapts the head's input
    width to your output).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from mlsgfx_nerf.common import (  # noqa: E402
    DATA_DIR,
    print_test_metrics,
    print_train_metrics,
    seed_everything,
)
from mlsgfx_nerf.trainer import (  # noqa: E402
    make_field,
    train_nerf,
    positional_encoding,
)

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE THIS LINE
# =============================================================================

# ----- BEGIN EDITABLE REGION -----
def view_encode(directions):
    """Positional encoding of the direction at 4 frequencies (NeRF's default)."""
    return positional_encoding(directions, 4)
# ----- END EDITABLE REGION -----

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — training and evaluation below
# =============================================================================

SETTINGS = {
    "lego":   {"scene": "lego"},
    "chair":  {"scene": "chair"},
    "mic":    {"scene": "mic"},
    "materials": {"scene": "materials"},
}


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--setting", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", type=str, default="/tmp/output")
    ap.add_argument("--steps", type=int, default=6000)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    import torch
    cfg = SETTINGS[args.setting]
    seed_everything(args.seed)
    os.environ.setdefault("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "0")
    scene_root = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, cfg["scene"])
    print_train_metrics(setting=args.setting, steps=args.steps)

    # measure the encoded width and build a field whose color head matches
    d = torch.zeros(4, 3)
    d[:, 2] = -1.0
    enc_dim = view_encode(d).shape[-1]
    from mlsgfx_nerf.trainer import NeRFField
    import torch.nn as nn
    hidden = 128
    geo_feat_dim = 15
    # build the field with a color head sized to the encoded width
    field = NeRFField(dir_freq=4)
    field.color_head = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(geo_feat_dim + enc_dim, hidden // 2), nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(hidden // 2, 3), nn.Sigmoid())

    # monkey-patch the forward to use our view_encode
    orig_forward = field.forward
    def fwd(positions, directions):
        h = field.backbone(positional_encoding(positions, field.pos_freq))
        geo = field.geo_out(h)
        density = field.density_head(geo)
        dd = directions / torch.clamp(directions.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True), min=1e-9)
        rgb = field.color_head(torch.cat([geo, view_encode(dd)], dim=-1))
        return rgb, density
    field.forward = fwd

    psnr, history = train_nerf(field, scene_root, steps=args.steps, seed=args.seed)
    print_train_metrics(final_loss=history[-1] if history else float("nan"))
    print_test_metrics(psnr=psnr, loss_2k=history[1] if len(history) > 1 else float("nan"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def view_encode(directions):
    """Real spherical harmonics up to degree 2."""
    import torch
    d = directions / torch.clamp(directions.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True), min=1e-9)
    x, y, z = d[..., 0], d[..., 1], d[..., 2]
    c = [
        0.2820947918 * torch.ones_like(x),  # l=0 term is a constant; stack needs a tensor
        0.4886025119 * y,
        0.4886025119 * z,
        0.4886025119 * x,
        1.0925484306 * x * y,
        1.0925484306 * y * z,
        0.3153915653 * (3 * z * z - 1),
        1.0925484306 * x * z,
        0.5462742153 * (x * x - y * y),
    ]
    return torch.stack(c, dim=-1)

ipe_cone.content:
def view_encode(directions):
    """PE of the direction with mip-NeRF's per-octave Gaussian attenuation."""
    import math
    import torch
    d = directions / torch.clamp(directions.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True), min=1e-9)
    sigma = 0.2                 # angular smoothing width in radians (chosen, not a pixel cone)
    cov = sigma ** 2
    freqs = [1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0]
    feats = [d]
    for f in freqs:
        # mip-NeRF Eq. 14: E[sin(2^l x)] = sin(2^l mu) * exp(-(1/2) 4^l sigma^2).
        # A Python float, not a tensor, so it cannot be broadcast-mangled.
        attenuate = math.exp(-0.5 * (f ** 2) * cov)
        feats.append(torch.sin(d * (math.pi * f)) * attenuate)
        feats.append(torch.cos(d * (math.pi * f)) * attenuate)
    return torch.cat(feats, dim=-1)

# Correspondence Weighting for Point-to-Plane ICP

## Research Question

Iterative Closest Point aligns a source point cloud to a target by alternating
nearest-neighbour matching and a rigid least-squares step. When the target has
noise and outliers, the per-correspondence weights decide whether the registration

files.content:
"""Correspondence weighting kernel for ICP — editable scaffold.

Two partial point clouds of the same surface are related by a known rigid
transform plus noise and outliers.  The fixed driver runs a point-to-plane ICP
loop (Gauss-Newton); at each iteration it calls the algorithm for the
per-correspondence weights.  Only the weighting is under study.

Interface contract
------------------
``correspondence_weights(src_matched, tgt_matched, tgt_normals, distances,
  iteration) -> np.ndarray (m,)``
    The matched source/target points, the target normals, the matched distances,
    and the iteration index.  Return non-negative weights ``(m,)`` used to
    weight each point-to-plane residual.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from mlsgfx_recon.common import (  # noqa: E402
    chamfer,
    make_fragment_pair,
    print_test_metrics,
    print_train_metrics,
    rot_err_deg,
    seed_everything,
    trans_err,
)

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE THIS LINE
# =============================================================================

# ----- BEGIN EDITABLE REGION -----
def correspondence_weights(src_matched, tgt_matched, tgt_normals, distances,
                           iteration):
    """Uniform weights (plain ICP, no outlier handling)."""
    return np.ones(src_matched.shape[0])
# ----- END EDITABLE REGION -----

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — the ICP loop and evaluation below
# =============================================================================

SETTINGS = {
    "bunny_easy":   {"mesh": "bunny.obj",     "angle": 10, "trans": [0.05, 0.02, 0.03], "noise": 0.002, "outliers": 0.02},
    "bunny_hard":   {"mesh": "bunny.obj",     "angle": 30, "trans": [0.1, 0.05, 0.08],  "noise": 0.004, "outliers": 0.05},
    "armadillo":    {"mesh": "armadillo.obj", "angle": 30, "trans": [0.1, 0.05, 0.08],  "noise": 0.003, "outliers": 0.04},
    "spot_noisy":   {"mesh": "spot.obj",      "angle": 45, "trans": [0.12, 0.06, 0.1],  "noise": 0.006, "outliers": 0.08},
}


def estimate_normals(pts, k=20):
    from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
    tree = cKDTree(pts)
    nrm = np.zeros_like(pts)
    for i in range(pts.shape[0]):
        _, idx = tree.query(pts[i], k=k)
        nb = pts[idx]
        cov = np.cov((nb - nb.mean(0)).T)
        w, v = np.linalg.eigh(cov)
        nrm[i] = v[:, 0]
    return nrm


def icp(src, tgt, tgt_nrm, max_iter=30):
    """Point-to-plane ICP with a swappable correspondence-weighting kernel."""
    from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
    R = np.eye(3)
    t = np.zeros(3)
    tree = cKDTree(tgt)
    for it in range(max_iter):
        src_t = src @ R.T + t
        dist, idx = tree.query(src_t, k=1)
        tgt_m = tgt[idx]
        nrm_m = tgt_nrm[idx]
        w = np.asarray(correspondence_weights(src_t, tgt_m, nrm_m, dist, it),
                       dtype=np.float64)
        w = np.maximum(w, 0.0)
        if w.sum() < 1e-12:
            w = np.ones_like(w)
        w = w / w.sum()
        # weighted point-to-plane Gauss-Newton
        A = np.cross(src_t, nrm_m)
        b = np.sum((tgt_m - src_t) * nrm_m, axis=1)
        M = np.concatenate([A, nrm_m], axis=1)
        W = np.sqrt(w)[:, None]
        Mw = M * W
        bw = b * np.sqrt(w)
        try:
            d, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Mw, bw, rcond=None)
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            break
        drot, dtrans = d[:3], d[3:]
        # apply the incremental rotation (Rodrigues) + translation
        ang = np.linalg.norm(drot)
        if ang > 1e-12:
            ax = drot / ang
            K = np.array([[0, -ax[2], ax[1]], [ax[2], 0, -ax[0]], [-ax[1], ax[0], 0]])
            dR = np.eye(3) + np.sin(ang) * K + (1 - np.cos(ang)) * K @ K
        else:
            dR = np.eye(3)
        R = dR @ R
        t = dR @ t + dtrans
    return R, t


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--setting", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", type=str, default="/tmp/output")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cfg = SETTINGS[args.setting]
    rng = seed_everything(args.seed)

    src, tgt, R_true, t_true = make_fragment_pair(
        cfg["mesh"], 4000, cfg["angle"], cfg["trans"], rng,
        noise=cfg["noise"], overlap=0.8)
    # add outliers to the target
    n_out = int(cfg["outliers"] * tgt.shape[0])
    if n_out > 0:
        lo, hi = tgt.min(0), tgt.max(0)
        out = rng.uniform(lo, hi, (n_out, 3))
        tgt = np.vstack([tgt, out])
    print_train_metrics(setting=args.setting, n_src=src.shape[0], n_tgt=tgt.shape[0])

    tgt_nrm = estimate_normals(tgt, k=20)
    R_est, t_est = icp(src, tgt, tgt_nrm)

    src_aligned = src @ R_est.T + t_est
    re = rot_err_deg(R_est, R_true)
    te = trans_err(t_est, t_true)
    ch = chamfer(src_aligned, tgt)
    success = 1.0 if re < 2.0 else 0.0

    print_train_metrics(rot_err=re, trans_err=te)
    print_test_metrics(
        rot_err=re,
        trans_err=te,
        chamfer=ch,
        success=success,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

tukey.content:
def correspondence_weights(src_matched, tgt_matched, tgt_normals, distances,
                           iteration):
    """Tukey biweight on the matched distance."""
    med = max(float(np.median(distances)), 1e-12)
    c = 4.685 * med
    u = np.clip(distances / c, -1.0, 1.0)
    return (1.0 - u ** 2) ** 2 * (np.abs(u) < 1.0)

plane_angle.content:
def correspondence_weights(src_matched, tgt_matched, tgt_normals, distances,
                           iteration):
    """Normal-compatibility + distance weighting."""
    # the source normal is approximated by the matched target normal under the
    # current transform; use the distance and the normal consistency of the
    # residual direction
    resid = tgt_matched - src_matched
    rn = np.linalg.norm(resid, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    rn = np.maximum(rn, 1e-12)
    cos_align = np.abs(np.sum(resid / rn * tgt_normals, axis=1))
    w_normal = np.clip(cos_align / 0.5, 0.0, 1.0)
    med = max(float(np.median(distances)), 1e-12)
    w_dist = 1.0 / (1.0 + (distances / (2.0 * med)) ** 2)
    return w_normal * w_dist

# Normal Orientation of an Unoriented Point Cloud

## Research Question

A scanned point cloud has per-point normals whose signs are arbitrary. Orienting
them consistently — all outward — is a prerequisite for Poisson reconstruction,
rendering and most geometry processing. The orientation is a global propagation
problem that local estimators get wrong at thin features. Which propagation rule
recovers the most consistent orientation?

## Background

* Hoppe, H., DeRose, T., Duchamp, T., McDonald, J., Stuetzle, W. *Surface
  Reconstruction from Unorganized Points*, SIGGRAPH 1992 — the orientability-
  weighted MST propagation.
* Metzer, G., Hanocka, R., Zorin, D., Giryes, R., Cohen-Or, D., Barnes, C.,
  Barenboim, A. *Orienting Point Clouds with Dipole Propagation*, ACM TOG 40(4)
  (SIGGRAPH 2021).
* Schall, O., Samozino, M. *Shape from Point Clouds: Learning without a Teacher*,
  CVPR 2021 — the learning-based end.

## What You Can Modify

`open3d-recon-lab/mlsgfx_recon/custom_orient.py`, lines 38–48 only.

```python
def orient_normals(pts: np.ndarray, raw_normals: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """(n,3) points + (n,3) arbitrarily-signed normals -> (n,3) consistent."""
```

You may add helper functions inside the region and use `numpy`, `scipy`, `open3d`.

## Fixed Pipeline

* Each setting samples a closed mesh uniformly, computes per-point normals by local
  PCA (16 neighbours), and randomly flips 50% of them.
* Scoring: the fraction of normals agreeing with the mesh's ground-truth outward
  normal (up to a global flip), and the chamfer distance of a screened-Poisson
  reconstruction built from the oriented cloud.

## Evaluation Scenarios

| setting | mesh | points |
|---|---|---|
| `spot` | spot | 8000 |
| `armadillo` | armadillo | 15000 |
| `nefertiti` | nefertiti | 15000 |
| `bunny` | held out | 15000 |

## Baselines

* **`centroid`** — orient every normal away from the cloud centroid.
* **`mst_propagate`** — orientability-weighted MST + sign propagation (Hoppe et al.
  1992).
* **`bfs_knn`** — BFS sign propagation over the kNN graph.

## Metric

Per setting: `consistency` (higher better) and `recon_chamfer` (lower better). The
setting score is a weighted mean of the two normalised terms; the task score is the
geometric mean over the four settings.

"""Normal orientation of an unoriented point cloud — editable scaffold.

The normals of a point cloud are computed by local PCA and then randomly flipped,
so half point the wrong way.  The algorithm must make them globally consistent.
Only the orientation step is under study.

Interface contract
------------------
``orient_normals(pts, raw_normals) -> (n, 3)``
    ``pts`` float64 ``(n,3)``, ``raw_normals`` float64 ``(n,3)`` (each up to a
    random sign).  Return the oriented normals, unit length, consistently
    outward/pointing the same way.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from mlsgfx_recon.common import (  # noqa: E402
    chamfer,
    load_mesh_points,
    print_test_metrics,
    print_train_metrics,
    seed_everything,
)

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE THIS LINE
# =============================================================================

# ----- BEGIN EDITABLE REGION -----
def orient_normals(pts: np.ndarray, raw_normals: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Flip every normal toward the cloud centroid's outward direction.

    The simplest heuristic: orient each normal away from the centroid of the
    point cloud (correct only for convex shapes).
    """
    c = pts.mean(axis=0)
    out = pts - c
    sign = np.sign(np.sum(raw_normals * out, axis=1, keepdims=True))
    sign = np.where(sign == 0, 1.0, sign)
    return raw_normals * sign
# ----- END EDITABLE REGION -----

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — GT normals and evaluation below
# =============================================================================

SETTINGS = {
    "spot":       {"mesh": "spot.obj",       "n": 8000},
    "armadillo":  {"mesh": "armadillo.obj",  "n": 15000},
    "nefertiti":  {"mesh": "nefertiti.obj",  "n": 15000},
    "bunny":      {"mesh": "bunny.obj",      "n": 15000},
}


def pca_normals(pts, k=16):
    from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
    tree = cKDTree(pts)
    nrm = np.zeros_like(pts)
    for i in range(pts.shape[0]):
        _, idx = tree.query(pts[i], k=k)
        nb = pts[idx]
        cov = np.cov((nb - nb.mean(0)).T)
        w, v = np.linalg.eigh(cov)
        nrm[i] = v[:, 0]
    nrm /= np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(nrm, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-18)
    return nrm


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--setting", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", type=str, default="/tmp/output")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cfg = SETTINGS[args.setting]
    rng = seed_everything(args.seed)

    pts, nrm_gt = load_mesh_points(cfg["mesh"], cfg["n"], rng)
    raw = pca_normals(pts, k=16)
    # randomly flip half
    flip = rng.random(pts.shape[0]) < 0.5
    raw[flip] *= -1.0
    print_train_metrics(setting=args.setting, n=pts.shape[0])

    est = np.asarray(orient_normals(pts.copy(), raw.copy()), dtype=np.float64)
    if est.shape != raw.shape:
        print(f"ERROR: orient_normals returned {est.shape}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(3)
    est_norm = np.linalg.norm(est, axis=1)
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(est_norm)) or np.mean(est_norm > 1e-6) < 0.99:
        print("ERROR: orient_normals returned degenerate (near-zero/non-finite) normals", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(3)
    est = est / np.maximum(est_norm[:, None], 1e-18)

    # consistency vs the mesh GT normals (sign matters up to a global flip)
    cos = np.sum(est * nrm_gt, axis=1)
    frac_pos = float((cos > 0).mean())
    consistency = max(frac_pos, 1.0 - frac_pos)

    # reconstruction quality: reconstruct with screened Poisson using the oriented
    # normals, measure chamfer to the GT point cloud
    import open3d as o3d
    pcd = o3d.geometry.PointCloud()
    pcd.points = o3d.utility.Vector3dVector(pts)
    pcd.normals = o3d.utility.Vector3dVector(est)
    recon_chamfer = float("nan")
    try:
        mesh, _ = o3d.geometry.TriangleMesh.create_from_point_cloud_poisson(
            pcd, depth=7, scale=1.1)
        mesh = mesh.remove_duplicated_vertices()
        rp = np.asarray(mesh.sample_points_uniformly(20000).points)
        recon_chamfer = chamfer(rp, pts)
    except Exception as e:
        print_train_metrics(poisson_failed=str(e)[:60])

    print_test_metrics(
        consistency=consistency,
        recon_chamfer=recon_chamfer,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def orient_normals(pts: np.ndarray, raw_normals: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Radial from the centroid."""
    c = pts.mean(axis=0)
    out = pts - c
    sign = np.sign(np.sum(raw_normals * out, axis=1, keepdims=True))
    sign = np.where(sign == 0, 1.0, sign)

mst_propagate.content:
def orient_normals(pts: np.ndarray, raw_normals: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """MST + sign propagation (Hoppe et al. 1992)."""
    from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
    from scipy.sparse.csgraph import minimum_spanning_tree, connected_components

    n = pts.shape[0]
    tree = cKDTree(pts)
    # kNN graph for the candidate edges
    k = 12
    _, idx = tree.query(pts, k=k + 1)
    rows, cols, wts = [], [], []
    for i in range(n):
        for j in idx[i, 1:]:
            w = 1.0 - abs(float(np.dot(raw_normals[i], raw_normals[j])))
            rows.append(i); cols.append(j); wts.append(w)
    import scipy.sparse as sp
    G = sp.coo_matrix((wts, (rows, cols)), shape=(n, n)).tocsr()
    mst = minimum_spanning_tree(G).tocoo()

    # BFS over the MST from the point farthest from the centroid
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for a, b in zip(mst.row, mst.col):
        adj[int(a)].append(int(b))
        adj[int(b)].append(int(a))
    start = int(np.argmax(np.linalg.norm(pts - pts.mean(0), axis=1)))
    sign = np.ones(n)
    # orient the start outward
    out_dir = pts[start] - pts.mean(0)
    if np.dot(raw_normals[start], out_dir) < 0:
        sign[start] = -1.0
    seen = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    stack = [start]
    seen[start] = True
    while stack:
        u = stack.pop()
        for v in adj[u]:
            if seen[v]:
                continue
            # make v agree with u
            d = float(np.dot(raw_normals[v], raw_normals[u]))
            sign[v] = sign[u] * (1.0 if d > 0 else -1.0)
            seen[v] = True
            stack.append(v)
    return raw_normals * sign[:, None]

def orient_normals(pts: np.ndarray, raw_normals: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """BFS sign propagation over the kNN graph."""
    from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

    n = pts.shape[0]
    tree = cKDTree(pts)
    _, idx = tree.query(pts, k=13)
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in idx[i, 1:]:
            adj[i].append(int(j))
            adj[int(j)].append(i)
    sign = np.ones(n)
    seen = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    start = int(np.argmax(np.linalg.norm(pts - pts.mean(0), axis=1)))
    out_dir = pts[start] - pts.mean(0)
    if np.dot(raw_normals[start], out_dir) < 0:
        sign[start] = -1.0
    stack = [start]
    seen[start] = True
    while stack:
        u = stack.pop()
        for v in adj[u]:
            if seen[v]:
                continue
            d = float(np.dot(raw_normals[v], raw_normals[u]))
            sign[v] = sign[u] * (1.0 if d > 0 else -1.0)
            seen[v] = True
            stack.append(v)
    return raw_normals * sign[:, None]

# Outlier Removal for Scanned Point Clouds

## Research Question

Real scans contain off-surface outliers that corrupt every downstream step. Removing
them without sacrificing real surface points is a density-estimation problem. Which
cleaning rule best separates outliers from the true surface?

## Background

* Rusu, R. B., Marton, Z. C., Blodow, N., Dolha, M., Beetz, M. *Towards 3D Point
  Cloud Based Object Maps for Household Environments*, Robot. Auton. Syst. 56(11),
  2008 — the statistical outlier filter.
* Breunig, M. M., Kriegel, H.-P., Ng, R. T., Sander, J. *LOF: Identifying
  Density-Based Local Outliers*, SIGMOD 2000 — the local outlier factor.
* Carr, J. C., Beatson, R. K., Cherrie, J. B., Mitchell, T. J., Fright, W. R.,
  McCallum, B. C., Evans, T. R. *Reconstruction and Representation of 3D Objects
  with Radial Basis Functions*, SIGGRAPH 2001 — the downstream motivation.

## What You Can Modify

`open3d-recon-lab/mlsgfx_recon/custom_outlier.py`, lines 36–43 only.

```python
def clean(pts: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """(n,3) corrupted cloud -> boolean keep mask."""
```

You may add helper functions inside the region and use `numpy`, `scipy`, `sklearn`,
`open3d`.

## Fixed Pipeline

* Each setting samples a mesh, adds Gaussian surface noise, mixes in uniform
  outliers in the bounding box, and shuffles.
* Scoring: precision/recall of the outlier flags against the known clean points,
  and the chamfer distance between the cleaned cloud and the clean cloud.

## Evaluation Scenarios

| setting | mesh | outliers | noise |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spot` | spot | 3% | 0.002 |
| `armadillo` | armadillo | 4% | 0.003 |
| `fandisk` | fandisk | 3% | 0.002 |
| `lucy` | held out | 5% | 0.003 |

## Baselines

* **`radius`** — drop points with fewer than 4 neighbours within a 2% ball.
* **`statistical`** — kNN mean distance beyond global mean + 2σ (Rusu et al. 2008).
* **`lof`** — local outlier factor, k = 20 (Breunig et al. 2000).
* **`bilateral_sor`** — density-adaptive statistical removal.

## Metric

Per setting: `precision` and `recall` (higher better) and `chamfer` (lower better).
The setting score is a weighted mean of the three normalised terms (1.0 / 1.0 /
0.8); the task score is the geometric mean over the four settings.

files.content:
"""Outlier removal for a scanned point cloud — editable scaffold.

A clean mesh is sampled and corrupted with uniform outliers and surface noise.
The algorithm must flag and remove the outliers while keeping the real surface
points.  Only the cleaning rule is under study.

Interface contract
------------------
``clean(pts) -> keep_mask``
    ``pts`` float64 ``(n,3)``.  Return a boolean ``(n,)`` mask: True = keep.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

sys.path.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from mlsgfx_recon.common import (  # noqa: E402
    chamfer,
    load_mesh_points,
    print_test_metrics,
    print_train_metrics,
    seed_everything,
)

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — DO NOT MODIFY ABOVE THIS LINE
# =============================================================================

# ----- BEGIN EDITABLE REGION -----
def clean(pts: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Radius-based removal: drop points with too few neighbours within a ball."""
    from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
    tree = cKDTree(pts)
    diag = float(np.linalg.norm(pts.max(0) - pts.min(0)))
    r = 0.02 * diag
    counts = tree.query_ball_point(pts, r, return_length=True)
    return counts >= 4
# ----- END EDITABLE REGION -----

# =============================================================================
# FIXED — corruption and evaluation below
# =============================================================================

SETTINGS = {
    "spot":       {"mesh": "spot.obj",      "n": 8000,  "outlier": 0.03, "noise": 0.002},
    "armadillo":  {"mesh": "armadillo.obj", "n": 15000, "outlier": 0.04, "noise": 0.003},
    "fandisk":    {"mesh": "fandisk.obj",   "n": 12000, "outlier": 0.03, "noise": 0.002},
    "lucy":       {"mesh": "lucy.obj",      "n": 15000, "outlier": 0.05, "noise": 0.003},
}


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    ap.add_argument("--setting", type=str, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--output-dir", type=str, default="/tmp/output")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cfg = SETTINGS[args.setting]
    rng = seed_everything(args.seed)

    clean_pts, _ = load_mesh_points(cfg["mesh"], cfg["n"], rng)
    # noise on the surface
    pts = clean_pts + rng.normal(0.0, cfg["noise"], clean_pts.shape)
    # uniform outliers in the bounding box
    n_out = int(cfg["outlier"] * pts.shape[0])
    lo, hi = pts.min(0), pts.max(0)
    pad = 0.1 * (hi - lo)
    outliers = rng.uniform(lo - pad, hi + pad, (n_out, 3))
    noisy = np.vstack([pts, outliers])
    gt_keep = np.zeros(noisy.shape[0], dtype=bool)
    gt_keep[: pts.shape[0]] = True
    # shuffle rows and their ground-truth labels together so gt_keep still
    # tracks each row's clean/outlier identity after reordering
    perm = rng.permutation(noisy.shape[0])
    noisy = noisy[perm]
    gt_keep = gt_keep[perm]
    print_train_metrics(setting=args.setting, n=noisy.shape[0], n_out=n_out)

    keep = np.asarray(clean(noisy.copy()), dtype=bool).reshape(-1)
    if keep.shape[0] != noisy.shape[0]:
        print(f"ERROR: clean returned mask of {keep.shape[0]}, expected {noisy.shape[0]}",
              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        raise SystemExit(3)

    tp = float(((keep) & (gt_keep)).sum())
    fp = float(((keep) & (~gt_keep)).sum())
    fn = float(((~keep) & (gt_keep)).sum())
    precision = tp / max(tp + fp, 1.0)
    recall = tp / max(tp + fn, 1.0)
    cham = chamfer(noisy[keep], clean_pts)

    print_test_metrics(
        precision=precision,
        recall=recall,
        chamfer=cham,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

statistical.content:
def clean(pts: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Statistical removal: mean kNN distance beyond global mean + 2 std is an
    outlier."""
    from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
    tree = cKDTree(pts)
    dist, _ = tree.query(pts, k=16 + 1)
    md = dist[:, 1:].mean(axis=1)
    mu, sd = md.mean(), md.std()
    return md < (mu + 2.0 * sd)

def clean(pts: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Local Outlier Factor (k=20) removal."""
    from sklearn.neighbors import LocalOutlierFactor
    clf = LocalOutlierFactor(n_neighbors=20, contamination="auto")
    keep = clf.fit_predict(pts) == 1
    return keep

bilateral_sor.content:
def clean(pts: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Density-adaptive statistical removal."""
    from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
    tree = cKDTree(pts)
    dist, _ = tree.query(pts, k=16 + 1)
    md = dist[:, 1:].mean(axis=1)
    # local scale: the 25th-percentile mean distance in the neighbourhood
    local_scale = np.percentile(md, 25)
    thr = 2.5 * local_scale
    return md < thr

tasks.description_md:
# Coarse Global Registration of Point-Cloud Fragments

## Research Question

When two fragments are related by a large rigid transform, local ICP falls into a
local minimum unless a good coarse alignment is provided. The coarse method —
feature matching, outlier rejection, the transform estimate — decides whether the
pipeline finds the global alignment. Which coarse registration initialises ICP best?

## Background

* Rusu, R. B., Blodow, N., Beetz, M. *Fast Point Feature Histograms (FPFH) for 3D
  Registration*, ICRA 2009 — the feature used by every baseline here.
* Fischler, M. A., Bolles, R. C. *Random Sample Consensus*, CACM 24(6), 1981 —
  RANSAC transform estimation.
* Zhou, Q.-Y., Park, J., Koltun, V. *Fast Global Registration*, ECCV 2016 — the
  line-process alternative to RANSAC.
* Leordeanu, M., Hebert, M. *A Spectral Technique for Correspondence Problems
  using Pairwise Constraints*, ICCV 2005 — the spectral matcher.
* Yang, H., Shi, J., Carlone, L. *TEASER: Fast and Certifiable Point Cloud
  Registration*, T-RO 2021 — the certifiable end of the spectrum.

## What You Can Modify

`open3d-recon-lab/mlsgfx_recon/custom_register.py`, lines 42–90 only.

```python
def register_coarse(src, tgt, fpfh_src, fpfh_tgt) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Point clouds (n,3) + FPFH features (n,33) -> (R (3,3), t (3,))."""
```

The driver then refines your estimate with a fixed short point-to-plane ICP (15
iterations, 70% inlier cutoff) and scores the final transform. You may add helper
functions inside the region and use `numpy`, `scipy`, `open3d`.

## Fixed Pipeline

* Each setting samples two partial views of a mesh (80% overlap) with Gaussian
  surface noise, applies a large rigid transform (90–120° + a translation), and
  asks for a coarse alignment from scratch.
* Scoring compares the post-refinement transform to the known ground truth.

## Evaluation Scenarios

| setting | mesh | transform |
|---|---|---|
| `bunny_45` | bunny | 90° + 0.6 |
| `bunny_60` | bunny | 120° + 0.6 |
| `armadillo_45` | armadillo | 90° + 0.5 |
| `spot_60` | held out | 120° + 0.5 |

## Baselines

* **`identity`** — no coarse alignment (ICP from scratch).
* **`ransac_fpfh`** — RANSAC over FPFH mutual correspondences.
* **`fast_gr`** — Geman-McClure line-process minimisation over FPFH matches
  (Zhou et al. 2016).
* **`spectral`** — spectral correspondence via the pairwise-compatibility matrix
  (Leordeanu & Hebert 2005).

## Metric

Per setting: `rot_err` (degrees, lower better), `trans_err` (relative, lower
better), `chamfer` (lower better), `success` (rot_err < 2°, higher better). The
setting score is a weighted mean of the four normalised terms; the task score is
the geometric mean over the four settings.
