# =====================================================================
# FIXED: training loop and evaluation
# =====================================================================
def _causal_lr_lambda(step: int, warmup: int, total: int) -> float:
    if step < warmup:
        return float(step + 1) / float(max(1, warmup))
    remaining = max(0, total - step)
    return remaining / float(max(1, total - warmup))


def train_model(
    model: nn.Module,
    config: TaskConfig,
    device: torch.device,
    train_seed: int,
) -> None:
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        model.parameters(),
        lr=config.lr,
        betas=(0.9, 0.999),
        weight_decay=config.weight_decay,
    )
    scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR(
        optimizer,
        lr_lambda=lambda step: _causal_lr_lambda(
            step, config.warmup_steps, config.max_steps
        ),
    )
    data_generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(train_seed)
    model.train()
    running_loss = 0.0
    running_acc = 0.0
    running_count = 0
    t0 = time.time()
    for step in range(1, config.max_steps + 1):
        tokens = sample_ffl_batch(
            batch_size=config.batch_size,
            seq_len=config.train_len,
            pi=config.train_pi,
            generator=data_generator,
        ).to(device)
        inp = tokens[:, :-1]
        tgt = tokens[:, 1:]
        logits = model(inp)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(
            logits.reshape(-1, VOCAB_SIZE),
            tgt.reshape(-1),
        )
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss.backward()
        if config.grad_clip > 0:
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), config.grad_clip)
        optimizer.step()
        scheduler.step()

        with torch.no_grad():
            read_logits = logits[..., [TOK_R0, TOK_R1]]
            read_preds = read_logits.argmax(dim=-1)
            target_bits = (tgt == TOK_R1).long()
            mask = read_mask(tgt)
            if mask.any():
                read_correct = ((read_preds == target_bits) & mask).sum().item()
                read_total = mask.sum().item()
            else:
                read_correct = 0
                read_total = 0
            running_loss += float(loss.item())
            running_acc += read_correct
            running_count += read_total
        if step == 1 or step % config.log_interval == 0 or step == config.max_steps:
            denom = max(1, running_count)
            avg_loss = running_loss / max(1, min(step, config.log_interval))
            avg_acc = running_acc / denom if denom > 0 else 0.0
            elapsed = time.time() - t0
            print(
                "TRAIN_METRICS "
                f"step={step} loss={avg_loss:.6f} read_acc={avg_acc:.6f} "
                f"reads_in_window={running_count} elapsed_s={elapsed:.1f}",
                flush=True,
            )
            running_loss = 0.0
            running_acc = 0.0
            running_count = 0


@torch.no_grad()
def evaluate_split(
    model: nn.Module,
    pi: float,
    seq_len: int,
    num_sequences: int,
    block_size: int,
    device: torch.device,
    eval_seed: int,
    eval_batch: int = 256,
) -> EvalReport:
    """Grade read-bit predictions per Liu et al. (NeurIPS 2023).

    At every read position we restrict the softmax to the two read tokens
    (r0 vs r1) and compare to the target bit. Besides the per-read and
    per-sequence error rates, reads are grouped — across the whole split,
    in generation order — into blocks of `block_size`; a block is an error
    if any read inside it is wrong. The headline score is
    1 - block_error_rate.
    """
    model.eval()
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(eval_seed)
    num_errors = 0
    num_reads = 0
    seq_with_error = 0
    total_seq = 0
    correct_bits: list[torch.Tensor] = []
    remaining = num_sequences
    while remaining > 0:
        b = min(eval_batch, remaining)
        tokens = sample_ffl_batch(
            batch_size=b,
            seq_len=seq_len,
            pi=pi,
            generator=generator,
        ).to(device)
        inp = tokens[:, :-1]
        tgt = tokens[:, 1:]
        logits = model(inp)
        read_logits = logits[..., [TOK_R0, TOK_R1]]
        read_preds = read_logits.argmax(dim=-1)
        target_bits = (tgt == TOK_R1).long()
        mask = read_mask(tgt)
        errors = mask & (read_preds != target_bits)
        num_errors += int(errors.sum().item())
        num_reads += int(mask.sum().item())
        per_seq_errors = errors.sum(dim=1)
        seq_with_error += int((per_seq_errors > 0).sum().item())
        total_seq += b
        remaining -= b
        # Ordered per-read correctness bits for block grouping.
        ok = (~errors)[mask]  # flattened row-major: sequence by sequence
        correct_bits.append(ok.cpu())
    all_ok = torch.cat(correct_bits) if correct_bits else torch.zeros(0, dtype=torch.bool)
    # Diagnostic: block error rate at candidate granularities (the headline
    # score uses only `block_size`; this line supports recalibration).
    _sweep = []
    for _bs in (16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024):
        _nb = int(all_ok.numel() // _bs)
        if _nb > 0:
            _blk = all_ok[: _nb * _bs].reshape(_nb, _bs)
            _sweep.append(f"b{_bs}={float((~_blk.all(dim=1)).sum().item()) / _nb:.6f}")
    print("BLOCK_SWEEP " + " ".join(_sweep), flush=True)
    n_blocks = int(all_ok.numel() // block_size)
    blocks_with_error = 0
    if n_blocks > 0:
        blocks = all_ok[: n_blocks * block_size].reshape(n_blocks, block_size)
        blocks_with_error = int((~blocks.all(dim=1)).sum().item())
    return EvalReport(
        pi=pi,
        seq_len=seq_len,
        num_sequences=total_seq,
        num_reads=num_reads,
        num_errors=num_errors,
        seq_with_error=seq_with_error,
        num_blocks=n_blocks,
        blocks_with_error=blocks_with_error,
    )


def resolve_device(device_arg: str) -> torch.device:
    if device_arg == "cpu":
        return torch.device("cpu")
    if device_arg == "cuda":
        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but no GPU is available.")
        return torch.device("cuda")
    return torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")


def run_benchmark(
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
    device: torch.device,
    eval_pi: float,
    eval_len: int,
    eval_num_sequences: int,
    eval_batch: int,
    block_size: int,
    label: str,
) -> dict:
    set_global_seed(seed)
    print(
        "TASK_CONFIG "
        f"label={label} train_len={config.train_len} train_pi={config.train_pi} "
        f"eval_len={eval_len} eval_pi={eval_pi} max_steps={config.max_steps} "
        f"batch_size={config.batch_size} eval_batch={eval_batch} "
        f"block_size={block_size} lr={config.lr} wd={config.weight_decay}",
        flush=True,
    )
    model = build_model(config).to(device)
    n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
    print(f"MODEL_INFO num_params={n_params}", flush=True)
    if n_params > 50_000_000:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Model has {n_params} > 50M parameters.")

    # Parallel-time guards (measured on the actual model instance).
    check_no_recurrent_modules(model)
    check_serial_depth(model, config, device)
    check_init_tripwire(model, config, device)

    train_model(model, config, device, train_seed=seed * 9973 + 1)

    report = evaluate_split(
        model=model,
        pi=eval_pi,
        seq_len=eval_len,
        num_sequences=eval_num_sequences,
        block_size=block_size,
        device=device,
        eval_seed=seed * 7919 + 11,
        eval_batch=eval_batch,
    )
    score = max(0.0, 1.0 - report.block_error_rate)
    metrics = {
        "read_error_rate": report.read_error_rate,
        "seq_error_rate": report.seq_error_rate,
        "block_error_rate": report.block_error_rate,
        "score": score,
        "num_reads": float(report.num_reads),
        "num_blocks": float(report.num_blocks),
        "num_sequences": float(report.num_sequences),
        "num_params": float(n_params),
    }
    print(
        "FINAL_METRICS "
        + " ".join(
            f"{key}={value:.6f}" if isinstance(value, float) else f"{key}={value}"
            for key, value in metrics.items()
        ),
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        f"TEST_METRICS read_error_rate={metrics['read_error_rate']:.8f} "
        f"seq_error_rate={metrics['seq_error_rate']:.8f} "
        f"block_error_rate={metrics['block_error_rate']:.8f} "
        f"score={metrics['score']:.6f}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return metrics


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run the theory-flip-flop task.")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--label", type=str, default="mid")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--device",
        choices=("auto", "cpu", "cuda"),
        default="auto",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--split",
        choices=("mid", "sparse", "long_ctx"),
        default="mid",
        help="Which OOD evaluation split to grade against.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=None)
    return parser.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    config = DEFAULT_TASK
    if args.max_steps is not None:
        config = replace(config, max_steps=args.max_steps)
    if args.batch_size is not None:
        config = replace(config, batch_size=args.batch_size)

    if args.split == "mid":
        eval_pi = config.eval_mid_pi
        eval_len = config.eval_mid_len
        eval_num = config.eval_mid_num_sequences
        eval_batch = 128
        block_size = config.block_size_mid
    elif args.split == "sparse":
        eval_pi = config.eval_pi_sparse
        eval_len = config.eval_len
        eval_num = config.eval_sparse_num_sequences
        eval_batch = 512
        block_size = config.block_size_sparse
    else:  # long_ctx
        eval_pi = config.eval_long_pi
        eval_len = config.eval_long_len
        eval_num = config.eval_long_num_sequences
        # Long-context attention has a large activation footprint (manual
        # implementations materialise T x T scores); keep this batch modest.
        eval_batch = 16
        block_size = config.block_size_long

    device = resolve_device(args.device)
    metrics = run_benchmark(
        config=config,
        seed=args.seed,
        device=device,
        eval_pi=eval_pi,
        eval_len=eval_len,
        eval_num_sequences=eval_num,
        eval_batch=eval_batch,
        block_size=block_size,
        label=args.label,
    )

    if args.output_dir is not None:
        args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        output_path = args.output_dir / f"{args.label}_seed{args.seed}.json"
        output_path.write_text(json.dumps({"config": asdict(config), "metrics": metrics}, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

class _AlibiAttention(nn.Module):
    """Causal MHA with fixed per-head ALiBi slopes; slope 0 = global head."""

    def __init__(self, d_model: int, slopes: tuple):
        super().__init__()
        n_heads = len(slopes)
        assert d_model % n_heads == 0
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.head_dim = d_model // n_heads
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(d_model, 3 * d_model, bias=False)
        self.out = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model, bias=False)
        self.register_buffer(
            "slopes", torch.tensor(slopes, dtype=torch.float32), persistent=False
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, T, D = x.shape
        qkv = self.qkv(x).view(B, T, 3, self.n_heads, self.head_dim)
        q, k, v = qkv.unbind(dim=2)
        q = q.transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.transpose(1, 2)
        scores = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-1, -2)) / math.sqrt(self.head_dim)
        pos = torch.arange(T, device=x.device)
        dist = (pos.view(1, T, 1) - pos.view(1, 1, T)).clamp_min(0).float()
        bias = -self.slopes.view(self.n_heads, 1, 1) * dist  # [H, T, T]
        scores = scores + bias.unsqueeze(0)
        causal = torch.ones(T, T, device=x.device, dtype=torch.bool).tril()
        scores = scores.masked_fill(~causal, float("-inf"))
        attn = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        out = torch.matmul(attn, v)
        out = out.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, T, D)
        return self.out(out)


class _AlibiBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, slopes: tuple):
        super().__init__()
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.attn = _AlibiAttention(d_model, slopes)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_model, 4 * d_model),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(4 * d_model, d_model),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = x + self.attn(self.ln1(x))
        x = x + self.mlp(self.ln2(x))
        return x


class FlipFlopModel(nn.Module):
    """NoPE Transformer with canonical ALiBi slopes (Press et al. 2022)."""

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = VOCAB_SIZE, max_len: int = 2048):
        super().__init__()
        d_model = 512
        n_layers = 6
        slopes = tuple(2.0 ** -(i + 1) for i in range(8))
        self.max_len = max_len
        self.tok = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            [_AlibiBlock(d_model, slopes) for _ in range(n_layers)]
        )
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        h = self.tok(tokens)
        for block in self.blocks:
            h = block(h)
        h = self.norm(h)
        return self.head(h)


def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    return FlipFlopModel(
        vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE,
        max_len=max(config.train_len, config.eval_long_len, config.depth_probe_long),
    )

class _SharpCausalAttention(nn.Module):
    """Multi-head causal self-attention with a sharpening temperature."""

    def __init__(self, d_model: int, n_heads: int, tau: float = 0.5):
        super().__init__()
        assert d_model % n_heads == 0
        self.n_heads = n_heads
        self.head_dim = d_model // n_heads
        self.tau = tau
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(d_model, 3 * d_model, bias=False)
        self.out = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, T, D = x.shape
        qkv = self.qkv(x).view(B, T, 3, self.n_heads, self.head_dim)
        q, k, v = qkv.unbind(dim=2)
        q = q.transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.transpose(1, 2)
        scores = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-1, -2))
        scores = scores / (math.sqrt(self.head_dim) * self.tau)
        causal = torch.ones(T, T, device=x.device, dtype=torch.bool).tril()
        scores = scores.masked_fill(~causal, float("-inf"))
        attn = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        out = torch.matmul(attn, v)
        out = out.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, T, D)
        return self.out(out)


class _SharpBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, n_heads: int, tau: float):
        super().__init__()
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.attn = _SharpCausalAttention(d_model, n_heads, tau)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_model, 4 * d_model),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(4 * d_model, d_model),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = x + self.attn(self.ln1(x))
        x = x + self.mlp(self.ln2(x))
        return x


class FlipFlopModel(nn.Module):
    """Transformer with sharpened (tau = 0.5) attention logits."""

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = VOCAB_SIZE, max_len: int = 2048,
                 tau: float = 0.5):
        super().__init__()
        d_model = 512
        n_layers = 6
        n_heads = 8
        self.tok = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.pos = nn.Embedding(max_len, d_model)
        self.max_len = max_len
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            [_SharpBlock(d_model, n_heads, tau) for _ in range(n_layers)]
        )
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        bsz, seq_len = tokens.shape
        pos_ids = torch.arange(seq_len, device=tokens.device).unsqueeze(0)
        h = self.tok(tokens) + self.pos(pos_ids)
        for block in self.blocks:
            h = block(h)
        h = self.norm(h)
        return self.head(h)


def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    return FlipFlopModel(
        vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE,
        max_len=max(config.train_len, config.eval_long_len, config.depth_probe_long),
    )

class FlipFlopModel(nn.Module):
    """Causal Transformer (vanilla, learned APE) — Liu et al. baseline."""

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = VOCAB_SIZE, max_len: int = 2048):
        super().__init__()
        d_model = 512
        n_layers = 6
        n_heads = 8
        self.tok = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.pos = nn.Embedding(max_len, d_model)
        self.max_len = max_len
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=d_model,
            nhead=n_heads,
            dim_feedforward=4 * d_model,
            dropout=0.0,
            batch_first=True,
            activation="gelu",
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=n_layers)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        bsz, seq_len = tokens.shape
        if seq_len > self.max_len:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Sequence length {seq_len} exceeds model max_len {self.max_len}."
            )
        pos_ids = torch.arange(seq_len, device=tokens.device).unsqueeze(0)
        h = self.tok(tokens) + self.pos(pos_ids)
        causal = torch.triu(
            torch.ones(seq_len, seq_len, device=tokens.device, dtype=torch.bool),
            diagonal=1,
        )
        h = self.encoder(h, mask=causal, is_causal=True)
        h = self.norm(h)
        return self.head(h)


def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Construct the autoregressive model graded by the FFLM evaluator."""
    return FlipFlopModel(
        vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE,
        max_len=max(config.train_len, config.eval_long_len, config.depth_probe_long),
    )

class _LongConvBlock(nn.Module):
    """Depthwise causal FFT long conv with decay envelope + H3-style gating."""

    def __init__(self, d_model: int, max_len: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.max_len = max_len
        self.kernel = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(d_model, max_len) * 0.002)
        self.log_decay = nn.Parameter(torch.linspace(-3.0, 1.0, d_model))
        self.in_gate = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model, bias=False)

    def _materialise_kernel(self, T: int) -> torch.Tensor:
        t = torch.arange(T, device=self.kernel.device, dtype=self.kernel.dtype)
        decay = torch.exp(
            -F.softplus(self.log_decay).unsqueeze(-1) * t.unsqueeze(0) / self.max_len
        )
        return self.kernel[:, :T] * decay  # [D, T]

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, T, D = x.shape
        v = x * torch.sigmoid(self.in_gate(x))       # positionwise gate
        k = self._materialise_kernel(T)              # [D, T]
        n = 2 * T
        Xf = torch.fft.rfft(v.transpose(1, 2), n=n)  # [B, D, n//2+1]
        Kf = torch.fft.rfft(k, n=n)                  # [D, n//2+1]
        y = torch.fft.irfft(Xf * Kf.unsqueeze(0), n=n)[..., :T]  # causal
        y = y.transpose(1, 2)                        # [B, T, D]
        return self.out_proj(y)


class _LTIBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model: int, max_len: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.conv = _LongConvBlock(d_model, max_len)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(d_model, 4 * d_model),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(4 * d_model, d_model),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = x + self.conv(self.ln1(x))
        x = x + self.mlp(self.ln2(x))
        return x


class FlipFlopModel(nn.Module):
    """6-block LTI long-conv model (data-independent token mixing)."""

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = VOCAB_SIZE, max_len: int = 2048):
        super().__init__()
        d_model = 512
        n_layers = 6
        self.max_len = max_len
        self.tok = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            [_LTIBlock(d_model, max_len) for _ in range(n_layers)]
        )
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size, bias=False)

    def forward(self, tokens: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        h = self.tok(tokens)
        for block in self.blocks:
            h = block(h)
        h = self.norm(h)
        return self.head(h)


def build_model(config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    return FlipFlopModel(
        vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE,
        max_len=max(config.train_len, config.eval_long_len, config.depth_probe_long),
    )

tasks.name: Synthetic Matrix Completion: Neural Matrix Factorization Architecture
tasks.summary: Given a sparse subset of entries of an unknown rank-r ground-truth matrix M*,
tasks.description_md:
# Synthetic Matrix Completion: Neural Matrix Factorization Architecture

## Research Question
Given a sparse subset of entries of an unknown rank-r ground-truth matrix M*,
how should we **parameterize a neural matrix factorization** (depth, initialization,
regularization, optimizer) so that gradient descent recovers M* as accurately
as possible on the *unobserved* entries?

This is the canonical "deep matrix factorization" question studied by Arora,
Cohen, Hu, Luo, "Implicit Regularization in Deep Matrix Factorization"
(NeurIPS 2019; [arXiv:1905.13655](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.13655)). They
showed empirically that *increasing the depth* of the factorization
M = W_d W_{d-1} ... W_1 introduces a stronger implicit bias toward low-rank
solutions, often beating both shallow factorizations and classical
nuclear-norm minimization.

## Background
Low-rank matrix completion is fundamental in collaborative filtering, signal
processing, and statistics. Classical approaches solve a convex relaxation
(minimize nuclear norm subject to fitting the observations) via algorithms
like SVT ([Cai-Candes-Shen 2010](https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.3286)) or perform
explicit non-convex factorization via alternating minimization
([Jain-Netrapalli-Sanghavi 2012](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.0467)).

Deep matrix factorization replaces the explicit rank constraint with depth:
write M as a product of d square (full hidden dim) bias-free linear layers
and minimize the squared error on observed entries by gradient descent. With
small initialization the resulting solution biases towards low effective
rank, and depth d >= 3 makes this bias sharper than depth 2 (and stronger
than the implicit nuclear-norm regularizer at low observation rates).

## What You Can Modify
Edit the scaffold file `pytorch-examples/theory_matrix_completion/custom_strategy.py`
inside the EDITABLE block. Concretely, the editable region contains:

1. `build_strategy() -> MatrixRecoveryStrategy` — the entry point the driver calls.
2. The `MatrixRecoveryStrategy` interface declaration.
3. One or more reference strategy classes (default: `DeepMatrixFactorization`).

You may completely replace the strategy class with any algorithm you like
(deeper factorizations, alternative initializations, balanced
parameterization, IRLS, ADMM, SVT, AltMin, neural ODE inits, etc.) as long
as the returned object implements `recover(observed_values, observed_mask,
n, rank_hint, device, max_iters, log_iters) -> torch.Tensor` of shape
`[n, n]`.

## Fixed Setup
- **Ground truth**: random rank-r matrix M* = (U V^T) / sqrt(r) with
  U, V ~ N(0, 1) i.i.d. of shape `[n, r]`, rescaled to `||M*||_F = n`.
  (Same construction as Arora et al. 2019; `gen_gt.py` in their repo.)
- **Observations**: uniformly random subset of the n*n entries at the
  configured observation rate (`gen_obs.py` in the reference repo). The
  observed entries carry additive i.i.d. Gaussian noise
  `N(0, noise_std^2)` (per-entry RMS of M* is 1 by the `||M*||_F = n`
  normalization). Evaluation always compares against the CLEAN M*, so
  interpolating the noisy observations to zero training loss is
  suboptimal: the oracle error floor is roughly
  `noise_std * sqrt(dof / m)` with `dof = r(2n - r)` and `m` observed
  entries.
- **Driver**: in the release configuration, samples **three** random
  ground-truth matrices per top-level seed (papers average over many
  random instances: 20 in Candes & Plan 2010 and Keshavan et al. 2010,
  3 trials in Arora et al. 2019) and runs one initialization per matrix,
  then calls `strategy.recover(...)` with a hard iteration budget. The
  reported metrics are means across the three matrices.
- **Metric**: relative Frobenius error on the *unobserved* entries
  (`test_rel_fro = ||(estimate - M*)[~mask]||_F / ||M*[~mask]||_F`), where
  lower is better. A derived `score = max(0, 1 - test_rel_fro)` may be printed
  for feedback, but the benchmark score spec uses `test_rel_fro` directly.
- Compute budget: each test command must finish in under 45 minutes on a
  single H100.

## Interface Notes
- `recover(...)` receives `observed_values` (M* masked to zero off the
  observation set), `observed_mask` (bool [n, n]), `n`, `rank_hint`
  (the true rank — you may use or ignore), `device`, `max_iters`, and
  `log_iters`.
- Return a CPU or GPU `torch.Tensor` of shape `[n, n]`. The driver moves
  it to CPU and casts to float32.
- Please emit `TRAIN_METRICS iter=... train_mse=...` periodically so the
  agent loop sees training progress.

## Evaluated Configurations
Three configurations are evaluated (`m/dof` = observed entries over the
rank-r degrees of freedom `r(2n - r)`). All use `n = 600`, the canonical
size of the noisy matrix-completion literature (Candes & Plan, Proc. IEEE
2010, Fig. 2 and Keshavan, Montanari & Oh, JMLR 2010, Sec. 1.6 both
simulate 600x600 matrices with rank and sampling swept):

| label       | n   | r | observed | noise_std | m/dof |
|-------------|-----|---|----------|-----------|-------|
| `rank4-600` | 600 | 4 | 4.25%    | 0.20      | 3.20  |
| `rank6-600` | 600 | 6 | 3.68%    | 0.15      | 1.85  |
| `rank8-600` | 600 | 8 | 3.97%    | 0.15      | 1.50  |

The ladder descends toward the exact-recovery sampling threshold, so the
science shifts from noise robustness (easy) to sample-starved implicit
regularization (hard). At `n = 600` the recovery phase transition is much
sharper than at the previous `n = 80-160` (Candes & Recht 2009, Fig. 1)
and the classical-recovery threshold itself grows with `n` (AltMin needs
`m ~ C n r log n`), so every rung sits at higher `m/dof` than before
(3.20 / 1.85 / 1.50 instead of 2.56 / 1.64 / 1.33) to stay on the
informative side of the transition; the sample-starved regime matches Arora et al. (2019), whose
100x100 experiments span `m/dof` 1.05-5.13.

The leaderboard primary metric per environment is `test_rel_fro` (lower better).
The task-level score is the geometric mean of normalized `test_rel_fro` terms
across the three environments.

## Baselines
- **shallow_mf** — Depth-2 matrix factorization (`M = W_2 W_1`),
  Gaussian init scale `1e-3`, Adam. Mirrors the depth-2 curve of Arora
  et al. (2019), Figure 1.
- **soft_impute** — SoftImpute (Mazumder, Hastie, Tibshirani, JMLR 2010):
  iterative soft-thresholded SVD, the standard convex nuclear-norm
  relaxation baseline. Does not interpolate the observation noise.
- **als** — Alternating least squares at the true rank (Jain, Netrapalli,
  Sanghavi, STOC 2013, arXiv:1212.0467) with spectral initialization
  (Keshavan-Montanari-Oh 2010). Very strong when sampling is comfortable,
  brittle near the sampling threshold.
- **deep_mf** — Depth-3 deep matrix factorization with small Gaussian
  init (`init_scale = 1e-3`) and learning rate `1e-3`, Adam. The depth-3
  setup of Arora et al. (2019), Figure 1.
tasks.description_html:
Synthetic Matrix Completion: Neural Matrix Factorization Architecture

Research Question

Given a sparse subset of entries of an unknown rank-r ground-truth matrix M, how should we parameterize a neural matrix factorization (depth, initialization, regularization, optimizer) so that gradient descent recovers M as accurately as possible on the unobserved entries?

This is the canonical "deep matrix factorization" question studied by Arora, Cohen, Hu, Luo, "Implicit Regularization in Deep Matrix Factorization" (NeurIPS 2019; arXiv:1905.13655). They showed empirically that increasing the depth of the factorization M = W_d W_{d-1} ... W_1 introduces a stronger implicit bias toward low-rank solutions, often beating both shallow factorizations and classical nuclear-norm minimization.

Background

Low-rank matrix completion is fundamental in collaborative filtering, signal processing, and statistics. Classical approaches solve a convex relaxation (minimize nuclear norm subject to fitting the observations) via algorithms like SVT (Cai-Candes-Shen 2010) or perform explicit non-convex factorization via alternating minimization (Jain-Netrapalli-Sanghavi 2012).

Deep matrix factorization replaces the explicit rank constraint with depth: write M as a product of d square (full hidden dim) bias-free linear layers and minimize the squared error on observed entries by gradient descent. With small initialization the resulting solution biases towards low effective rank, and depth d >= 3 makes this bias sharper than depth 2 (and stronger than the implicit nuclear-norm regularizer at low observation rates).

What You Can Modify

Edit the scaffold file pytorch-examples/theory_matrix_completion/custom_strategy.py inside the EDITABLE block. Concretely, the editable region contains:

  1. build_strategy() -> MatrixRecoveryStrategy — the entry point the driver calls.
  2. The MatrixRecoveryStrategy interface declaration.
  3. One or more reference strategy classes (default: DeepMatrixFactorization).

You may completely replace the strategy class with any algorithm you like (deeper factorizations, alternative initializations, balanced parameterization, IRLS, ADMM, SVT, AltMin, neural ODE inits, etc.) as long as the returned object implements recover(observed_values, observed_mask, n, rank_hint, device, max_iters, log_iters) -> torch.Tensor of shape [n, n].

Fixed Setup

  • Ground truth: random rank-r matrix M* = (U V^T) / sqrt(r) with U, V ~ N(0, 1) i.i.d. of shape [n, r], rescaled to ||M*||_F = n. (Same construction as Arora et al. 2019; gen_gt.py in their repo.)
  • Observations: uniformly random subset of the nn entries at the configured observation rate (gen_obs.py in the reference repo). The observed entries carry additive i.i.d. Gaussian noise N(0, noise_std^2) (per-entry RMS of M is 1 by the ||M*||_F = n normalization). Evaluation always compares against the CLEAN M*, so interpolating the noisy observations to zero training loss is suboptimal: the oracle error floor is roughly noise_std * sqrt(dof / m) with dof = r(2n - r) and m observed entries.
  • Driver: in the release configuration, samples three random ground-truth matrices per top-level seed (papers average over many random instances: 20 in Candes & Plan 2010 and Keshavan et al. 2010, 3 trials in Arora et al. 2019) and runs one initialization per matrix, then calls strategy.recover(...) with a hard iteration budget. The reported metrics are means across the three matrices.
  • Metric: relative Frobenius error on the unobserved entries (test_rel_fro = ||(estimate - M*)[~mask]||_F / ||M*[~mask]||_F), where lower is better. A derived score = max(0, 1 - test_rel_fro) may be printed for feedback, but the benchmark score spec uses test_rel_fro directly.
  • Compute budget: each test command must finish in under 45 minutes on a single H100.

Interface Notes

  • recover(...) receives observed_values (M* masked to zero off the observation set), observed_mask (bool [n, n]), n, rank_hint (the true rank — you may use or ignore), device, max_iters, and log_iters.
  • Return a CPU or GPU torch.Tensor of shape [n, n]. The driver moves it to CPU and casts to float32.
  • Please emit TRAIN_METRICS iter=... train_mse=... periodically so the agent loop sees training progress.

Evaluated Configurations

Three configurations are evaluated (m/dof = observed entries over the rank-r degrees of freedom r(2n - r)). All use n = 600, the canonical size of the noisy matrix-completion literature (Candes & Plan, Proc. IEEE 2010, Fig. 2 and Keshavan, Montanari & Oh, JMLR 2010, Sec. 1.6 both simulate 600x600 matrices with rank and sampling swept):

label n r observed noise_std m/dof
rank4-600 600 4 4.25% 0.20 3.20
rank6-600 600 6 3.68% 0.15 1.85
rank8-600 600 8 3.97% 0.15 1.50

The ladder descends toward the exact-recovery sampling threshold, so the science shifts from noise robustness (easy) to sample-starved implicit regularization (hard). At n = 600 the recovery phase transition is much sharper than at the previous n = 80-160 (Candes & Recht 2009, Fig. 1) and the classical-recovery threshold itself grows with n (AltMin needs m ~ C n r log n), so every rung sits at higher m/dof than before (3.20 / 1.85 / 1.50 instead of 2.56 / 1.64 / 1.33) to stay on the informative side of the transition; the sample-starved regime matches Arora et al. (2019), whose 100x100 experiments span m/dof 1.05-5.13.

The leaderboard primary metric per environment is test_rel_fro (lower better). The task-level score is the geometric mean of normalized test_rel_fro terms across the three environments.

Baselines

  • shallow_mf — Depth-2 matrix factorization (M = W_2 W_1), Gaussian init scale 1e-3, Adam. Mirrors the depth-2 curve of Arora et al. (2019), Figure 1.
  • soft_impute — SoftImpute (Mazumder, Hastie, Tibshirani, JMLR 2010): iterative soft-thresholded SVD, the standard convex nuclear-norm relaxation baseline. Does not interpolate the observation noise.
  • als — Alternating least squares at the true rank (Jain, Netrapalli, Sanghavi, STOC 2013, arXiv:1212.0467) with spectral initialization (Keshavan-Montanari-Oh 2010). Very strong when sampling is comfortable, brittle near the sampling threshold.
  • deep_mf — Depth-3 deep matrix factorization with small Gaussian init (init_scale = 1e-3) and learning rate 1e-3, Adam. The depth-3 setup of Arora et al. (2019), Figure 1.

files.content:
"""Deep matrix factorization scaffold for MLS-Bench.

The fixed driver samples a random low-rank ground-truth matrix M*, picks a
random observation mask, adds i.i.d. Gaussian noise to the OBSERVED entries,
and asks the agent to design a recovery algorithm that fits the noisy
observations and generalizes to the *unobserved* entries. Evaluation always
compares against the clean M*, so interpolating the observation noise hurts:
the achievable error is floored at roughly sigma * sqrt(dof / m).

The scientific question is the **neural matrix factorization architecture**:
depth of the factorization, initialization, optimizer, regularization. The
benchmark is inspired by Arora, Cohen, Hu and Luo, "Implicit Regularization
in Deep Matrix Factorization" (NeurIPS 2019; arXiv:1905.13655).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import random
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field, replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable

import torch
from torch import nn


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Benchmark configuration
# =====================================================================
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskConfig:
    n: int = 600                      # square matrix side
    rank: int = 4                     # true rank of M*
    observation_rate: float = 0.042524  # fraction of entries observed
    noise_std: float = 0.20           # additive N(0, sigma^2) noise on OBSERVED entries
    num_matrices: int = 3             # random ground-truth matrices per top-level seed
    num_inits: int = 1                # one init per top-level seed
    max_iters: int = 20000            # max optimizer iterations per run
    eval_interval: int = 1000         # log every this many iterations
    early_stop_train_loss: float = 1e-7  # train MSE early-stop threshold
    train_loss_patience: int = 4      # consecutive logs below threshold to stop
    # The total wall-time budget per run is bounded by max_iters; the
    # editable strategy may exit early if it converges.


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunResult:
    matrix_index: int
    init_index: int
    iters: int
    train_mse: float
    test_rel_fro: float            # relative Frobenius error on unobserved entries
    test_mse: float                # MSE on unobserved entries
    full_rel_fro: float            # relative Frobenius error on full matrix


DEFAULT_TASK = TaskConfig()


def set_global_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def sample_ground_truth(
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Sample a random rank-r matrix M* with Frobenius norm equal to n.

    Follows Arora et al. (2019), gen_gt.py:
        U, V ~ N(0, 1), shape (n, r); M = U V^T / sqrt(r); rescale to ||M||_F = n.
    """
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    U = torch.randn(config.n, config.rank, generator=generator)
    V = torch.randn(config.n, config.rank, generator=generator)
    M = (U @ V.T) / math.sqrt(config.rank)
    M = M / M.norm() * config.n
    return M


def sample_observation_mask(
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Sample a random Bernoulli mask with the desired observation rate."""
    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    total = config.n * config.n
    num_observed = max(1, int(round(total * config.observation_rate)))
    indices = torch.randperm(total, generator=generator)[:num_observed]
    mask = torch.zeros(total, dtype=torch.bool)
    mask[indices] = True
    return mask.view(config.n, config.n)


def relative_fro_error(estimate: torch.Tensor, truth: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    """Compute ||estimate - truth||_F / ||truth||_F."""
    denom = float(truth.norm().item())
    if denom == 0.0:
        return float(estimate.norm().item())
    return float((estimate - truth).norm().item() / denom)


def masked_mse(estimate: torch.Tensor, truth: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    diff = (estimate - truth)[mask]
    if diff.numel() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(diff.pow(2).mean().item())


# =====================================================================
# EDITABLE: matrix recovery strategy
# =====================================================================
# Design freedom: the agent may freely modify the body of build_strategy()
# below. The returned object must implement:
#
#     recover(observed_values, observed_mask, n, rank_hint, device, max_iters,
#             log_iters) -> torch.Tensor  (shape [n, n], dtype float32)
#
# The fixed driver gives you:
#   - observed_values: torch.Tensor [n, n] with M*[i,j] where mask is True
#                      and 0 elsewhere (the unobserved entries are zeroed out
#                      so you cannot peek at the truth).
#   - observed_mask:   torch.Tensor [n, n] of dtype bool.
#   - n, rank_hint:    matrix side and TRUE rank of M* (you may use rank_hint
#                      as side information or ignore it).
#   - device:          torch.device for placing tensors.
#   - max_iters:       hard budget on optimizer iterations.
#   - log_iters:       suggested interval at which to print TRAIN_METRICS.
#
# Return: a full [n, n] estimate of M*. Evaluation compares this estimate
# against the ground-truth M* on the *unobserved* entries (and reports the
# full-matrix error as a secondary metric).


def build_strategy() -> "MatrixRecoveryStrategy":
    """Return the matrix-recovery strategy used by the fixed driver."""
    return DeepMatrixFactorization(depth=3, init_scale=1e-3, lr=1e-3)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reference implementation: deep matrix factorization (Arora et al. 2019)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class MatrixRecoveryStrategy:
    """Interface contract; subclass and implement `recover`."""

    def recover(
        self,
        observed_values: torch.Tensor,
        observed_mask: torch.Tensor,
        n: int,
        rank_hint: int,
        device: torch.device,
        max_iters: int,
        log_iters: int,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        raise NotImplementedError


class DeepMatrixFactorization(MatrixRecoveryStrategy):
    """End-to-end parameterization M = W_d ... W_1 with bias-free Linears."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        depth: int = 3,
        init_scale: float = 1e-3,
        lr: float = 1e-3,
        train_thres: float = 1e-7,
    ) -> None:
        if depth < 2:
            raise ValueError("DeepMatrixFactorization requires depth >= 2.")
        self.depth = depth
        self.init_scale = float(init_scale)
        self.lr = float(lr)
        self.train_thres = float(train_thres)

    def _build(self, n: int, device: torch.device) -> nn.Sequential:
        layers = [nn.Linear(n, n, bias=False) for _ in range(self.depth)]
        # Gaussian init with controlled end-to-end Frobenius scale, mirroring
        # Arora et al. (2019) gen_gt.py / init_model.
        scale = (self.init_scale ** (1.0 / self.depth)) * (n ** (-0.5))
        for layer in layers:
            nn.init.normal_(layer.weight, mean=0.0, std=scale)
        return nn.Sequential(*layers).to(device)

    @staticmethod
    def _e2e(model: nn.Sequential) -> torch.Tensor:
        out = None
        for layer in model:
            out = layer.weight.t() if out is None else layer(out)
        return out

    def recover(
        self,
        observed_values: torch.Tensor,
        observed_mask: torch.Tensor,
        n: int,
        rank_hint: int,
        device: torch.device,
        max_iters: int,
        log_iters: int,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        model = self._build(n, device)
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=self.lr)
        mask = observed_mask.to(device)
        target = observed_values.to(device)
        denom = max(int(mask.sum().item()), 1)

        for it in range(1, max_iters + 1):
            e2e = self._e2e(model)
            residual = (e2e - target) * mask
            loss = residual.pow(2).sum() / denom
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

            if it == 1 or it % log_iters == 0 or it == max_iters:
                print(
                    f"TRAIN_METRICS iter={it} train_mse={loss.item():.6e}",
                    flush=True,
                )
                if loss.item() <= self.train_thres:
                    break

        with torch.no_grad():
            return self._e2e(model).detach().cpu()


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: evaluation driver
# =====================================================================
def resolve_device(device_arg: str) -> torch.device:
    if device_arg == "cpu":
        return torch.device("cpu")
    if device_arg == "cuda":
        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but no GPU is available.")
        return torch.device("cuda")
    return torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")


def maybe_apply_smoke_mode(config: TaskConfig, enabled: bool) -> TaskConfig:
    if not enabled:
        return config
    return replace(
        config,
        n=30,
        rank=3,
        num_matrices=1,
        num_inits=1,
        max_iters=400,
        eval_interval=50,
    )


def evaluate_estimate(
    estimate: torch.Tensor,
    ground_truth: torch.Tensor,
    mask: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Return (test_rel_fro, test_mse, full_rel_fro)."""
    missing = ~mask
    if missing.sum().item() == 0:
        test_rel_fro = 0.0
        test_mse = 0.0
    else:
        test_rel_fro = relative_fro_error(
            estimate[missing], ground_truth[missing]
        )
        test_mse = masked_mse(estimate, ground_truth, missing)
    full_rel_fro = relative_fro_error(estimate, ground_truth)
    return test_rel_fro, test_mse, full_rel_fro


def run_one(
    strategy: MatrixRecoveryStrategy,
    ground_truth: torch.Tensor,
    observed_values: torch.Tensor,
    mask: torch.Tensor,
    config: TaskConfig,
    device: torch.device,
    matrix_index: int,
    init_index: int,
    init_seed: int,
) -> RunResult:
    set_global_seed(init_seed)
    t0 = time.time()
    estimate = strategy.recover(
        observed_values=observed_values,
        observed_mask=mask,
        n=config.n,
        rank_hint=config.rank,
        device=device,
        max_iters=config.max_iters,
        log_iters=config.eval_interval,
    )
    elapsed = time.time() - t0

    if not isinstance(estimate, torch.Tensor):
        raise TypeError("Strategy must return a torch.Tensor.")
    if estimate.shape != (config.n, config.n):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Strategy returned shape {tuple(estimate.shape)}, expected ({config.n}, {config.n})."
        )

    estimate = estimate.detach().to(torch.float32).cpu()
    truth_cpu = ground_truth.detach().to(torch.float32).cpu()
    mask_cpu = mask.detach().cpu()

    train_mse = masked_mse(estimate, truth_cpu, mask_cpu)
    test_rel_fro, test_mse, full_rel_fro = evaluate_estimate(
        estimate, truth_cpu, mask_cpu
    )

    print(
        "RUN_METRICS "
        f"matrix={matrix_index} init={init_index} elapsed={elapsed:.2f} "
        f"train_mse={train_mse:.6e} test_rel_fro={test_rel_fro:.6e} "
        f"test_mse={test_mse:.6e} full_rel_fro={full_rel_fro:.6e}",
        flush=True,
    )

    return RunResult(
        matrix_index=matrix_index,
        init_index=init_index,
        iters=config.max_iters,
        train_mse=train_mse,
        test_rel_fro=test_rel_fro,
        test_mse=test_mse,
        full_rel_fro=full_rel_fro,
    )


def run_benchmark(
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
    device: torch.device,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    print(
        "TASK_CONFIG "
        + " ".join(
            [
                f"n={config.n}",
                f"rank={config.rank}",
                f"obs_rate={config.observation_rate}",
                f"noise_std={config.noise_std}",
                f"num_matrices={config.num_matrices}",
                f"num_inits={config.num_inits}",
                f"max_iters={config.max_iters}",
            ]
        ),
        flush=True,
    )

    strategy = build_strategy()
    print(f"STRATEGY {type(strategy).__name__}", flush=True)

    results: list[RunResult] = []
    for matrix_index in range(config.num_matrices):
        ground_truth = sample_ground_truth(config, seed=seed + 17 * matrix_index)
        mask = sample_observation_mask(
            config, seed=seed + 23 * matrix_index + 101
        )
        noise_generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + 31 * matrix_index + 7)
        noise = torch.randn(config.n, config.n, generator=noise_generator) * config.noise_std
        observed_values = (ground_truth + noise) * mask
        print(
            "DATASET_METRICS "
            f"matrix={matrix_index} n={config.n} rank={config.rank} "
            f"num_observed={int(mask.sum().item())} "
            f"noise_std={config.noise_std:.4f} "
            f"frobenius_norm={float(ground_truth.norm().item()):.4f}",
            flush=True,
        )
        ground_truth = ground_truth.to(device)
        observed_values = observed_values.to(device)
        mask = mask.to(device)

        for init_index in range(config.num_inits):
            init_seed = seed * 1_000_000 + matrix_index * 1_000 + init_index
            results.append(
                run_one(
                    strategy=strategy,
                    ground_truth=ground_truth,
                    observed_values=observed_values,
                    mask=mask,
                    config=config,
                    device=device,
                    matrix_index=matrix_index,
                    init_index=init_index,
                    init_seed=init_seed,
                )
            )

    test_rel_fro = torch.tensor(
        [r.test_rel_fro for r in results], dtype=torch.float64
    )
    full_rel_fro = torch.tensor(
        [r.full_rel_fro for r in results], dtype=torch.float64
    )
    train_mse = torch.tensor(
        [r.train_mse for r in results], dtype=torch.float64
    )
    test_mse = torch.tensor(
        [r.test_mse for r in results], dtype=torch.float64
    )

    final_metrics = {
        "test_rel_fro": float(test_rel_fro.mean().item()),
        "test_rel_fro_std": float(test_rel_fro.std(unbiased=False).item()),
        "full_rel_fro": float(full_rel_fro.mean().item()),
        "full_rel_fro_std": float(full_rel_fro.std(unbiased=False).item()),
        "train_mse": float(train_mse.mean().item()),
        "test_mse": float(test_mse.mean().item()),
        # Score = 1 - test_rel_fro, clamped to [0, 1], so higher is better.
        "score": float(max(0.0, 1.0 - test_rel_fro.mean().item())),
        "num_runs": int(len(results)),
    }
    print(
        "FINAL_METRICS "
        + " ".join(
            f"{key}={value:.6e}"
            if isinstance(value, float)
            else f"{key}={value}"
            for key, value in final_metrics.items()
        ),
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        f"TEST_METRICS test_rel_fro={final_metrics['test_rel_fro']:.6e} "
        f"full_rel_fro={final_metrics['full_rel_fro']:.6e} "
        f"score={final_metrics['score']:.6e}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return {
        "config": asdict(config),
        "metrics": final_metrics,
        "results": [asdict(r) for r in results],
    }


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Run the MLS-Bench theory-matrix-completion task."
    )
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--label", type=str, default="eval")
    parser.add_argument("--device", choices=("auto", "cpu", "cuda"), default="auto")
    parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--observation-rate", type=float, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--noise-std", type=float, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--num-matrices", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--num-inits", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--max-iters", type=int, default=None)
    return parser.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    config = maybe_apply_smoke_mode(DEFAULT_TASK, args.smoke)
    if args.n is not None:
        config = replace(config, n=args.n)
    if args.rank is not None:
        config = replace(config, rank=args.rank)
    if args.observation_rate is not None:
        config = replace(config, observation_rate=args.observation_rate)
    if args.noise_std is not None:
        config = replace(config, noise_std=args.noise_std)

def build_strategy() -> "MatrixRecoveryStrategy":
    """Return the matrix-recovery strategy used by the fixed driver."""
    return DeepMatrixFactorization(depth=3, init_scale=1e-3, lr=1e-3)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reference implementation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class MatrixRecoveryStrategy:
    """Interface contract; subclass and implement `recover`."""

    def recover(
        self,
        observed_values: torch.Tensor,
        observed_mask: torch.Tensor,
        n: int,
        rank_hint: int,
        device: torch.device,
        max_iters: int,
        log_iters: int,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        raise NotImplementedError


class DeepMatrixFactorization(MatrixRecoveryStrategy):
    """End-to-end depth-d parameterization M = W_d ... W_1, full hidden dim."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        depth: int = 3,
        init_scale: float = 1e-3,
        lr: float = 1e-3,
        train_thres: float = 1e-7,
    ) -> None:
        if depth < 2:
            raise ValueError("DeepMatrixFactorization requires depth >= 2.")
        self.depth = depth
        self.init_scale = float(init_scale)
        self.lr = float(lr)
        self.train_thres = float(train_thres)

    def _build(self, n: int, device: torch.device) -> nn.Sequential:
        layers = [nn.Linear(n, n, bias=False) for _ in range(self.depth)]
        scale = (self.init_scale ** (1.0 / self.depth)) * (n ** (-0.5))
        for layer in layers:
            nn.init.normal_(layer.weight, mean=0.0, std=scale)
        return nn.Sequential(*layers).to(device)

    @staticmethod
    def _e2e(model: nn.Sequential) -> torch.Tensor:
        out = None
        for layer in model:
            out = layer.weight.t() if out is None else layer(out)
        return out

    def recover(
        self,
        observed_values: torch.Tensor,
        observed_mask: torch.Tensor,
        n: int,
        rank_hint: int,
        device: torch.device,
        max_iters: int,
        log_iters: int,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        model = self._build(n, device)
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=self.lr)
        mask = observed_mask.to(device)
        target = observed_values.to(device)
        denom = max(int(mask.sum().item()), 1)

        for it in range(1, max_iters + 1):
            e2e = self._e2e(model)
            residual = (e2e - target) * mask
            loss = residual.pow(2).sum() / denom
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

            if it == 1 or it % log_iters == 0 or it == max_iters:
                print(
                    f"TRAIN_METRICS iter={it} train_mse={loss.item():.6e}",
                    flush=True,
                )
                if loss.item() <= self.train_thres:
                    break

        with torch.no_grad():
            return self._e2e(model).detach().cpu()

def build_strategy() -> "MatrixRecoveryStrategy":
    """Return the matrix-recovery strategy used by the fixed driver."""
    return SoftImpute(lam_frac=0.02, num_sweeps=300)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Interface contract (fixed shape expected by the driver).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class MatrixRecoveryStrategy:
    """Interface contract; subclass and implement `recover`."""

    def recover(
        self,
        observed_values: torch.Tensor,
        observed_mask: torch.Tensor,
        n: int,
        rank_hint: int,
        device: torch.device,
        max_iters: int,
        log_iters: int,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        raise NotImplementedError


class SoftImpute(MatrixRecoveryStrategy):
    """Mazumder et al. (2010) SoftImpute with a relative threshold.

    lam_frac    Soft-threshold as a fraction of the current top singular
                value (relative regularization path).
    num_sweeps  Number of fill-in / soft-threshold sweeps (each sweep is
                one SVD; well below the max_iters budget).
    """

    def __init__(self, lam_frac: float = 0.02, num_sweeps: int = 300) -> None:
        self.lam_frac = float(lam_frac)
        self.num_sweeps = int(num_sweeps)

    def recover(
        self,
        observed_values: torch.Tensor,
        observed_mask: torch.Tensor,
        n: int,
        rank_hint: int,
        device: torch.device,
        max_iters: int,
        log_iters: int,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        mask = observed_mask.to(device)
        target = observed_values.to(device)
        z = target.clone()
        x = z.clone()
        sweeps = min(self.num_sweeps, max_iters)
        for sweep in range(1, sweeps + 1):
            u, sing, vh = torch.linalg.svd(z, full_matrices=False)
            lam = self.lam_frac * sing[0]
            sing_thresholded = (sing - lam).clamp(min=0.0)
            x = u @ torch.diag(sing_thresholded) @ vh
            z = torch.where(mask, target, x)
            if sweep == 1 or sweep % max(log_iters // 10, 1) == 0 or sweep == sweeps:
                resid = ((x - target)[mask] ** 2).mean().item() if mask.any() else 0.0
                eff_rank = int((sing_thresholded > 1e-8).sum().item())
                print(
                    f"TRAIN_METRICS iter={sweep} train_mse={resid:.6e} "
                    f"effective_rank={eff_rank}",
                    flush=True,
                )
        return x.detach().cpu()

def build_strategy() -> "MatrixRecoveryStrategy":
    """Return the matrix-recovery strategy used by the fixed driver."""
    return AlternatingLeastSquares(num_sweeps=60, ridge=1e-2)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Interface contract (fixed shape expected by the driver).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
class MatrixRecoveryStrategy:
    """Interface contract; subclass and implement `recover`."""

    def recover(
        self,
        observed_values: torch.Tensor,
        observed_mask: torch.Tensor,
        n: int,
        rank_hint: int,
        device: torch.device,
        max_iters: int,
        log_iters: int,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        raise NotImplementedError


class AlternatingLeastSquares(MatrixRecoveryStrategy):
    """Jain-Netrapalli-Sanghavi alternating minimization at the true rank.

    Each sweep solves, row by row, the ridge least-squares problem for U
    with V fixed and then for V with U fixed, using only observed entries.
    """

    def __init__(self, num_sweeps: int = 60, ridge: float = 1e-2) -> None:
        self.num_sweeps = int(num_sweeps)
        self.ridge = float(ridge)

    @staticmethod
    def _solve_rows(
        target: torch.Tensor,
        mask: torch.Tensor,
        factor: torch.Tensor,
        ridge: float,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """For each row i, solve min_u ||target[i, obs] - u @ factor[obs].T||^2 + ridge||u||^2."""
        n, r = target.shape[0], factor.shape[1]
        out = torch.zeros(n, r, device=target.device, dtype=target.dtype)
        eye = torch.eye(r, device=target.device, dtype=target.dtype)
        for i in range(n):
            obs = mask[i]
            count = int(obs.sum().item())
            if count == 0:
                continue
            f = factor[obs]                      # [m_i, r]
            y = target[i, obs]                   # [m_i]
            gram = f.T @ f + ridge * count * eye / max(n, 1)
            rhs = f.T @ y
            out[i] = torch.linalg.solve(gram, rhs)
        return out

    def recover(
        self,
        observed_values: torch.Tensor,
        observed_mask: torch.Tensor,
        n: int,
        rank_hint: int,
        device: torch.device,
        max_iters: int,
        log_iters: int,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        mask = observed_mask.to(device)
        target = observed_values.to(device)
        r = max(int(rank_hint), 1)

        # Spectral initialization (Keshavan-Montanari-Oh 2010): SVD of the
        # zero-filled observation matrix rescaled by the sampling rate.
        obs_rate = float(mask.float().mean().item())
        u0, s0, v0h = torch.linalg.svd(target / max(obs_rate, 1e-8), full_matrices=False)
        u_factor = u0[:, :r] * s0[:r].sqrt().unsqueeze(0)
        v_factor = v0h[:r].T * s0[:r].sqrt().unsqueeze(0)

        sweeps = min(self.num_sweeps, max_iters)
        for sweep in range(1, sweeps + 1):
            u_factor = self._solve_rows(target, mask, v_factor, self.ridge)
            v_factor = self._solve_rows(target.T, mask.T, u_factor, self.ridge)
            if sweep == 1 or sweep % 10 == 0 or sweep == sweeps:
                estimate = u_factor @ v_factor.T
                resid = ((estimate - target)[mask] ** 2).mean().item()
                print(
                    f"TRAIN_METRICS iter={sweep} train_mse={resid:.6e}",
                    flush=True,
                )
        return (u_factor @ v_factor.T).detach().cpu()

tasks.description_md:
# Theory Modular Addition (Grokking)

## Research Question
On hidden-relabeling modular-addition tasks `y = pi[(sigma[a] + sigma[b]) mod p]`, can you
*accelerate* grokking — the delayed jump from memorization to generalization —
by changing only the **model architecture**, the **optimizer hyperparameters**,
and an **optional per-step gradient hook**, while keeping every other aspect of
the training pipeline fixed?

## Background
Power, Burns, Edwards, Babuschkin, and Misra introduced "grokking" in
"Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets"
(arXiv:2201.02177, 2022). Training a small transformer on binary operation
tables `a o b = c` over abstract symbols, they observed that training accuracy
reaches ~100% within 10^3 optimization steps while validation accuracy stays at
chance for orders of magnitude longer before jumping to ~100%; the delay grows
sharply as the training fraction shrinks (Power 2022, Figure 1), and weight
decay is the most effective known accelerator (Section 3.3). Nanda, Chan,
Lieberum, Smith, and Steinhardt reverse-engineered the algorithm learned by a
*one-layer* transformer on `a + b mod 113` (arXiv:2301.05217, ICLR 2023,
Section 3), showing the model implements a discrete-Fourier circuit; their
mainline protocol (which this benchmark follows) trains full-batch AdamW for
40,000 steps. Gromov (arXiv:2301.02679, 2023) showed that two-layer MLPs with
quadratic activations also grok on modular arithmetic. Liu, Michaud, and
Tegmark ("Omnigrok", ICLR 2023, arXiv:2210.01117) showed the grokking delay is
controlled by the initial weight norm. Lee, Kang, and Choi (arXiv:2405.20233,
2024) introduced *Grokfast*, gradient filters that accelerate grokking by
roughly 10-20x on modular arithmetic.

Following Power et al., who present group elements to the network as abstract
symbols with no internal numeric structure, the benchmark trains on
`y = pi[(sigma[a] + sigma[b]) mod p]`, where the input relabeling `sigma`
(shared by both operands) and the output relabeling `pi` are **hidden per-run
random permutations** of `Z_p` drawn inside the fixed benchmark code. Every
such operation is exactly isomorphic to plain `a + b mod p` (relabel the
token-embedding and unembedding rows), so the grokking dynamics are identical
to the canonical papers' — but the target mapping can only be learned from the
training pairs: no architecture can hard-code the answer table without
learning the relabelings.

In this benchmark, the *dataset construction*, *train/test split*, *loss
function*, *training loop*, and *step budget* are all fixed. Your scientific
freedom is in (a) the **model architecture**, (b) the **optimizer + its
hyperparameters**, and (c) an optional **per-step gradient hook** that runs
between `loss.backward()` and `optimizer.step()` (suitable for techniques
like Grokfast).

## What You Can Modify
Edit the scaffold file
`pytorch-examples/theory_modular_addition/custom_strategy.py` **only** inside
the editable block containing:

1. Any helper `nn.Module` classes you need
2. `build_model(p, config) -> nn.Module`
3. `make_optimizer(model, config) -> torch.optim.Optimizer`
4. `class TrainHook` with `post_grad(self, step)`

The benchmark is evaluated at a fixed prime `p=113` (the Nanda 2023 setting)
under three train fractions: `frac40` (0.40), `frac30` (0.30), and `frac25`
(0.25). Smaller fractions delay or prevent grokking within the step budget
(Power 2022, Section 3.1: "in the vicinity of 25-30% of data, a decrease of
1% of training data leads to an increase of 40-50% in median time to
generalization").

## Fixed Setup
- Task: `y = pi[(sigma[a] + sigma[b]) mod p]` for `a, b in {0, ..., p-1}`,
  with hidden per-run random permutations `sigma`, `pi` of `Z_p` (`sigma`
  shared by both operands).
- Inputs to the model: `LongTensor` of shape `[B, 2]` with values in `[0, p)`.
- Output of the model: `FloatTensor` of shape `[B, p]` (logits over the `p` classes).
- Loss: cross-entropy.
- Optimization: **full-batch** gradient descent over the training pairs
  (Nanda 2023 mainline protocol).
- Train/test split: a fixed fraction `train_frac` of the `p*p` table, with one
  split (and one hidden operation) per top-level seed.
- Step budget: up to `max_steps = 40000` optimizer steps per run (Nanda 2023:
  40,000 full-batch epochs), with early stopping once `test_acc >= 0.99` is
  sustained over 2 consecutive eval points. Runs also stop gracefully at the
  wall-clock safeguard before the runner's per-seed timeout, recording the
  latest evaluation metrics as a valid non-grokking result.
- Evaluation grid: a geometric grid of 61 steps from 50 to 40000 (grokking
  delays vary over orders of magnitude, so evaluation is log-uniform in time).

## Interface Notes
- `build_model(p, config)` must return a `torch.nn.Module` whose `forward(x)`
  takes `x: LongTensor[B, 2]` and returns `logits: FloatTensor[B, p]`.
  It must not depend on the train/test split.
- `make_optimizer(model, config)` must return a standard `torch.optim.Optimizer`.
- `TrainHook.__init__(self, model, config)` is called once per run.
- `TrainHook.post_grad(self, step)` is called after `loss.backward()` and
  before `optimizer.step()`; the hook may freely modify `p.grad` of each
  parameter. Returning `None` (the default) means "do nothing".

## Metrics
The leaderboard records, per environment, the mean over runs of:

- `score_<env>` = `log_auc_<env>` — the **primary signal**: area under the
  test-accuracy-versus-log(step) curve on the geometric eval grid, normalised
  to [0, 1]. After an early stop the last observed accuracy is carried
  forward. A method that groks at step `g` scores roughly
  `log(40000/g) / log(40000/50)`, so grokking one order of magnitude earlier
  is worth about 0.34 of score; a method that never generalises within the
  budget scores near the chance floor `1/p`. This makes the benchmark about
  HOW FAST a method generalises, not merely whether it eventually does.
- `test_accuracy_<env>` — final held-out accuracy at the last training step
  (diagnostic; not part of the aggregate).
- `mean_steps_to_grok_<env>` — first eval step of a sustained
  `test_acc >= 0.99` streak (set to `max_steps` if the model never groks).
- `grok_rate_<env>` — fraction of runs that grokked within the step budget.
- `best_test_accuracy_<env>` and `train_accuracy_<env>` for diagnostics.

The aggregated task score is the geometric mean of `score_<env>` over the
three train fractions. Higher is better.

## Baselines (variants of the editable block)
- **default** — Nanda 2023 reference: 1-layer transformer
  (`d_model=128`, 4 heads, `d_mlp=512`) trained with `AdamW(lr=1e-3, wd=1.0,
  betas=(0.9, 0.98))`, matching the Power 2022 default AdamW hyperparameters.
- **grokfast** — Lee 2024 (arXiv:2405.20233) Grokfast-EMA: same baseline
  optimizer with an EMA-of-gradient amplification hook (`alpha=0.98`,
  `lamb=2.0`).
- **mlp_quad** — Gromov 2023 (arXiv:2301.02679) two-layer fully-connected
  network without biases, quadratic activation, one-hot inputs, hidden
  width 256.
- **omnigrok_init** — default architecture and optimizer, but every
  parameter is multiplied by `alpha = 0.5` at initialisation (Liu, Michaud,
  Tegmark, ICLR 2023, arXiv:2210.01117): a reduced initial weight norm
  largely removes the grokking delay.

  • default — Nanda 2023 reference: 1-layer transformer (d_model=128, 4 heads, d_mlp=512) trained with AdamW(lr=1e-3, wd=1.0, betas=(0.9, 0.98)), matching the Power 2022 default AdamW hyperparameters.
  • grokfast — Lee 2024 (arXiv:2405.20233) Grokfast-EMA: same baseline optimizer with an EMA-of-gradient amplification hook (alpha=0.98, lamb=2.0).
  • mlp_quad — Gromov 2023 (arXiv:2301.02679) two-layer fully-connected network without biases, quadratic activation, one-hot inputs, hidden width 256.
  • omnigrok_init — default architecture and optimizer, but every parameter is multiplied by alpha = 0.5 at initialisation (Liu, Michaud, Tegmark, ICLR 2023, arXiv:2210.01117): a reduced initial weight norm largely removes the grokking delay.
