"""Semiautomaton-simulation scaffold for MLS-Bench — parallel-time edition.

Research question: which **parallel-time architecture** (and AdamW recipe)
best LEARNS to simulate hard finite-state semiautomata from full state
supervision, within a fixed online-training budget?

Setup follows Liu, Ash, Goel, Krishnamurthy & Zhang, "Transformers Learn
Shortcuts to Automata" (ICLR 2023, arXiv:2210.10749): sequences of length
T = 100, online training with a freshly drawn batch at every step, batch
size 16, AdamW, per-position cross-entropy on the full state sequence
(App. B.1.1 / B.3). Their headline finding: shallow non-recurrent networks
learn o(T)-depth "shortcuts" to solvable semiautomata, but accuracy on the
non-solvable S5 word problem climbs slowly with depth (Fig. 3a, best of 20
replicates: depth-1 7.9%, depth-8 51.8%, depth-9 97.2%, depth-16 99.9%).
Simulating a non-solvable group is NC1-complete (Barrington, JCSS 1989),
so no constant-depth parallel model can express it (unless TC0 = NC1), and
Merrill, Petty & Sabharwal, "The Illusion of State in State-Space Models"
(ICML 2024, arXiv:2404.08819) prove diagonal linear recurrences (S4/Mamba
family) sit in L-uniform TC0 — they need depth growing with T on exactly
this problem.

IMPORTANT — why recurrent models are excluded here: NC1-hardness only
constrains models whose serial computation depth does not grow with T.
A sequential RNN simulates ANY finite automaton by construction; both
reference papers use it as the trivial skyline (Liu et al. Fig. 5: a
1-layer LSTM reaches 100% on every task; Merrill et al. Fig. 3: a 1-layer
RNN solves every word problem). The open research question lives entirely
in the parallel-time regime, so this scaffold enforces it structurally
with two FIXED runtime guards that are *measured*, never self-reported:

  1. a module scan rejecting `nn.LSTM / nn.GRU / nn.RNN / *Cell` instances;
  2. an autograd-graph serial-depth probe: the longest path in the backward
     graph at seq_len 1024 may exceed the one at seq_len 256 by at most 80
     nodes. Per-token (or fine-grained chunkwise) python recurrences fail;
     attention, convolutions, and log-depth associative scans pass.

The transition tables are driver-private (`_PRIVATE_TABLES`) and the
automaton seed is masked before editable code sees the config: the model
must LEARN the automaton from sampled (input, state) streams. Hard-coding
or reconstructing any transition table inside the editable block is out of
contract, and an init-time tripwire aborts any run whose *untrained* model
already beats 25% accuracy (chance is at most 1/24).

The editable region exposes three functions:
  1. `build_model(env_spec, config)` returns an `nn.Module` mapping a token
     id sequence `[B, T]` to per-position state logits `[B, T, Q]`.
  2. `get_optimizer_config(config)` returns AdamW hyperparameters.
  3. `forward_logits(model, input_ids, env_spec)` is the inference wrapper.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import itertools
import json
import math
import random
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable

import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Benchmark configuration
# =====================================================================
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EnvSpec:
    """Public environment description. Transition tables are driver-private."""

    name: str
    alphabet_size: int
    num_states: int
    seq_len: int   # training/eval sequence length (Liu et al. 2023: T = 100)
    max_len: int   # maximum length the model must support (depth probe uses it)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskConfig:
    env_name: str = "random_dfa"
    seq_len: int = 100            # Liu et al. 2023 App. B.1.1: T = 100
    train_steps: int = 40_000
    batch_size: int = 16          # Liu et al. 2023 App. B.3 (GPT-2 recipe)
    eval_batches: int = 48
    log_interval: int = 1000
    seed: int = 0
    max_grad_norm: float = 1.0
    # random_dfa specific (used only when env_name == "random_dfa")
    dfa_alphabet: int = 8
    dfa_states: int = 60
    dfa_seed: int = 1234          # masked (-1) before editable code sees it
    early_stop_acc: float = 0.999
    early_stop_windows: int = 3
    # parallel-time guard
    depth_probe_short: int = 256
    depth_probe_long: int = 1024
    depth_slack: int = 80
    init_tripwire_acc: float = 0.25


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OptimizerConfig:
    lr: float
    wd: float
    beta1: float
    beta2: float


def set_global_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def sinusoidal_table(max_len: int, d_model: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Fixed sinusoidal positional encodings (Vaswani et al. 2017).

    Liu et al. 2023 report their main results with sinusoidal encodings
    (App. B.1.1); shared here so every architecture can reuse it.
    """
    position = torch.arange(max_len, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1)
    div = torch.exp(
        torch.arange(0, d_model, 2, dtype=torch.float32)
        * (-math.log(10000.0) / d_model)
    )
    table = torch.zeros(max_len, d_model)
    table[:, 0::2] = torch.sin(position * div)
    table[:, 1::2] = torch.cos(position * div[: d_model // 2])
    return table


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Environments
# =====================================================================
# Driver-private transition tables, keyed by env name. Reading, copying, or
# reconstructing these from the editable block is OUT OF CONTRACT: the model
# must learn the automaton from the sampled (input, state) streams alone.
_PRIVATE_TABLES: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}


def _random_dfa(config: TaskConfig) -> tuple[EnvSpec, torch.Tensor]:
    """Random deterministic transition table delta: Q x Sigma -> Q.

    A generic semiautomaton in the sense of Liu et al. 2023 Sec. 3: random
    transformations mix aperiodic (rank-collapsing) structure with group
    structure, so difficulty interpolates between their easy and hard
    families as |Q| grows. Fixed per benchmark (seeded by dfa_seed).
    """
    Q, Sigma = config.dfa_states, config.dfa_alphabet
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(config.dfa_seed)
    delta = torch.randint(0, Q, (Q, Sigma), generator=g, dtype=torch.long)
    spec = EnvSpec(
        name=f"random_dfa_q{Q}",
        alphabet_size=Sigma,
        num_states=Q,
        seq_len=config.seq_len,
        max_len=max(config.seq_len, config.depth_probe_long),
    )
    return spec, delta


def _s5_word(config: TaskConfig) -> tuple[EnvSpec, torch.Tensor]:
    """The S5 word problem — the flagship hard task of Liu et al. 2023.

    States are the 120 permutations of 5 items; following their App. B.1.1
    the alphabet consists of the minimal generators — a transposition and a
    5-cycle — plus 6 other fixed permutations (seeded). The state is the
    running left-product g_t = a_t o g_{t-1} from the identity. The word
    problem of any non-solvable group is NC1-complete (Barrington 1989);
    Merrill et al. 2024 prove it is inexpressible by diagonal SSMs.
    """
    elements = list(itertools.permutations(range(5)))   # lexicographic, id first
    index = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(elements)}

    def compose(p: tuple[int, ...], q: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        # (p o q)(i) = p[q[i]] — apply q first, then p.
        return tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(5))

    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(config.dfa_seed)
    alphabet = [(1, 0, 2, 3, 4), (1, 2, 3, 4, 0)]   # transposition, 5-cycle
    while len(alphabet) < 8:
        cand = elements[int(torch.randint(0, 120, (1,), generator=g).item())]
        if cand not in alphabet:
            alphabet.append(cand)
    Q, Sigma = 120, len(alphabet)
    delta = torch.zeros(Q, Sigma, dtype=torch.long)
    for qi, elem in enumerate(elements):
        for ai, a in enumerate(alphabet):
            delta[qi, ai] = index[compose(a, elem)]
    spec = EnvSpec(
        name="s5_word",
        alphabet_size=Sigma,
        num_states=Q,
        seq_len=config.seq_len,
        max_len=max(config.seq_len, config.depth_probe_long),
    )
    return spec, delta


_ENV_BUILDERS: dict[str, Callable[[TaskConfig], tuple[EnvSpec, torch.Tensor]]] = {
    "random_dfa": _random_dfa,
    "s5_word": _s5_word,
}


def build_env_spec(config: TaskConfig) -> EnvSpec:
    if config.env_name not in _ENV_BUILDERS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown env {config.env_name!r}")
    spec, delta = _ENV_BUILDERS[config.env_name](config)
    _PRIVATE_TABLES[spec.name] = delta
    return spec


def sample_batch(spec: EnvSpec, batch_size: int, length: int,
                 generator: torch.Generator) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Walk the (private) transition table from state 0 for `length` steps."""
    delta = _PRIVATE_TABLES[spec.name]
    inputs = torch.randint(
        0, spec.alphabet_size, (batch_size, length),
        generator=generator, dtype=torch.long,
    )
    cur = torch.zeros(batch_size, dtype=torch.long)
    states = torch.zeros(batch_size, length, dtype=torch.long)
    for t in range(length):
        cur = delta[cur, inputs[:, t]]
        states[:, t] = cur
    return inputs, states


def normalize_optimizer_config(cfg: dict[str, float]) -> OptimizerConfig:
    required = {"lr", "wd", "beta1", "beta2"}
    missing = required - set(cfg)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing optimizer hyperparameters: {sorted(missing)}")
    out = OptimizerConfig(
        lr=float(cfg["lr"]),
        wd=float(cfg["wd"]),
        beta1=float(cfg["beta1"]),
        beta2=float(cfg["beta2"]),
    )
    if out.lr <= 0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW learning rate must be positive.")
    if out.wd < 0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW weight decay must be non-negative.")
    if not 0.0 < out.beta1 < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW beta1 must satisfy 0 < beta1 < 1.")
    if not 0.0 < out.beta2 < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW beta2 must satisfy 0 < beta2 < 1.")
    return out


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: parallel-time guards (measured, never self-reported)
# =====================================================================
_FORBIDDEN_RECURRENT = (nn.LSTM, nn.GRU, nn.RNN, nn.RNNBase,
                        nn.LSTMCell, nn.GRUCell, nn.RNNCell)


def check_no_recurrent_modules(model: nn.Module) -> None:
    for mod in model.modules():
        if isinstance(mod, _FORBIDDEN_RECURRENT):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Recurrent module {type(mod).__name__} detected. This task "
                f"restricts the design space to parallel-time architectures: "
                f"a sequential RNN simulates any finite automaton by "
                f"construction (Liu et al. 2023 Fig. 5 report a 1-layer LSTM "
                f"at 100% on every task), so it is the excluded skyline here."
            )


def _graph_depth(output: torch.Tensor) -> int:
    """Longest path length in the autograd graph rooted at `output`."""
    root = output.grad_fn
    if root is None:
        return 0
    depth: dict = {}
    stack = [root]
    while stack:
        node = stack[-1]
        if node in depth:
            stack.pop()
            continue
        pending = [
            child
            for child, _ in node.next_functions
            if child is not None and child not in depth
        ]
        if pending:
            stack.extend(pending)
        else:
            best = 0
            for child, _ in node.next_functions:
                if child is not None:
                    best = max(best, depth[child])
            depth[node] = 1 + best
            stack.pop()
    return depth[root]


def check_serial_depth(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec,
                       config: TaskConfig, device: torch.device) -> None:
    """Reject architectures whose serial depth grows with sequence length.

    Two dummy batches (lengths depth_probe_short and depth_probe_long) are
    forwarded and the longest autograd paths compared. Constant-depth models
    (attention, convolutions) and log-depth associative scans pass; per-token
    python recurrences add thousands of serial nodes and fail.
    """
    was_training = model.training
    model.train()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
    depths = []
    for probe_len in (config.depth_probe_short, config.depth_probe_long):
        tokens = torch.randint(
            0, env_spec.alphabet_size, (2, probe_len),
            generator=gen, dtype=torch.long,
        ).to(device)
        logits = forward_logits(model, tokens, env_spec)
        depths.append(_graph_depth(logits))
    model.train(was_training)
    short_d, long_d = depths
    if long_d > short_d + config.depth_slack:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Serial-depth guard: autograd depth grew from {short_d} "
            f"(len {config.depth_probe_short}) to {long_d} "
            f"(len {config.depth_probe_long}); allowed slack is "
            f"{config.depth_slack}. Sequentially-recurrent computation is "
            f"not admissible in this task."
        )
    print(
        f"DEPTH_PROBE short={short_d} long={long_d} slack={config.depth_slack}",
        flush=True,
    )


@torch.no_grad()
def check_init_tripwire(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec,
                        config: TaskConfig, device: torch.device) -> None:
    """Abort if the *untrained* model already simulates the automaton.

    Chance accuracy is at most 1/24; an untrained learned model sits near
    chance, while a hard-coded (or table-reading) simulator is near 1.0.
    """
    was_training = model.training
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(20240819)
    correct, total = 0, 0
    for _ in range(4):
        xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size, config.seq_len, gen)
        xb, yb = xb.to(device), yb.to(device)
        preds = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec).argmax(dim=-1)
        correct += (preds == yb).sum().item()
        total += yb.numel()
    model.train(was_training)
    acc = correct / max(total, 1)
    print(f"INIT_TRIPWIRE acc={acc:.6f} threshold={config.init_tripwire_acc}",
          flush=True)
    if acc >= config.init_tripwire_acc:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Init tripwire: untrained model reaches accuracy {acc:.4f} "
            f">= {config.init_tripwire_acc} (chance <= 1/24). Hard-coding "
            f"the automaton instead of learning it is out of contract."
        )


# =====================================================================
# EDITABLE: model + optimizer + forward wrapper
# =====================================================================
class CustomSequenceModel(nn.Module):
    """Default baseline: shallow GPT-2-style Transformer.

    Follows Liu et al. 2023 App. B.3: embedding dim 512, MLP width 512,
    8 heads, sinusoidal positional encodings; depth 1 is their shallowest
    configuration. Maps token ids [B, T] to state logits [B, T, Q].
    """

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, num_states: int, max_len: int,
                 d_model: int = 512, n_heads: int = 8, n_layers: int = 1,
                 dropout: float = 0.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.token_emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.register_buffer(
            "pos_table", sinusoidal_table(max_len, d_model), persistent=False)
        encoder_layer = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=d_model, nhead=n_heads, dim_feedforward=d_model,
            dropout=dropout, batch_first=True, activation="gelu",
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=n_layers)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, num_states)
        mask = torch.triu(torch.ones(max_len, max_len), diagonal=1).bool()
        self.register_buffer("causal_mask", mask, persistent=False)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, T = input_ids.shape
        x = self.token_emb(input_ids) + self.pos_table[:T].unsqueeze(0)
        x = self.encoder(x, mask=self.causal_mask[:T, :T], is_causal=True)
        return self.head(x)


def build_model(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Construct the sequence model. Output: [B, T, num_states] logits."""
    return CustomSequenceModel(
        vocab_size=env_spec.alphabet_size,
        num_states=env_spec.num_states,
        max_len=env_spec.max_len,
        d_model=512,
        n_heads=8,
        n_layers=1,
        dropout=0.0,
    )


def get_optimizer_config(config: TaskConfig) -> dict[str, float]:
    """AdamW hyperparameters (Liu et al. 2023 App. B.3: lr 3e-4, wd 1e-4)."""
    return {"lr": 3e-4, "wd": 1e-4, "beta1": 0.9, "beta2": 0.999}


def forward_logits(model: nn.Module, input_ids: torch.Tensor,
                   env_spec: EnvSpec) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Run the model on `input_ids` and return logits [B, T, num_states]."""
    return model(input_ids)


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: training and evaluation driver
# =====================================================================
def evaluate(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig,
             device: torch.device, eval_seed: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(eval_seed)
    correct, total, loss_sum = 0, 0, 0.0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(config.eval_batches):
            xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size,
                                  config.seq_len, gen)
            xb = xb.to(device)
            yb = yb.to(device)
            logits = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec)
            loss = F.cross_entropy(
                logits.reshape(-1, env_spec.num_states),
                yb.reshape(-1),
            )
            preds = logits.argmax(dim=-1)
            correct += (preds == yb).sum().item()
            total += yb.numel()
            loss_sum += loss.item() * yb.numel()
    return correct / max(total, 1), loss_sum / max(total, 1)


def train(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig,
          device: torch.device) -> dict[str, float]:
    set_global_seed(config.seed)
    # Editable code sees the public spec and a config with the automaton
    # seed masked: the transition table must be learned, not reconstructed.
    masked_config = replace(config, dfa_seed=-1)
    model = build_model(env_spec, masked_config).to(device)
    check_no_recurrent_modules(model)
    check_serial_depth(model, env_spec, config, device)
    check_init_tripwire(model, env_spec, config, device)
    opt_cfg = normalize_optimizer_config(get_optimizer_config(masked_config))
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        model.parameters(),
        lr=opt_cfg.lr, betas=(opt_cfg.beta1, opt_cfg.beta2),
        weight_decay=opt_cfg.wd,
    )
    n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
    print(
        f"MODEL_CONFIG env={env_spec.name} alphabet={env_spec.alphabet_size} "
        f"states={env_spec.num_states} seq_len={env_spec.seq_len} "
        f"params={n_params}",
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        f"OPT_CONFIG lr={opt_cfg.lr} wd={opt_cfg.wd} "
        f"beta1={opt_cfg.beta1} beta2={opt_cfg.beta2}",
        flush=True,
    )

    train_gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(config.seed * 7919 + 1)
    stable_windows = 0
    last_train_acc = 0.0
    for step in range(1, config.train_steps + 1):
        model.train()
        xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size,
                              config.seq_len, train_gen)
        xb = xb.to(device)
        yb = yb.to(device)
        logits = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(
            logits.reshape(-1, env_spec.num_states),
            yb.reshape(-1),
        )
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss.backward()
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), config.max_grad_norm)
        optimizer.step()

        if step == 1 or step % config.log_interval == 0 or step == config.train_steps:
            train_acc = (logits.argmax(dim=-1) == yb).float().mean().item()
            last_train_acc = train_acc
            print(
                f"TRAIN_METRICS step={step} loss={loss.item():.6f} "
                f"train_acc={train_acc:.6f}",
                flush=True,
            )
            if train_acc >= config.early_stop_acc:
                stable_windows += 1
            else:
                stable_windows = 0
            if stable_windows >= config.early_stop_windows:
                print(f"EARLY_STOP step={step} train_acc={train_acc:.6f}",
                      flush=True)
                break

    eval_acc, eval_loss = evaluate(model, env_spec, config, device,
                                   eval_seed=config.seed * 100003 + 7)
    # Rescale so that chance level (1/|Q|) pins to 0.
    chance = 1.0 / env_spec.num_states
    score = max(0.0, (eval_acc - chance) / (1.0 - chance))
    return {
        "test_accuracy": eval_acc,
        "test_loss": eval_loss,
        "score": score,
        "last_train_acc": last_train_acc,
        "num_params": float(n_params),
    }


def resolve_device(arg: str) -> torch.device:
    if arg == "cpu":
        return torch.device("cpu")
    if arg == "cuda":
        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but no GPU is available.")
        return torch.device("cuda")
    return torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")


def maybe_apply_smoke(config: TaskConfig, enabled: bool) -> TaskConfig:
    if not enabled:
        return config
    return replace(
        config, train_steps=400, eval_batches=4, log_interval=100,
    )


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="MLS-Bench theory-semiautomata.")
    p.add_argument("--env", choices=tuple(_ENV_BUILDERS), default="random_dfa")
    p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument("--label", default="random_dfa")
    p.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--device", choices=("auto", "cpu", "cuda"), default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--seq-len", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--train-steps", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--eval-batches", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--dfa-states", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--dfa-alphabet", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--dfa-seed", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    return p.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    config = TaskConfig(env_name=args.env, seed=args.seed)
    if args.seq_len is not None:
        config = replace(config, seq_len=args.seq_len)
    if args.train_steps is not None:
        config = replace(config, train_steps=args.train_steps)
    if args.batch_size is not None:
        config = replace(config, batch_size=args.batch_size)
    if args.eval_batches is not None:
        config = replace(config, eval_batches=args.eval_batches)
    if args.dfa_states is not None:
        config = replace(config, dfa_states=args.dfa_states)
    if args.dfa_alphabet is not None:
        config = replace(config, dfa_alphabet=args.dfa_alphabet)
    if args.dfa_seed is not None:
        config = replace(config, dfa_seed=args.dfa_seed)
    config = maybe_apply_smoke(config, args.smoke)

    device = resolve_device(args.device)
    env_spec = build_env_spec(config)
    print(
        "TASK_CONFIG "
        f"env={env_spec.name} alphabet={env_spec.alphabet_size} "
        f"states={env_spec.num_states} seq_len={env_spec.seq_len} "
        f"batch={config.batch_size} steps={config.train_steps} "
        f"eval_batches={config.eval_batches} seed={config.seed}",
        flush=True,
    )

    metrics = train(env_spec, config, device)
    print(
        "FINAL_METRICS "
        + " ".join(f"{k}={v:.6f}" for k, v in metrics.items()),
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        f"TEST_METRICS test_accuracy={metrics['test_accuracy']:.6f} "
        f"score={metrics['score']:.6f}",
        flush=True,
    )

    if args.output_dir is not None:
        args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out = args.output_dir / f"{args.label}_seed{args.seed}.json"
        out.write_text(json.dumps({
            "config": asdict(config),
            "env": {
                "name": env_spec.name,
                "alphabet_size": env_spec.alphabet_size,
                "num_states": env_spec.num_states,
                "seq_len": env_spec.seq_len,
            },
            "metrics": metrics,
        }, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

class CustomSequenceModel(nn.Module):
    """Looped Transformer: one shared encoder layer applied n_loops times."""

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, num_states: int, max_len: int,
                 d_model: int = 512, n_heads: int = 8, n_loops: int = 8,
                 dropout: float = 0.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.n_loops = n_loops
        self.token_emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.register_buffer(
            "pos_table", sinusoidal_table(max_len, d_model), persistent=False)
        self.block = nn.TransformerEncoderLayer(
            d_model=d_model, nhead=n_heads, dim_feedforward=d_model,
            dropout=dropout, batch_first=True, activation="gelu",
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.final_norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, num_states)
        mask = torch.triu(torch.ones(max_len, max_len), diagonal=1).bool()
        self.register_buffer("causal_mask", mask, persistent=False)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, T = input_ids.shape
        x = self.token_emb(input_ids) + self.pos_table[:T].unsqueeze(0)
        mask = self.causal_mask[:T, :T]
        for _ in range(self.n_loops):
            x = self.block(x, src_mask=mask, is_causal=True)
        x = self.final_norm(x)
        return self.head(x)


def build_model(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Looped Transformer: shared block, 8 loops, d_model=512, 8 heads."""
    return CustomSequenceModel(
        vocab_size=env_spec.alphabet_size,
        num_states=env_spec.num_states,
        max_len=env_spec.max_len,
        d_model=512,
        n_heads=8,
        n_loops=8,
        dropout=0.0,
    )


def get_optimizer_config(config: TaskConfig) -> dict[str, float]:
    """AdamW (Liu et al. 2023 App. B.3 grid; 1e-4 is stabler when looped)."""
    return {"lr": 1e-4, "wd": 1e-4, "beta1": 0.9, "beta2": 0.999}


def forward_logits(model: nn.Module, input_ids: torch.Tensor,
                   env_spec: EnvSpec) -> torch.Tensor:
    return model(input_ids)

# Synthetic Single-Index Recovery

## Research Question
Design a training recipe (initialisation + per-step optimisation + optional
post-hoc refit) for a fixed two-layer ReLU MLP that recovers the *index
direction* `theta*` and the *link* `g` of a single-index model
`y = g(<theta*, x>) + noise` across multiple link families.

## Background
A single-index model assumes the target depends on the input only through a
one-dimensional projection. It is a classical semi-parametric workhorse and
the simplest non-trivial model where neural networks must perform *feature
learning* (going beyond the kernel regime). Four results frame the problem:

* **Ben Arous, Gheissari, Jagannath**, *Online stochastic gradient descent
  on non-convex losses from high-dimensional inference*, JMLR 22 (2021),
  arXiv:2003.10409 -- introduces the *information exponent* `k` of `g`
  and shows online SGD on a single neuron needs `n ~ d log d` samples for
  weak recovery when `k = 2` and `n = Omega(d^{k-1})` when `k >= 3`.
* **Damian, Lee, Soltanolkotabi**, *Neural Networks can Learn
  Representations with Gradient Descent*, COLT 2022, arXiv:2206.15144 --
  shows that **one giant gradient step** on the first layer (followed by a
  ridge readout) learns the relevant direction with `n = O(d^2)` samples
  when the leap/information exponent is at most 2, beating the kernel
  rate; from a random start a single step generally needs `n ~ d^k`
  (Dandi, Krzakala, Loureiro, Pesce, Stephan, JMLR 2024, arXiv:2305.18270).
* **Damian, Nichani, Ge, Lee**, *Smoothing the Landscape Boosts the Signal
  for SGD*, NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2305.10633 -- online SGD on a
  **smoothed** loss with radius `lambda = d^{1/4}` attains the
  CSQ-optimal sample complexity `n = O(d^{k/2} polylog d)`.
* **Lee, Oko, Suzuki, Wu**, arXiv:2406.01581, and **Arnaboldi, Dandi,
  Krzakala, Loureiro, Pesce, Stephan**, arXiv:2405.15459 -- reusing each
  sample/batch more than once breaks the CSQ barrier: for polynomial links
  SGD variants with sample reuse need only `n = Theta~(d)` samples.

The benchmark is an information-exponent ladder over Hermite links in
which **the sample budget follows each rung's own scaling law** (rather
than a fixed `n` shared across rungs, which would let one uncontrolled
quantity determine difficulty):

| Label      | `g(z)`             | `d`  | `k` | `n_train` | budget scale        |
|------------|--------------------|------|-----|-----------|---------------------|
| `he2-d512` | `He_2(z)/sqrt(2)`  | 512  | 2   | 3072      | `6d ~ d log d`      |
| `he3-d256` | `He_3(z)/sqrt(6)`  | 256  | 3   | 6144      | `1.5 d^{3/2}`       |
| `he4-d96`  | `He_4(z)/sqrt(24)` | 96   | 4   | 3456      | `(3/8) d^2`         |

Each rung's `n` sits at the CSQ-optimal scale `d^{k/2}` for its own
information exponent (`d log d` for `k = 2`, where that is the online-SGD
threshold), with constants calibrated so that the strongest reference
method achieves *partial but incomplete* recovery within the fixed step
budget (8000 steps, batch 256, drawn with replacement from the fixed
training pool). Methods that need `n ~ d^{k-1}` samples therefore sit at
the random-overlap floor (`~ sqrt(2/(pi d))`), one-step moment methods
recover partially, smoothing-based methods recover most of the
direction, and methods that exploit **sample reuse** to approach the
information-theoretic `n ~ d` rate have headroom on every rung.

## What You Can Modify
Edit `pytorch-examples/theory_single_index/custom_strategy.py` only inside
the `EDITABLE` block. Everything else (data generator, model class,
evaluation, driver, link functions) is fixed.

The editable block must export `build_strategy(config)`, returning an
object with four callbacks:

| Callback                                       | Contract                                                                                                  |
|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `init_two_layer(net, config)`                  | Initialise `net.fc1`, `net.fc2` (any in-place scheme allowed); may freeze parameters via `requires_grad_` |
| `make_optimizer(net, config) -> Optimizer`     | Return a `torch.optim.Optimizer` controlling the trainable parameters                                     |
| `training_step(net, opt, x, y, step, cfg)`     | Run one update on the given mini-batch and return `StepMetrics(loss=..., extra=...)`                      |
| `finalize(net, x_train, y_train, config)`      | Optional global refit (e.g. closed-form ridge readout) after the step budget is exhausted                 |

You may NOT change `TwoLayerMLP`, the data generator, the link
functions, the evaluation function, or the driver.

## Fixed Setup
* Model: `TwoLayerMLP = Linear(d, W) -> ReLU -> Linear(W, 1)` with
  `W = 256`.
* Inputs: `x ~ N(0, I_d)` with `d = 512 / 256 / 96` per environment.
* Noise: zero-mean Gaussian with `sigma = 0.1` (training only;
  test target is noise-free).
* Training set: `n_train = 3072 / 6144 / 3456` per environment (see the
  ladder table); batch size 256; up to 8000 steps, mini-batches drawn
  with replacement from the fixed training pool (sample reuse allowed).
* Per environment: one internal replica per top-level seed (different
  `theta*` and data draws), trained from scratch. The release config uses
  three top-level seeds.
* Wall-clock budget: well under 30 minutes per (baseline x env) on a
  single H100.

## Metrics
For each environment we report:

* `test_mse_<env>`     -- mean squared error on a 8192-point noise-free
                           test set (lower is better).
* `direction_recovery_<env>` = `|<theta_hat, theta*>|` for that replica
                           (higher is better; 1 == perfect).
* `score_<env>` = `direction_recovery_<env>` (the primary signal).

`theta_hat` is the top eigenvector of the readout-weighted second-moment
matrix `sum_j |a_j| * w_j w_j^T` of the first-layer rows `w_j` (readout
weights `a_j`) -- the sign-invariant form of the standard first-moment
estimator of Bietti et al. (2022), needed because for even links the
trained rows split into `+theta` and `-theta` groups.

## Baselines
* **sgd_mlp** -- vanilla 2-layer ReLU MLP + SGD with momentum, Kaiming
  init (Bietti et al. 2022 reference baseline). Needs `n ~ d^{k-1}`;
  at these budgets it stays near the random-overlap floor on every rung.
* **frozen_bias** -- shallow network with biases frozen at random init
  (Bietti et al. 2022, Theorem 1).
* **damian_giant_step** -- one large full-batch step on the first layer
  with the moment estimator matched to the link's information exponent
  (spectral for k=2, tensor contraction for k=3, iterated fourth-order
  power map for k=4) + closed-form ridge readout (Damian, Lee,
  Soltanolkotabi 2022; Dandi et al. 2024).
* **smoothed_sgd** -- projected SGD on the smoothed correlation loss with
  radius `lambda = d^{1/4}` and the paper's learning-rate scaling, then a
  `lambda -> 0` phase and a ridge readout (Damian, Nichani, Ge, Lee 2023).
  The strongest reference method: it attains the CSQ-optimal `d^{k/2}`
  rate, but is deliberately budget-limited to partial recovery here.

files.content:
"""Single-index model learning scaffold for MLS-Bench.

The data-generating process is::

    x ~ N(0, I_d)
    y = g(<theta_star, x>) + eps,   eps ~ N(0, sigma^2)

with ``theta_star`` a random unit vector in R^d.  Three link families are
exercised by the benchmark scripts:

  * ``he2`` -- g(z) = He_2(z)/sqrt(2)     (information exponent k=2)
  * ``he3`` -- g(z) = He_3(z)/sqrt(6)     (information exponent k=3)
  * ``he4`` -- g(z) = He_4(z)/sqrt(24)    (information exponent k=4)

(the legacy ``relu`` / ``sign`` k=1 links remain available via --link).

The model architecture is a two-layer ReLU MLP with width ``W`` and a
scalar output.  Training, evaluation, the data generator, and the MLP
class are fixed.  The agent only controls ``build_strategy(...)`` in the
EDITABLE block, which returns an object implementing four callbacks:

    init_two_layer(net, config)              -- initialise weights / biases
    make_optimizer(net, config)              -- construct the optimizer
    training_step(net, opt, x, y, step, cfg) -> StepMetrics
    finalize(net, x_train, y_train, cfg)     -- optional refit / cleanup

The fixed driver loops over ``training_step``, periodically evaluates,
and reports MSE on a held-out test set plus direction recovery
``|<theta_hat, theta*>|`` based on the readout-weighted first-layer rows
(the estimator used by Bietti et al. 2022 and Damian et al. 2022).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import random
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable

import torch
from torch import nn


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: benchmark configuration
# =====================================================================
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskConfig:
    dim: int = 128
    width: int = 256
    link: str = "he3"           # one of {"he2", "he3", "he4"} (+"relu"/"sign"/"hermite" legacy)
    noise_std: float = 0.1
    n_train: int = 65_536
    n_test: int = 8_192
    batch_size: int = 256
    max_steps: int = 8_000
    eval_interval: int = 500
    log_interval: int = 1000
    base_lr: float = 1e-2
    weight_decay: float = 0.0
    momentum: float = 0.9


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StepMetrics:
    loss: float
    extra: dict[str, float]


DEFAULT_TASK = TaskConfig()


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: link functions, data, model, evaluator
# =====================================================================
def link_function(name: str) -> Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor]:
    if name == "relu":
        return lambda z: torch.relu(z)
    if name == "he2":
        # He_2(z) = z^2 - 1; normalise by sqrt(2) so Var_g(N(0,1)) = 1.
        # Information exponent k=2.
        return lambda z: (z.pow(2) - 1.0) / math.sqrt(2.0)
    if name in ("hermite", "he3"):
        # He_3(z) = z^3 - 3z; normalise by sqrt(6) so Var_g(N(0,1)) = 1.
        # Information exponent k=3.
        return lambda z: (z.pow(3) - 3.0 * z) / math.sqrt(6.0)
    if name == "he4":
        # He_4(z) = z^4 - 6z^2 + 3; normalise by sqrt(24) so Var = 1.
        # Information exponent k=4.
        return lambda z: (z.pow(4) - 6.0 * z.pow(2) + 3.0) / math.sqrt(24.0)
    if name == "sign":
        # +-1 valued; treated as regression with MSE for a uniform interface.
        return lambda z: torch.sign(z).to(z.dtype)
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown link function: {name}")


def set_global_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def sample_theta_star(dim: int, seed: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    v = torch.randn(dim, generator=g)
    return v / v.norm().clamp_min(1e-12)


def sample_inputs(n: int, dim: int, seed: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    return torch.randn(n, dim, generator=g)


def make_targets(
    x: torch.Tensor,
    theta_star: torch.Tensor,
    link: str,
    noise_std: float,
    seed: int,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
    z = x @ theta_star
    y_clean = link_function(link)(z)
    noise = torch.randn(y_clean.shape, generator=g) * noise_std
    return (y_clean + noise).to(torch.float32)


class TwoLayerMLP(nn.Module):
    """Fixed architecture: Linear(d, W) -> ReLU -> Linear(W, 1)."""

    def __init__(self, dim: int, width: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(dim, width, bias=True)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(width, 1, bias=True)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.fc2(torch.relu(self.fc1(x))).view(-1)


def estimate_theta_hat(net: TwoLayerMLP) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Recover the implicit direction from the first-layer weights.

    The direction is the top eigenvector of the readout-weighted
    second-moment matrix ``sum_j |a_j| w_j w_j^T``. This is the
    sign-invariant version of the first-moment estimator of Bietti et al.
    (NeurIPS 2022, eqn. 4): for EVEN links the trained rows split into
    +theta and -theta groups, so the plain weighted sum cancels while the
    second-moment estimator does not. For odd links the two estimators
    recover the same direction.
    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        a = net.fc2.weight.view(-1)            # [W]
        w = net.fc1.weight                     # [W, d]
        weighted = a.abs().unsqueeze(1) * w    # [W, d]
        moment = weighted.t() @ w              # [d, d]
        moment = 0.5 * (moment + moment.t())
        eigvals, eigvecs = torch.linalg.eigh(moment)
        idx = int(eigvals.abs().argmax().item())
        v = eigvecs[:, idx]
        norm = v.norm().clamp_min(1e-12)
        return (v / norm).cpu()


@torch.no_grad()
def evaluate_model(
    net: TwoLayerMLP,
    x_test: torch.Tensor,
    y_test: torch.Tensor,
    theta_star: torch.Tensor,
    device: torch.device,
    batch_size: int = 4096,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    net.eval()
    sq_sum = 0.0
    total = 0
    for start in range(0, x_test.shape[0], batch_size):
        end = start + batch_size
        bx = x_test[start:end].to(device)
        by = y_test[start:end].to(device)
        preds = net(bx)
        sq_sum += torch.sum((preds - by) ** 2).item()
        total += by.numel()
    mse = sq_sum / max(total, 1)
    theta_hat = estimate_theta_hat(net)
    direction = float(torch.abs(torch.dot(theta_hat, theta_star.cpu())).item())
    return {"test_mse": mse, "direction_recovery": direction}


# =====================================================================
# EDITABLE: build_strategy(config) -> Strategy
# =====================================================================
class Strategy:
    """Default vanilla SGD strategy on a 2-layer ReLU MLP.

    Reference: Bietti, Bruna, Sanford, Song. "Learning Single-Index
    Models with Shallow Neural Networks", NeurIPS 2022 (arXiv:2210.15651).
    """

    def __init__(self, config: TaskConfig) -> None:
        self.config = config

    def init_two_layer(self, net: TwoLayerMLP, config: TaskConfig) -> None:
        # Standard PyTorch defaults: kaiming_uniform on fc1 + fc2.
        gain = nn.init.calculate_gain("relu")
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(net.fc1.weight, a=math.sqrt(5))
        nn.init.zeros_(net.fc1.bias)
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(net.fc2.weight, a=math.sqrt(5))
        nn.init.zeros_(net.fc2.bias)

    def make_optimizer(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> torch.optim.Optimizer:
        return torch.optim.SGD(
            net.parameters(),
            lr=config.base_lr,
            momentum=config.momentum,
            weight_decay=config.weight_decay,
        )

    def training_step(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        y: torch.Tensor,
        step: int,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> StepMetrics:
        net.train()
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        preds = net(x)
        loss = torch.mean((preds - y) ** 2)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        return StepMetrics(loss=float(loss.item()), extra={})

    def finalize(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        x_train: torch.Tensor,
        y_train: torch.Tensor,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> None:
        return


def build_strategy(config: TaskConfig) -> Strategy:
    """Return the strategy object the driver will call.

    Override this function (and/or the ``Strategy`` class above) to study
    alternative training recipes for single-index recovery.
    """
    return Strategy(config)


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: training driver
# =====================================================================
def resolve_device(device_arg: str) -> torch.device:
    if device_arg == "cpu":
        return torch.device("cpu")
    if device_arg == "cuda":
        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but no GPU is available.")
        return torch.device("cuda")
    return torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")


def maybe_apply_smoke_mode(config: TaskConfig, enabled: bool) -> TaskConfig:
    if not enabled:
        return config
    return replace(
        config,
        dim=32,
        width=64,
        n_train=2_048,
        n_test=1_024,
        max_steps=400,
        eval_interval=100,
        log_interval=500,
    )


def train_single_run(
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
    device: torch.device,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    set_global_seed(seed)

    theta_star = sample_theta_star(config.dim, seed + 11)
    x_train = sample_inputs(config.n_train, config.dim, seed + 101)
    y_train = make_targets(
        x_train, theta_star, config.link, config.noise_std, seed + 1001
    )
    x_test = sample_inputs(config.n_test, config.dim, seed + 202)
    y_test = make_targets(
        x_test, theta_star, config.link, 0.0, seed + 2002
    )  # noise-free test targets for clean MSE

    net = TwoLayerMLP(config.dim, config.width).to(device)
    strategy = build_strategy(config)
    strategy.init_two_layer(net, config)
    optimizer = strategy.make_optimizer(net, config)

    perm_gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed + 4001)
    window_loss = 0.0
    window_count = 0
    best_mse = float("inf")
    best_dir = 0.0

    for step in range(1, config.max_steps + 1):
        idx = torch.randint(
            0, x_train.shape[0], (config.batch_size,), generator=perm_gen
        )
        bx = x_train[idx].to(device)
        by = y_train[idx].to(device)
        metrics = strategy.training_step(net, optimizer, bx, by, step, config)
        window_loss += metrics.loss
        window_count += 1

        if step == 1 or step % config.log_interval == 0:
            avg = window_loss / max(window_count, 1)
            print(
                "TRAIN_METRICS "
                f"step={step} train_loss={avg:.6f}",
                flush=True,
            )
            window_loss = 0.0
            window_count = 0

        if step % config.eval_interval == 0 or step == config.max_steps:
            eval_metrics = evaluate_model(
                net, x_test, y_test, theta_star, device
            )
            print(
                "EVAL_METRICS "
                f"step={step} test_mse={eval_metrics['test_mse']:.6f} "
                f"direction_recovery={eval_metrics['direction_recovery']:.6f}",
                flush=True,
            )
            if eval_metrics["test_mse"] < best_mse:
                best_mse = eval_metrics["test_mse"]
                best_dir = eval_metrics["direction_recovery"]

    strategy.finalize(net, x_train, y_train, config)
    final_metrics = evaluate_model(net, x_test, y_test, theta_star, device)
    if final_metrics["test_mse"] < best_mse:
        best_mse = final_metrics["test_mse"]
        best_dir = final_metrics["direction_recovery"]

    return {
        "final_test_mse": float(final_metrics["test_mse"]),
        "final_direction_recovery": float(final_metrics["direction_recovery"]),
        "best_test_mse": float(best_mse),
        "best_direction_recovery": float(best_dir),
    }


def run_benchmark(
    config: TaskConfig,
    seed: int,
    device: torch.device,
    num_replicas: int = 1,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    print(
        "TASK_CONFIG "
        + " ".join(
            [
                f"dim={config.dim}",
                f"width={config.width}",
                f"link={config.link}",
                f"noise_std={config.noise_std}",
                f"n_train={config.n_train}",
                f"max_steps={config.max_steps}",
                f"batch_size={config.batch_size}",
                f"num_replicas={num_replicas}",
            ]
        ),
        flush=True,
    )

    replicas: list[dict[str, float]] = []
    for replica_index in range(num_replicas):
        replica_seed = seed * 10_000 + replica_index
        result = train_single_run(config, replica_seed, device)
        replicas.append(result)
        print(
            "RUN_METRICS "
            f"replica={replica_index} "
            f"test_mse={result['final_test_mse']:.6f} "
            f"direction_recovery={result['final_direction_recovery']:.6f} "
            f"best_test_mse={result['best_test_mse']:.6f} "
            f"best_direction_recovery={result['best_direction_recovery']:.6f}",
            flush=True,
        )

    mse = torch.tensor([r["final_test_mse"] for r in replicas])
    direction = torch.tensor(
        [r["final_direction_recovery"] for r in replicas]
    )
    best_mse_tensor = torch.tensor([r["best_test_mse"] for r in replicas])
    best_dir_tensor = torch.tensor(
        [r["best_direction_recovery"] for r in replicas]
    )

    final_metrics = {
        "test_mse": float(mse.mean().item()),
        "direction_recovery": float(direction.mean().item()),
        "best_test_mse": float(best_mse_tensor.mean().item()),
        "best_direction_recovery": float(best_dir_tensor.mean().item()),
        "test_mse_std": float(mse.std(unbiased=False).item()),
        "direction_recovery_std": float(direction.std(unbiased=False).item()),
        "score": float(direction.mean().item()),
        "num_replicas": int(num_replicas),
    }

    print(
        "FINAL_METRICS "
        + " ".join(
            f"{key}={value:.6f}" if isinstance(value, float) else f"{key}={value}"
            for key, value in final_metrics.items()
        ),
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        "TEST_METRICS "
        f"test_mse={final_metrics['test_mse']:.6f} "
        f"direction_recovery={final_metrics['direction_recovery']:.6f} "
        f"score={final_metrics['score']:.6f}",
        flush=True,
    )
    return {
        "config": asdict(config),
        "metrics": final_metrics,
        "replicas": replicas,
    }


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Run the MLS-Bench theory-single-index task."
    )
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--label", type=str, default="eval")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--device", choices=("auto", "cpu", "cuda"), default="auto"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--dim", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--width", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--link", type=str, default=None, choices=("relu", "he2", "hermite", "he3", "he4", "sign")
    )
    parser.add_argument("--noise-std", type=float, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--n-train", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--num-replicas", type=int, default=1)
    return parser.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    config = maybe_apply_smoke_mode(DEFAULT_TASK, args.smoke)
    if args.dim is not None:
        config = replace(config, dim=args.dim)
    if args.width is not None:
        config = replace(config, width=args.width)
    if args.link is not None:
        config = replace(config, link=args.link)
    if args.noise_std is not None:
        config = replace(config, noise_std=args.noise_std)
    if args.n_train is not None:
        config = replace(config, n_train=args.n_train)
    if args.max_steps is not None:
        config = replace(config, max_steps=args.max_steps)

    device = resolve_device(args.device)
    summary = run_benchmark(
        config=config,
        seed=args.seed,
        device=device,
        num_replicas=args.num_replicas,
    )

    if args.output_dir is not None:
        args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out = args.output_dir / f"{args.label}_seed{args.seed}.json"
        out.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

class Strategy:
    """Vanilla SGD on a two-layer ReLU MLP (Bietti et al., 2022 baseline)."""

    def __init__(self, config: TaskConfig) -> None:
        self.config = config

    def init_two_layer(self, net: TwoLayerMLP, config: TaskConfig) -> None:
        # Kaiming-normal first layer; small uniform second layer.
        nn.init.kaiming_normal_(net.fc1.weight, nonlinearity="relu")
        nn.init.zeros_(net.fc1.bias)
        bound = 1.0 / math.sqrt(config.width)
        nn.init.uniform_(net.fc2.weight, -bound, bound)
        nn.init.zeros_(net.fc2.bias)

    def make_optimizer(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> torch.optim.Optimizer:
        return torch.optim.SGD(
            net.parameters(),
            lr=config.base_lr,
            momentum=config.momentum,
            weight_decay=config.weight_decay,
        )

    def training_step(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        y: torch.Tensor,
        step: int,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> StepMetrics:
        net.train()
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        preds = net(x)
        loss = torch.mean((preds - y) ** 2)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        return StepMetrics(loss=float(loss.item()), extra={})

    def finalize(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        x_train: torch.Tensor,
        y_train: torch.Tensor,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> None:
        return


def build_strategy(config: TaskConfig) -> Strategy:
    return Strategy(config)

class Strategy:
    """Frozen-bias shallow network (Bietti et al., NeurIPS 2022, Thm 1)."""

    def __init__(self, config: TaskConfig) -> None:
        self.config = config

    def init_two_layer(self, net: TwoLayerMLP, config: TaskConfig) -> None:
        # Random first-layer weights on the unit sphere; biases sampled
        # uniformly in [-1, 1] and frozen (see Bietti et al. 2022, eqn. 3).
        with torch.no_grad():
            W = torch.randn_like(net.fc1.weight)
            W = W / W.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
            net.fc1.weight.copy_(W)
            net.fc1.bias.uniform_(-1.0, 1.0)
        net.fc1.bias.requires_grad_(False)

        bound = 1.0 / math.sqrt(config.width)
        nn.init.uniform_(net.fc2.weight, -bound, bound)
        nn.init.zeros_(net.fc2.bias)

    def make_optimizer(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> torch.optim.Optimizer:
        params = [p for p in net.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
        return torch.optim.SGD(
            params,
            lr=config.base_lr,
            momentum=config.momentum,
            weight_decay=config.weight_decay,
        )

    def training_step(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        y: torch.Tensor,
        step: int,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> StepMetrics:
        net.train()
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        preds = net(x)
        loss = torch.mean((preds - y) ** 2)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        return StepMetrics(loss=float(loss.item()), extra={})

    def finalize(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        x_train: torch.Tensor,
        y_train: torch.Tensor,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> None:
        return


def build_strategy(config: TaskConfig) -> Strategy:
    return Strategy(config)

class Strategy:
    """One giant full-batch step on the first layer, then fit the readout.

    See Damian, Lee, Soltanolkotabi (COLT 2022, arXiv:2206.15144)
    sections 3-4, and the empirical replay in Dandi et al. (JMLR 2024,
    arXiv:2305.18270).
    """

    _INFO_EXPONENT = {"relu": 1, "sign": 1, "he2": 2, "hermite": 3, "he3": 3, "he4": 4}

    def __init__(self, config: TaskConfig) -> None:
        self.config = config
        self.info_exponent = self._INFO_EXPONENT.get(config.link, 1)
        # Dimension-scaled giant-step LR (with the 1/sqrt(width) readout
        # normalization): eta = sqrt(width) * d^((k-1)/2).
        self._giant_lr = math.sqrt(max(config.width, 1)) * (
            float(config.dim) ** max(0.0, 0.5 * (self.info_exponent - 1))
        )

    def init_two_layer(self, net: TwoLayerMLP, config: TaskConfig) -> None:
        # Random probes on the sphere. The full-batch giant step in finalize()
        # converts these probes into feature rows aligned with theta_star.
        with torch.no_grad():
            W = torch.randn_like(net.fc1.weight)
            W = W / W.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
            net.fc1.weight.copy_(W)
            nn.init.zeros_(net.fc1.bias)
            net.fc2.weight.fill_(1.0 / math.sqrt(config.width))
            nn.init.zeros_(net.fc2.bias)

    def make_optimizer(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> torch.optim.Optimizer:
        # The fixed driver only exposes mini-batches to training_step(), but
        # the Damian giant step is an empirical full-batch update. Keep the
        # loop cheap and perform the actual one-step update in finalize().
        return torch.optim.SGD(net.parameters(), lr=0.0)

    def training_step(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        y: torch.Tensor,
        step: int,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> StepMetrics:
        # No mini-batch updates: a noisy batch-256 first step is precisely the
        # failure mode. Return the batch target energy for progress logging.
        return StepMetrics(loss=float(torch.mean(y * y).item()), extra={})

    @staticmethod
    def _normalize(v: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return v / v.norm().clamp_min(1e-12)

    def _first_order_direction(self, x: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # k=1 links (ReLU/sign): the first Hermite moment is nonzero.
        return self._normalize((y[:, None] * x).mean(dim=0))

    def _spectral_direction(self, x: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # k=2 links: top |eigenvalue| eigenvector of E[y (x x^T - I)].
        d = x.shape[1]
        a = (x * y[:, None]).t() @ x / float(x.shape[0])
        a = 0.5 * (a + a.t()) - float(y.mean()) * torch.eye(d, device=x.device)
        eigvals, eigvecs = torch.linalg.eigh(a)
        idx = int(eigvals.abs().argmax().item())
        return self._normalize(eigvecs[:, idx])

    def _hermite_contract(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        y: torch.Tensor,
        v: torch.Tensor,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Multivariate third-Hermite contraction:
        # E[y * (x <x,v>^2 - x ||v||^2 - 2 v <x,v>)].
        z = x @ v
        contracted = (
            y[:, None]
            * (x * z.square()[:, None] - x - 2.0 * v[None, :] * z[:, None])
        ).mean(dim=0)
        return self._normalize(contracted)

    def _hermite_direction(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        y: torch.Tensor,
        probes: torch.Tensor,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Average many one-step probe contractions, then refine with the
        # tensor power map. This is the k=3 full-batch giant-step signal.
        probes = probes / probes.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
        z = x @ probes.t()
        y_col = y[:, None]
        first = (y_col * x).mean(dim=0)
        yz = (y_col * z).mean(dim=0)
        term = (y_col * z.square()).t() @ x / float(x.shape[0])
        term = term - first[None, :] - 2.0 * probes * yz[:, None]
        direction = self._normalize(term.mean(dim=0))
        for _ in range(2):
            direction = self._hermite_contract(x, y, direction)
        return direction

    def _fourth_order_direction(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        y: torch.Tensor,
        probes: torch.Tensor,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        # k=4 power map: v -> E[y He_3(<v,x>) x]; population value is
        # proportional to <v,theta>^3 theta, so the contraction has
        # exponent 3 and from random probes it needs n >> d^3 samples.
        # We start from the empirically best probe and iterate.
        probes = probes / probes.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
        z = x @ probes.t()                                   # [N, W]
        he3 = z.pow(3) - 3.0 * z
        scores = (y[:, None] * he3).mean(dim=0).abs()        # [W]
        v = probes[int(scores.argmax().item())]
        for _ in range(5):
            zv = x @ v
            he3v = zv.pow(3) - 3.0 * zv
            v = self._normalize((y * he3v)[:, None].mul(x).mean(dim=0))
        return v

    def _estimate_direction(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        x_train: torch.Tensor,
        y_train: torch.Tensor,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        probes = net.fc1.weight.detach()
        if self.info_exponent >= 4:
            return self._fourth_order_direction(x_train, y_train, probes)
        if self.info_exponent == 3:
            return self._hermite_direction(x_train, y_train, probes)
        if self.info_exponent == 2:
            return self._spectral_direction(x_train, y_train)
        return self._first_order_direction(x_train, y_train)

    def _apply_giant_step(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        x_train: torch.Tensor,
        y_train: torch.Tensor,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> None:
        direction = self._estimate_direction(net, x_train, y_train)
        probes = net.fc1.weight.detach()
        jitter = torch.randn_like(probes)
        jitter = jitter - (jitter @ direction)[:, None] * direction[None, :]
        jitter = jitter / jitter.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)

        # Dimension-scaled giant step: the larger eta is, the more completely
        # the random probe rows are overwritten by the empirical signal.
        mix = self._giant_lr / (self._giant_lr + 1.0)
        rows = (1.0 - mix) * probes + mix * direction[None, :] + 0.05 * jitter
        rows = rows / rows.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
        with torch.no_grad():
            net.fc1.weight.copy_(rows)
            # Damian et al. re-sample biases before fitting the readout; a
            # spread of thresholds gives the ridge head a usable link basis.
            net.fc1.bias.copy_(
                torch.linspace(-2.5, 2.5, config.width, device=rows.device)
            )

    def finalize(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        x_train: torch.Tensor,
        y_train: torch.Tensor,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> None:
        # Closed-form ridge regression on the (now frozen) features. This
        # is exactly what Damian et al. (2022) call the "linear readout"
        # stage after the giant step.
        device = next(net.parameters()).device
        with torch.no_grad():
            x_device = x_train.to(device)
            y_device = y_train.to(device)
            self._apply_giant_step(net, x_device, y_device, config)
            feats = torch.relu(
                x_device @ net.fc1.weight.t() + net.fc1.bias
            )  # [N, W]
            feats = torch.cat(
                [feats, torch.ones(feats.shape[0], 1, device=device)], dim=1
            )
            target = y_device.view(-1, 1)
            lam = max(config.weight_decay, 1e-4)
            gram = feats.t() @ feats + lam * torch.eye(
                feats.shape[1], device=device
            )
            rhs = feats.t() @ target
            beta = torch.linalg.solve(gram, rhs).view(-1)
            net.fc2.weight.copy_(beta[:-1].view(1, -1))
            net.fc2.bias.fill_(float(beta[-1]))


def build_strategy(config: TaskConfig) -> Strategy:
    return Strategy(config)

smoothed_sgd.content:
class Strategy:
    """Smoothed online SGD on a single spherical neuron + ridge readout.

    Reference: Damian, Nichani, Ge, Lee. "Smoothing the Landscape Boosts
    the Signal for SGD: Optimal Sample Complexity for Learning Single
    Index Models", NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv:2305.10633).  Phase 1 runs
    projected SGD on the smoothed correlation loss
    ``L_lambda(w) = -E_u E[y * He_k(<(w + lambda*u)/||w + lambda*u||, x>)]``
    with lambda = d^{1/4} (their Algorithm 1); phase 2 sets lambda = 0 to
    convert weak recovery into strong recovery.  The learning rate uses
    the paper's scaling ``eta ~ (1 + lambda^2)^{k-1} * d^{-k/2}``.
    ``finalize`` plants the learned direction into the first layer and
    fits the readout by closed-form ridge regression (as in Damian et
    al. 2022).
    """

    _INFO_EXPONENT = {"relu": 1, "sign": 1, "he2": 2, "hermite": 3, "he3": 3, "he4": 4}
    _LR_SCALE = 3.0        # global tuning constant c
    _NUM_PERTURB = 4       # Monte-Carlo draws for the smoothing expectation
    _PHASE1_FRAC = 0.6     # fraction of steps run with smoothing on

    def __init__(self, config: TaskConfig) -> None:
        self.config = config
        self.k = self._INFO_EXPONENT.get(config.link, 1)
        d = float(config.dim)
        # lambda = d^{1/4} for k >= 3 (Damian et al. 2023); smoothing is
        # unnecessary in the SGD-efficient regime k <= 2.
        self.lam = d ** 0.25 if self.k >= 3 else 0.0
        self.eta1 = self._LR_SCALE * ((1.0 + self.lam ** 2) ** (self.k - 1)) * d ** (-0.5 * self.k)
        self.eta2 = self._LR_SCALE / d
        self.u: torch.Tensor | None = None

    def init_two_layer(self, net: TwoLayerMLP, config: TaskConfig) -> None:
        with torch.no_grad():
            W = torch.randn_like(net.fc1.weight)
            W = W / W.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
            net.fc1.weight.copy_(W)
            nn.init.zeros_(net.fc1.bias)
            net.fc2.weight.fill_(1.0 / math.sqrt(config.width))
            nn.init.zeros_(net.fc2.bias)
        device = net.fc1.weight.device
        v = torch.randn(config.dim, device=device)
        self.u = v / v.norm().clamp_min(1e-12)

    def make_optimizer(self, net: TwoLayerMLP, config: TaskConfig) -> torch.optim.Optimizer:
        # The spherical neuron is updated manually inside training_step.
        return torch.optim.SGD(net.parameters(), lr=0.0)

    def _hermite_deriv(self, z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # He_k'(z) = k * He_{k-1}(z)
        if self.k == 2:
            return 2.0 * z
        if self.k == 3:
            return 3.0 * (z.pow(2) - 1.0)
        if self.k == 4:
            return 4.0 * (z.pow(3) - 3.0 * z)
        return torch.ones_like(z)

    def training_step(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        y: torch.Tensor,
        step: int,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> StepMetrics:
        assert self.u is not None
        w = self.u
        phase1 = step <= int(self._PHASE1_FRAC * config.max_steps)
        lam = self.lam if phase1 else 0.0
        eta = self.eta1 if phase1 else self.eta2
        d = x.shape[1]
        grad = torch.zeros_like(w)
        n_draws = self._NUM_PERTURB if lam > 0 else 1
        for _ in range(n_draws):
            if lam > 0:
                u_pert = torch.randn(d, device=x.device)
                u_pert = u_pert - torch.dot(u_pert, w) * w
                u_pert = u_pert / u_pert.norm().clamp_min(1e-12)
                w_tilde = w + lam * u_pert
                w_tilde = w_tilde / w_tilde.norm().clamp_min(1e-12)
            else:
                w_tilde = w
            z = x @ w_tilde
            # gradient of  -mean(y * He_k(z))  w.r.t. w_tilde
            grad = grad - (y * self._hermite_deriv(z)) @ x / x.shape[0]
        grad = grad / n_draws
        grad = grad - torch.dot(grad, w) * w        # project to tangent space
        gnorm = grad.norm()
        if torch.isfinite(gnorm) and gnorm > 10.0:
            grad = grad * (10.0 / gnorm)
        w = w - eta * grad
        self.u = w / w.norm().clamp_min(1e-12)
        corr = float(torch.mean(y * (x @ self.u)).item())
        return StepMetrics(loss=abs(corr), extra={})

    def finalize(
        self,
        net: TwoLayerMLP,
        x_train: torch.Tensor,
        y_train: torch.Tensor,
        config: TaskConfig,
    ) -> None:
        assert self.u is not None
        device = next(net.parameters()).device
        with torch.no_grad():
            direction = self.u.to(device)
            jitter = torch.randn(config.width, config.dim, device=device)
            jitter = jitter - (jitter @ direction)[:, None] * direction[None, :]
            jitter = jitter / jitter.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
            rows = direction[None, :] + 0.05 * jitter
            rows = rows / rows.norm(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
            net.fc1.weight.copy_(rows)
            net.fc1.bias.copy_(
                torch.linspace(-2.5, 2.5, config.width, device=device)
            )
            x_device = x_train.to(device)
            y_device = y_train.to(device)
            feats = torch.relu(x_device @ net.fc1.weight.t() + net.fc1.bias)
            feats = torch.cat(
                [feats, torch.ones(feats.shape[0], 1, device=device)], dim=1
            )
            lam = max(config.weight_decay, 1e-4)
            gram = feats.t() @ feats + lam * torch.eye(feats.shape[1], device=device)
            rhs = feats.t() @ y_device.view(-1, 1)
            beta = torch.linalg.solve(gram, rhs).view(-1)
            net.fc2.weight.copy_(beta[:-1].view(1, -1))
            net.fc2.bias.fill_(float(beta[-1]))


def build_strategy(config: TaskConfig) -> Strategy:
    return Strategy(config)

tasks.description_md:
# Theory-Staircase: Learning Sparse Functions on the Hypercube

## Research Question
For a two-layer fully connected neural network of width `M` trained by
one-pass batch-SGD on the hypercube `{+1, -1}^d`, can you design the model
(architecture / initialization / parametrization), the optimizer, and the
training step so that the network learns the latent target

```
f*(x) = h*(x_{j_1}, ..., x_{j_P})
```

as SAMPLE-EFFICIENTLY as possible across the full range of "hierarchy
levels" of the latent target `h*` — the leap-1 (MSP) staircase, the leap-2
staircase, and the 3-sparse parity?

## Background
Abbe, Boix-Adsera, and Misiakiewicz (COLT 2022, arXiv:2202.08658) introduced
the **merged-staircase property (MSP)**: a sparse latent target
`h* : {+1, -1}^P -> R` with non-zero Fourier coefficients indexed by
`S = {S_1, ..., S_m}` satisfies MSP iff the supports can be ordered so that
`|S_i \ ∪_{j<i} S_j| <= 1` for every `i`. They prove that MSP is both
**necessary and nearly sufficient** for a two-layer mean-field SGD network
to learn `f*` in `O(d)` samples; for non-MSP targets the dimension-free
dynamics are stuck at strictly positive risk (Theorem 7). The follow-up
(COLT 2023, arXiv:2302.11055) quantifies this with the **leap complexity**:
SGD climbs the staircase saddle-to-saddle, picking up the monomials
sequentially, and a leap-`k` target takes `Theta~(d^max(k-1,1))` online-SGD
steps. **When** each monomial is picked up — not only whether it is learned
at the end — is therefore the scientifically meaningful quantity, and it is
exactly how these papers present the phenomenon (test error versus SGD
steps on a log axis).

Two further reference points: fixed random features of width `M` can only
express the degree-`k` components of a sparse target when `M` scales like
`d^k` (Ghorbani-Mei-Misiakiewicz-Montanari, Ann. Stat. 2021), so lazy /
NTK-style methods fail on the higher-degree monomials at `M = d`.
Feature-learning SGD reaches `k`-sparse parities near the `~d^{k-1}`-step
computational limit (Barak et al. 2022, arXiv:2207.08799), and batch REUSE
breaks the information/leap-exponent barrier of one-pass SGD: two gradient
steps on the same batch of size `O(d)` already produce escape for
information exponent `> 2` (Dandi et al., ICML 2024, arXiv:2402.03220).

## What You Can Modify
Edit the scaffold file `pytorch-examples/theory_staircase/custom_strategy.py`
only inside the editable block containing the three functions:

1. `build_model(config)` — returns the trainable `nn.Module`. The module
   must take an input of shape `[batch_size, d]` (with entries in
   `{+1, -1}`) and return a tensor of shape `[batch_size]` or
   `[batch_size, 1]`.
2. `get_optimizer(model, config)` — returns the `torch.optim.Optimizer`
   used to update the model.
3. `train_step(model, optimizer, x, y)` — one training update on a fresh
   batch `(x, y)`; must return a Python `float` training loss.

The data sampler (uniform on `{+1, -1}^d`), the targets `h1`, `h2`, `h3`,
the training label noise, and the checkpoint-evaluation pipeline are all
FIXED inside the harness and must not be modified.

## Fixed Setup
- Ambient dimension `d = 100` (the Figure-1 protocol of Abbe et al. 2022:
  `d = N = 100`, `b = 150`, mean-field step size `eta = 1/2`).
- Width `M = 100`, batch size `b = 150` (one-pass: every batch is freshly
  sampled from the uniform distribution on `{+1, -1}^d`).
- Training labels carry additive Gaussian noise with `sigma = 0.5`
  (training only — evaluation always compares to the noiseless target).
- Three latent targets, one per evaluation environment:
  - `h1(z) = z1 + z1 z2 + z1 z2 z3 + z1 z2 z3 z4` — the exact Figure-1
    staircase of Abbe et al. 2022 (MSP / leap-1). `T = 24 000` steps.
  - `h2(z) = z1 z2 + z1 z2 z3 z4` — leap-2 staircase (non-MSP).
    `T = 40 000` steps.
  - `h3(z) = z1 z2 z3` — 3-sparse parity (leap-3, information exponent 3).
    `T = 40 000` steps.
- The latent subset `I = {j_1, ..., j_P}` is drawn fresh per run from OS
  entropy (it cannot be precomputed from the harness seeds; by
  exchangeability of the coordinates the choice of `I` does not affect
  difficulty). Three independent runs per environment per top-level seed;
  the release config uses three top-level seeds (nine runs per
  environment, comparable to the 10-experiment averages of Abbe et al.
  Fig. 1).

## Interface Notes
- `build_model` must construct a fresh model — the harness re-creates one
  for each run.
- `get_optimizer` must wrap only `model.parameters()` (or a filtered
  subset).
- `train_step` performs the update(s) for one fresh batch and returns the
  scalar training loss as a Python `float`. You must call
  `optimizer.zero_grad()` inside `train_step`.
- Everything is run inside one Python process per environment per seed.

## Metric
During each run the model is evaluated at 24 log-spaced checkpoints
between step 200 and the step budget `T`, on 8 192 fresh test samples per
checkpoint, against the NOISELESS target:

- `R^2(t) = max(0, 1 - test_mse(t) / Var(h*))` — `Var(h*)` = number of
  monomials (4 / 2 / 1); a trivial zero predictor scores exactly 0.
- `score_{env}` — **staircase score**: the mean of `R^2(t)` over the
  log-spaced checkpoints, averaged over runs. This is the primary
  leaderboard metric. A method that never learns scores 0; a method that
  learns earlier (smaller effective leap / better sample efficiency)
  scores strictly higher than one that learns late; a score of 1 would
  require learning the target instantly, which is impossible (`Omega(d)`
  steps even for leap-1 targets).
- `final_r2_{env}`, `test_mse_{env}`, `fourier_recovery_{env}` — final
  checkpoint diagnostics (informational).

The aggregate task score is the geometric mean of the three per-environment
staircase scores. A catastrophic failure on `h2` or `h3` is not papered
over by a great result on `h1`.

## Baselines (variants of the reference setup)
- **mean_field_sgd** — Two-layer fully-connected network with shifted
  sigmoid activation `sigma(x) = (1 + exp(-x + 0.5))^(-1)`, no trainable
  first-layer bias, `a_j ~ Unif({+1, -1})`, `w_j ~ N(0, I_d)` at
  initialization, SGD with the width-corrected mean-field step sizes
  (`eta = 1/2` in the mean-field parametrization; because the scaffold
  normalizes the output by `1/M` explicitly, the torch learning rate is
  `eta * M` on the particles and `eta` on the readout). This matches the
  experimental setup of Abbe-Boix-Adsera-Misiakiewicz COLT 2022 Figure 1.
  Learns the leap-1 staircase h1; provably stuck in the dimension-free
  regime on h2, and slow on the parity h3.
- **ntk** — Same width but with NTK-style first layer (`w ~ N(0, 1/d)`,
  `b ~ N(0, 1)`) FROZEN at initialization; only the readout is trained
  (the canonical lazy / random-features baseline of Jacot-Gabriel-Hongler
  NeurIPS 2018), with a constant step size large enough that the head
  regression actually converges. No feature learning: partial credit on
  the degree-1 monomial of h1 only.
- **curriculum_layerwise** — combines mu-P-style initialization
  (Yang-Hu 2020), shifted-sigmoid activation with nonzero low
  derivatives near the origin, Adam with per-layer learning rates, and
  layer-wise alternating updates to drive saddle-to-saddle dynamics
  (Abbe-Boix-Adsera-Misiakiewicz, COLT 2023, arXiv:2302.11055).
- **reuse_sgd** — the mean-field setup plus batch reuse: `train_step`
  performs two consecutive SGD updates on the same fresh batch (the
  `T = 2` protocol of Dandi et al., ICML 2024, arXiv:2402.03220, adapted
  to the online setting; identical fresh-sample budget to one-pass SGD at
  2x gradient work). Dramatically accelerates the parity h3 (information
  exponent 3) but does not help the leap-2 staircase h2, whose escape is
  governed by the information-exponent-2 first monomial.
